findings.title: execution_rate_limit.persistence_path accepted at boot, fails every web run
findings.summary: RateLimitSettings.persistence_path has no validator. Its path rules (no URI, must resolve under data_dir) run only in RuntimeRateLimitConfig.from_settings, called per run at execution/service.py:3631. Nothing checks them at WebSettings construction, lifespan or readiness.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator sets ELSPETH_WEB__EXECUTION_RATE_LIMIT={"persistence_path":"/var/lib/elspeth/rl.db"} with data_dir=/data, or uses '../rl.db'. Boot and readiness pass. Every web-executed run raises ValueError('rate_limit.persistence_path escapes allowed root ...') before the orchestrator starts. The except BaseException at service.py:4048 catches it and marks the run failed, so the misconfiguration shows up first as user run failures.
findings.evidence: grep -rn execution_rate_limit src: only config.py:511/1446 and execution/service.py:3631. contracts/config/runtime.py:55-75 holds the only validation (_resolve_rate_limit_persistence_path). core/config.py:1885 declares persistence_path as a plain str | None.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a WebSettings model_validator(mode='after') that calls RuntimeRateLimitConfig.from_settings(self.execution_rate_limit, state_dir=self.data_dir), or _resolve_rate_limit_persistence_path, so a bad path fails at boot. Pin it with an escaping-path test.

verdicts.reason: I traced the failure path and it is real. At the pinned commit, nothing checks WebSettings.execution_rate_limit.persistence_path at boot. The only place the path rule is enforced is RuntimeRateLimitConfig.from_settings, which runs once per web run inside _run_pipeline's try block. A path outside data_dir, or a URI, therefore passes WebSettings construction and startup. Every web run then raises ValueError and is marked failed. I found no validator and no recorded ruling that covers this. Low severity is right: the fault is operator misconfiguration, it fails closed, and the error message names the setting. But the problem is not reported at boot, and users see it first as failed runs.
verdicts.evidence:
- web/config.py:511 declares `execution_rate_limit: RateLimitSettings = Field(default_factory=RateLimitSettings)`. The field arrived in window commit 24dccdd9e ("feat(web): operator execution_rate_limit for web-executed runs"), found with `git log -S`.
- The only other mention in web/config.py is line 1446, where the field is added to the `_JSON_OBJECT_FIELDS` env decoder.
- None of the field/model validators in web/config.py (lines 694-1361) touch rate_limit. `grep -rn rate_limit src/elspeth/web` finds only the composer, write and auth limiters, plus service.py:3631.
- core/config.py declares `persistence_path: str | None = Field(default=None, ...)` with no validator.
- contracts/config/runtime.py:55-76, `_resolve_rate_limit_persistence_path`, holds the only path validation:
  - it rejects `file:` and `://` URIs;
  - it resolves absolute paths as given and relative paths under state_dir;
  - it raises `ValueError(f"rate_limit.persistence_path escapes allowed root {state_dir}: ...")` when `candidate.relative_to(state_dir)` fails.
  - It is called from `from_settings` at runtime.py:487.
- web/execution/service.py:3631 is the only web caller: `RuntimeRateLimitConfig.from_settings(self._settings.execution_rate_limit, state_dir=self._settings.data_dir)`. It sits inside `_run_pipeline` (def at 2874, try at 2913), whose `except BaseException as exc:` at 4048 catches the error and fails the run.
- Concrete case: `persistence_path="/var/lib/elspeth/rl.db"` with `data_dir=/data`, or `"../rl.db"`. Either one resolves outside /data, so every run raises ValueError before `RateLimitRegistry` is built.
- No entry in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md mentions execution_rate_limit or persistence_path.

findings.title: execution_rate_limit undocumented; comment omits per-run scope and non-LLM keys
findings.summary: The new operator knob has no entry in docs/reference/environment-variables.md. Its comment says limiters are keyed by provider type (true only for LLM transforms) and does not say that each run gets a fresh in-memory RateLimitRegistry.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sets services.openrouter.requests_per_minute=600 to stay under a provider quota. service.py:3636 builds a new RateLimitRegistry per run, and with no persistence_path the buckets live only in that run, so N concurrent web runs send up to N x 600/min. An operator trying to throttle azure_ai_search, web_scrape or the Azure safety transforms has no documented key: they use azure_ai_search:<hostname>, web_scrape, blob_fetch, dataverse_* and the plugin self.name.
findings.evidence: grep -rn EXECUTION_RATE_LIMIT docs deploy returns nothing. llm/transform.py:1733-1742 holds the LLM keys; azure/ai_search.py:138 builds limiter_service_name = f'azure_ai_search:{hostname}'; execution/service.py:3636 builds RateLimitRegistry(rate_limit_config) inside the per-run body.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an ELSPETH_WEB__EXECUTION_RATE_LIMIT entry to environment-variables.md giving the JSON shape, the per-run scope (persistence_path under data_dir shares buckets across runs) and the full limiter-key list. Correct the config.py comment to match.

verdicts.reason: The finding holds only in part. Confirmed: ELSPETH_WEB__EXECUTION_RATE_LIMIT is a real operator knob. 24dccdd9e added it as a JSON field in _JSON_OBJECT_FIELDS (config.py:1446). It has no entry in docs/reference/environment-variables.md or anywhere else under docs/ or deploy/, although that reference documents every other JSON web knob (LLM_PROFILES, PLUGIN_CONTROL_MODES, BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_DEFAULT_PROFILES, AZURE_SEARCH_PROFILES and so on). The config.py comment is also incomplete. It names only the four LLM provider keys, but azure_ai_search uses a different key, 'azure_ai_search:<hostname>' (ai_search.py:138), so an operator has no documented key for non-LLM limiters. Refuted: the headline failure scenario, "N concurrent web runs send up to N x 600/min". ExecutionService runs pipelines on ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) (service.py:1091, and the class docstring at 1036-1037 says so). Within one process web runs are serialised, so the fresh RateLimitRegistry built per run (service.py:3636, closed at 4331-4332) does not multiply the rate. The worst case in one process is a small burst at a run boundary. Multiplication happens only across processes or replicas. In that case a persistence_path on replica-local disk would not share buckets either, so the suggested "persistence_path shares buckets" fix is also wrong for multi-replica deployments. The per-run scope matches CLI semantics, and the comment explicitly says this is the same block as the CLI's `rate_limit:`, so leaving it out does not make the comment false. What survives is a documentation and supportability gap with no behavioural failure, so it stays low severity.
verdicts.evidence:
- The grep for execution_rate_limit over docs/, deploy/ and src/ matched only src: config.py:511 (the field), config.py:1446 (_JSON_OBJECT_FIELDS) and service.py:3631 (the consumer). It found no docs.
- environment-variables.md:705, :762 and :806 document the sibling JSON knobs BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_DEFAULT_PROFILES, AWS_TEXTRACT_PROFILES and AZURE_SEARCH_PROFILES; :342 documents LLM_PROFILES.
- config.py:503-511: the comment says "Limiters are keyed by provider type (openrouter, azure_openai, bedrock, gateway)". That is true only for LLM limiters (llm/transform.py:1733-1742). ai_search.py:138 builds f"azure_ai_search:{hostname}".
- service.py:1091 `self._executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)`, and the docstring at 1036-1037 says "submits _run_pipeline() to a ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers=1". Runs in one process never overlap, which refutes the in-process N x rate claim.
- service.py:3631 calls from_settings(..., state_dir=data_dir), and runtime.py:57-58 returns None when persistence_path is None, so each run gets an in-memory registry. service.py:3636 constructs it and service.py:4331-4332 closes it, which confirms the per-run scope.

findings.title: Deleting the dev-admin account lets the next registrant of that username inherit the credential grant
findings.summary: is_dev_admin grants credential administration by username. delete_user deliberately frees the username for re-registration. ce3602aed lets any live admin reach DELETE, and the only guard is self-deletion. Open registration (the default) activates a newcomer immediately and does not reserve dev_admin_user.
findings.failure_scenario: Settings: dev_admin_user=devadmin, registration_mode=open. Admin A deletes the 'devadmin' account (204; R5 does not protect it because it holds no admin role). An anonymous user POSTs /api/auth/register with username devadmin and gets an active identity, so is_dev_admin is true. They POST /api/auth/admin/users/<A>/reset-password, receive A's new password, sign in as A and gain full identity-admin.
findings.evidence: admin_routes.py:131 (username comparison), :139-140, :235-240 (only a self-delete guard); local.py delete_user docstring ('a later registration of the same username gets a FRESH identity'); app.py:1116-1119 (activate when registration_mode == 'open'); config.py:224 (default 'open'); routes.py register has no reserved-name check. Before the window only the dev admin could reach DELETE, and it cannot delete itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse deletion of settings.dev_admin_user on this route, as self-deletion is refused. Also reserve that name at registration and/or bind the grant to the identity first admitted under it.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute it. I traced the whole path at 74c0ce0db and it holds. is_dev_admin grants credential administration by username alone (admin_routes.py:131). ce3602aed swapped `_require_dev_admin` for `_require_local_account_admin` (admin_routes.py:145-157), so any live human admin can now reach DELETE. The only name guard on that route stops an admin deleting their own account (admin_routes.py:235-237). Nothing protects the account named by settings.dev_admin_user. R5 (LastActiveAdminProtected) only covers the last active human admin role holder, and a plain dev_admin account holds no role. By design, delete_user retires the identity and its natural key so that 'a later registration of the same username gets a FRESH identity' (local.py:645-648). Registration mode defaults to 'open' (config.py:224). Under open mode _admit_identity activates newcomers at once (app.py:1116-1119). The register route checks only registration_mode and has no reserved-name check. A newcomer who registers that username passes is_dev_admin and can call reset-password on any account, including admin A, since set_password has no target guard. That takes over identity administration. No recorded ruling covers this. The config comment, the reference docs and identity-providers.md:47 all describe the grant as belonging to 'the one local user' by that name, which is exactly the weakness. I am lowering severity from high to medium for three reasons. (1) The attack needs a legitimate admin to delete the dev-admin account while leaving dev_admin_user configured, on a deployment that has both open registration and the short-term dev grant enabled. (2) The root weakness is older than the window: the grant was already bound to a username that could be claimed. Under open registration anyone can take the name whenever no account holds it (for example before the operator creates it, or after an out-of-band removal), and register has never reserved it. The window adds one new API path to that state, but it did not create the class of bug. (3) The attacker also has to win the race to re-register the freed name. The suggested fix is correct: refuse DELETE on settings.dev_admin_user and reserve the name at registration. Binding the grant to an identity would also fix the older exposure.
verdicts.evidence: admin_routes.py:123-131 (is_dev_admin compares user.username == settings.dev_admin_user); admin_routes.py:134-143 (can_manage_local_accounts: dev admin OR active_human_admin_ids); admin_routes.py:145-157 + ce3602aed diff (the dependency changed from _require_dev_admin, which admitted only the dev admin, to _require_local_account_admin); admin_routes.py:235-237 (only guard: user_id == admin.username); admin_routes.py:239-250 (LastActiveAdminProtected is the only refusal); admin_routes.py:205-219 (reset_password has no target restriction, so the new holder can reset admin A's password and receives it); local.py:631-648 (delete_user retires the identity and its natural key, and the docstring says a re-registration gets a FRESH identity); config.py:224-228 (registration_mode defaults to 'open'; dev_admin_user is a username grant); app.py:1110-1119 (activate=settings.registration_mode == 'open'); routes.py register (around lines 371-381) checks only registration_mode, with no reserved or dev_admin_user check; the dev_admin_user docs (identity-providers.md:47, configuration.md:381) contain no ruling that the name is reserved or that deleting it is allowed.

verdicts.reason: I traced every step of the path at 74c0ce0db and nothing guards it. (1) After ce3602aed, `_require_local_account_admin` lets any active human admin reach DELETE /api/auth/admin/users/{user_id} (admin_routes.py:146-159). Before the change only `is_dev_admin` could reach it. (2) The only guard in delete_user is `user_id == admin.username` (admin_routes.py:235). No check refers to settings.dev_admin_user. The dev_admin_user setting is read in only three places: config.py, admin_routes.py:120/131 and routes.py:796. (3) The retirer refuses only for R5 (last active human admin). A dev-admin account that holds no admin role passes, and `retire_identity` rewrites the natural key so the name is free for a fresh identity (identity_authority.py:2124-2131; local.py:645-648). (4) registration_mode defaults to "open" (config.py:224). `register` has no reserved-name check (routes.py:78-110, 355-428), and `_admit_identity` passes `activate=settings.registration_mode == "open"` (app.py:1116-1119), so the newcomer is active right away. (5) `_authenticate_sync` builds UserIdentity with `username=claims.username`, the local username (local.py:1313-1315). For the newcomer, `is_dev_admin` compares that against dev_admin_user and returns True (admin_routes.py:131). (6) `reset_password` accepts any local username and returns the new password (admin_routes.py:207-222), so the attacker can take over admin A's account. No recorded ruling in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md covers the dev admin. The new test file has no case for deleting the dev-admin account and re-registering the name. Two caveats, neither of which refutes the finding. First, the name was already unreserved before the window: if the dev-admin account had never been registered, the first open registrant could claim it. The window adds the new step, which is that an ordinary admin can free an established dev-admin name over HTTP. Second, the exploit needs registration_mode=open, which is the default. In email_verified mode the identity is left pending (activate=False). I keep the severity at high because the payoff is an anonymous user gaining credential administration over every local account, including the admins.
verdicts.evidence: admin_routes.py:131 `return dev_admin_surface_enabled(settings) and user.username == settings.dev_admin_user`; admin_routes.py:141-144 live-admin grant (added in ce3602aed); admin_routes.py:235-237: the only guard is the self-delete check `if user_id == admin.username`; admin_routes.py:207-222: reset_password on any username returns the generated password; local.py:645-648 and identity_authority.py:2127-2131: retirement rewrites the (provider, subject) key, so the freed username gets a FRESH identity; config.py:224: `registration_mode ... = "open"`; app.py:1116-1119: `activate=settings.registration_mode == "open"`; routes.py:78-110 RegisterRequest: no reserved-name validator; local.py:1313-1315: `UserIdentity(user_id=claims.identity_id, username=claims.username)`; grep for dev_admin_user under src/elspeth/web: only config.py, admin_routes.py:120/131 and routes.py:796, so registration and deletion are never guarded. `git show ce3602aed`: the dependency changed from `_require_dev_admin` to `_require_local_account_admin` on all four routes.

findings.title: Admin password reset and account creation write no audit row now that every administrator can use them
findings.summary: The base docstring justified structlog-only mutations because the surface was 'off in any deployment whose audit trail matters'. ce3602aed enabled it for every local-auth administrator and rewrote the docstring to say the routes 'retain their operational log events', but added no auth_events row. AuthAuditEventType has no credential-reset or credential-created event. The 2026-08-07 spec accepts this gap only for the CLI. No ruling in recent-code-hints covers it.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin A POSTs /api/auth/admin/users/B/reset-password on admin B, receives B's password, signs in as B, and performs role grants that the Landscape attributes to B. The Landscape has no event for the reset or its actor; only a dev_admin_password_reset structlog line exists. set_password (local.py:720-727) also leaves B's outstanding JWTs valid.
findings.evidence: Base docstring at 7c986dc97, lines 10-13, vs HEAD admin_routes.py:7-9; :203 and :220 call _slog.info only; contracts/auth.py:100-128 event vocabulary; audit.py:1365-1398 shows that administrative disable records actor_identity_id; spec docs/specs/2026-08-07-change-password-panel-design.md § Audit accepts the gap for the CLI only.
findings.suggested_fix: Record an auth_events row, with the acting identity and request provenance, for create and reset before responding, and fail closed. Or record an explicit operator ruling that accepts the gap for local-auth deployments.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute it. The code path is reachable as described, no guard writes an auth_events row, and I found no recorded ruling that accepts the gap for the widened surface. Before this window, the audit gap was justified only because the surface was limited to one configured dev account and was 'off in any deployment whose audit trail matters'. ce3602aed opened the same routes to every live local-auth administrator, deleted that justification, and added no audit record. The finding also says outstanding JWTs survive a reset, and that is correct: set_password only updates the hash. I kept the severity at high. The actor must already be an administrator, but these routes also let one administrator reset another administrator's password and then act under that person's name in the Landscape without trace. That attribution gap is exactly what an audit-grade product has to close.
verdicts.evidence: Pinned commit 74c0ce0db. admin_routes.py:134-143: can_manage_local_accounts admits any user in authority.active_human_admin_ids(). admin_routes.py:146-158: _require_local_account_admin applies that check to every route. The reset route (admin_routes.py:207-222) calls provider.set_password and then only _slog.info("dev_admin_password_reset", ...) at :220. The create route (admin_routes.py:184-205) only calls _slog.info at :203. Neither route checks whether the target is itself an administrator. local.py:451-481 (create_user) and local.py:720-735 (set_password) are plain sqlite writes with no audit callback or token_audit_intents row, and the set_password docstring says outstanding JWTs are not revoked. contracts/auth.py:100-128: AuthAuditEventType has no credential-created or credential-reset event. Running `git show ce3602aed` shows the old docstring ('Mutations are recorded via structlog only -- this surface is off in any deployment whose audit trail matters') replaced with 'Credential creation and reset retain their operational log events', and the config.py comment changed from 'production deployments ... must leave this unset' to local-auth administrators holding the capability. The only accepted-gap text I found is docs/specs/2026-08-07-change-password-panel-design.md:446, which covers only the CLI `elspeth composer users add`. docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md contains no ruling on audit for reset-password or credential creation (grep for reset-password, set_password, credential and auth_events rows came back empty). grep for dev_admin_password_reset across src and docs matches only admin_routes.py:220.

verdicts.reason: The core defect holds at 74c0ce0db. ce3602aed ("let local administrators manage local accounts", Fixes elspeth-3031873251) widened the credential surface from the single configured dev admin to every active human administrator on a local-auth deployment. It kept structlog as the only record of credential creation and reset. I found no ruling that accepts this: recent-code-hints has no entry for it, the commit message says nothing about audit, and the one accepted gap in the change-password spec covers only the CLI. The window rewrote the docstring and dropped the base's justification ("off in any deployment whose audit trail matters") instead of addressing the gap. The reset-then-impersonate path is concrete: A resets B, signs in as B, and the Landscape has no row for the reset or its actor. I am lowering severity to medium for three reasons. (1) The same structlog-only reset already existed before the window for the dev admin on any local deployment, so the window widened an existing gap rather than creating one. (2) The claim that B's outstanding JWTs stay valid is documented, deliberate behaviour, not a defect: the local.py:720-725 docstring says so, and the people-access plan says the UI must not promise sign-out. (3) The creation half matters less. A new credential grants no authority until identity admission, which the docstring says runs on the existing audited paths. The remaining gap is attribution of an administrator-initiated credential takeover. That is real in an audit-grade product, but the actor is already a fully trusted, deployment-wide administrator.
verdicts.evidence:
Evidence at the pinned commit:
- The route logs only. At admin_routes.py:217-222, reset_password calls provider.set_password and then _slog.info("dev_admin_password_reset", ...). At :194-205, create_user does the same with _slog.info("dev_admin_user_created"). Neither route writes an auth_events row.
- The route is open to every local-auth administrator. At admin_routes.py:134-158, can_manage_local_accounts admits any id in authority.active_human_admin_ids (identity_authority.py:1471-1482) on auth_provider=="local". At base, _require_dev_admin admitted only the configured dev_admin_user.
- The audit justification was removed, not replaced. The base docstring said "Mutations are recorded via structlog only -- this surface is off in any deployment whose audit trail matters". At HEAD, :7-9 says instead that creation and reset "retain their operational log events".
- The event vocabulary has no event for this. contracts/auth.py AuthAuditEventType lists login, token_issued, auth_failure, logout, identity_*, role_*, relationship_* and governance events. It has no credential-created or credential-reset event.
- The only recorded acceptance covers the CLI. docs/specs/2026-08-07-change-password-panel-design.md § Audit says: "Also unrecorded by design: `elspeth composer users add` writes no auth_events row". It records nothing for the web admin routes, and neither recent-code-hints.md nor the ce3602aed message does either.
- Grounds for the lower severity: local.py:720-725 set_password documents "Outstanding JWTs are NOT revoked" as deliberate, and docs/plans/2026-09-20-people-access-panel.md:316-317 repeats it. Identity admission and retirement are audited separately (docstring :8-9, delete path via provider.delete_user with a reason).

findings.title: Web credential deletion's retirement audit row names no actor although many admins can now delete
findings.summary: delete_user passes only the username and reason to the provider. _record_retirement writes identity_disabled with metadata.actor='operator', no actor_identity_id and no request fields. That was defensible when the only deleters were the single dev admin or the CLI. After ce3602aed, any of N administrators can delete, and the Landscape cannot say which one did.
findings.failure_scenario: Admins A and B exist. The account 'jane' is deleted with reason 'left the team'. auth_events shows identity_disabled, cause credential_deleted, actor 'operator', no request_id. The deleting admin appears only in the structlog line at :257-263.
findings.evidence: admin_routes.py:240; app.py:1056-1066; audit.py:1029-1046 ('actor': 'operator', request fields None); identity_authority.py:545-551 IdentityRetired ('no actor identity to name'); by contrast audit.py:1377-1398 record_identity_disabled carries actor_identity_id.
findings.suggested_fix: Thread admin.user_id and the request through LocalAuthProvider.delete_user, RetireIdentity and IdentityRetired, and record them as record_identity_disabled does. Keep 'operator' only for the CLI path.

verdicts.reason: I traced the path at 74c0ce0db and the finding holds. Since ce3602aed, `_require_local_account_admin` lets two kinds of caller use DELETE /api/auth/admin/users/{user_id}: the configured dev_admin_user and any identity in `authority.active_human_admin_ids`. Before that commit only the single configured dev admin could, so the deleter could be worked out from configuration. Now it cannot. The route hands only (user_id, reason) to `LocalAuthProvider.delete_user`. No actor, admin id or request goes into the retirement chain: not through `retire_identity`, not through `IdentityRetired`, and not through `record_identity_retired`, which hardcodes metadata actor='operator' and sets request_id, client_host and user_agent to None. `retire_identity` also emits `IdentityAuthorityRevoked` with actor_kind='operator' and actor_identity_id=None. The only thing that names the admin is the structlog line, and structlog is not the audit trail. I found no ruling in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md that accepts this. The reason text the admin types, recorded as 'local credential deleted: <words>', does not reliably identify the deleter. The frontend calls this route from client.ts:588, so the path is live. One more point: the `record_identity_retired` docstring says the deleting surface 'is the OPERATOR and has no request to read'. For the web route that is now false, because that route has both a request and an authenticated admin. Medium severity is right: this is an attribution gap in the audit trail, and no data is corrupted.
verdicts.evidence:
- src/elspeth/web/auth/admin_routes.py:229 and :240: admin = Depends(_require_local_account_admin), then `provider.delete_user(user_id, reason=body.reason)`. No admin id or request is passed.
- admin_routes.py:257-263: the admin appears only in `_slog.info("dev_admin_user_deleted", actor=admin.user_id, ...)`.
- ce3602aed diff: `can_manage_local_accounts` widened the gate from `is_dev_admin` (one configured user) to any user in `authority.active_human_admin_ids`.
- src/elspeth/web/auth/local.py:631 and :688: `delete_user(self, user_id, *, reason)` calls `self._retire_identity(user_id, reason, credential_exists, delete_credential)` with no actor parameter.
- src/elspeth/web/coordination/identity_authority.py:2112-2121: `retire_identity` has no actor parameter. :2190-2200 emits `IdentityAuthorityRevoked(actor_kind="operator", actor_identity_id=None)`. :545-551: the `IdentityRetired` docstring says 'no actor identity to name'.
- src/elspeth/web/app.py:1056-1066: `_record_retirement` passes only provider, identity_id, username, retired_subject and reason.
- src/elspeth/web/auth/audit.py:1008-1046: `record_identity_retired` writes request_id, client_host and user_agent as None and metadata {'actor':'operator','cause':'credential_deleted',...}. Its docstring claims the deleting surface 'has no request to read', which is stale for the web route.
- By contrast, audit.py:1377-1398 `record_identity_disabled` uses `_admin_provenance(request, actor_identity_id=...)`.
- No matching ruling in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md.

findings.area: web/composer advisor gate persistence (blast radius of advisor_decision.py:22)
findings.title: Completion-gates schema v2 and required cause shipped without a session epoch bump
findings.summary: Commit 41aeaeac0 added the required AdvisorSignoffGateFact.cause (advisor_decision.py:22). parse_completion_gates now rejects any completion_gates value that lacks schema_version==2 or a valid cause, including an empty mapping. SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH and _COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH stayed at 65, the value set by 539121b17, whose writers produced exactly those now-rejected shapes.
findings.failure_scenario: 1. A session store is created at epoch 65 by any build from 539121b17 to 41aeaeac0^ (the epoch-65 deploy note required a DB rename, so this is the expected operator state). 2. Build 74c0ce0db is deployed; the epoch check passes (65 == 65). 3. Every session that ever finished a compose turn has composer_meta.completion_gates == {} or a block without a cause. 4. The next message/compose/validate/execute request on that session, and the audit-readiness and shareable-review reads (messages.py:216, compose.py:135, _helpers.py:998/2760, execution/service.py:1272/1800/2794, execution/routes.py:1003, audit_readiness/service.py:564, shareable_reviews/service.py:434), raises ValueError('Tier 1: completion_gates.schema_version must be 2'). The result is a crash on each request for every existing session, where the project convention is a clean refusal at startup.
findings.evidence: git show 539121b17:src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py lines 185-238: the writers return {} or {advisor_signoff:{status,detail,suggestion,for_graph,note}} with no version or cause. At HEAD, completion_gates.py:273-276 requires version 2 and :309-315 requires cause. sessions/models.py:358 and schema.py:40 were last changed in 539121b17, whose message says a required note key 'cannot be read forward. Pre-1.0 policy: the store is recreated'. HEAD writers (completion_gates_meta_from_facts :185, called from _helpers.py:997/998/2763) always emit schema_version 2, so only rows written before 41aeaeac0 are affected. Recorded ruling (docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md:17,111,260): old-format envelopes must fail validation. Rejecting them is deliberate; leaving out the epoch fence is the disputed part.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH and _COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH to 66, update the epoch literal sites (tripwire tests, docs, website/get-started.html), and record it in the hints appendix. Old stores are then refused once at startup with the recreate instruction.

verdicts.reason:
I traced the path at 74c0ce0db and could not refute it. 41aeaeac0 removed completion_gates_meta_value, which wrote {} on every clean turn and a cause-less {advisor_signoff:{status,detail,suggestion,for_graph,note}} on a block. At HEAD, parse_completion_gates (completion_gates.py:273-276) rejects any envelope without schema_version==2, including {}, and :309-315 rejects any block without a valid cause. The epoch stayed at 65 (models.py:358, schema.py:40). No commit after 41aeaeac0 in the window (23185f55a merge, 74c0ce0db CHANGELOG) bumps it.

The codebase's own convention is to fence exactly this class of change at startup. The epoch-62 comment at models.py:346-348 reads: "Semantic-only JSON grammar cut: reject earlier stores at startup before an old blocked envelope can fail during session reload." The 539121b17 message bumped to 65 for a required JSON key because such a store "cannot be read forward".

The recorded ruling does not cover the missing fence. It says "no backwards compatibility; old-format envelopes must fail validation" and "do not add migrations, compatibility branches or reset existing data" (plan :17, :111, :260; hints entry). An epoch bump is none of those things. It is the project's fail-closed refusal of a stale store, not compatibility code, and the ruling is silent on it. 74c0ce0db makes the gap visible in the docs: the CHANGELOG now says startup accepts "an existing database matching the exact current schema epoch (session 65)". An epoch-65 store written before 41aeaeac0 passes that check, then every existing session fails with ValueError on each of the uncaught parse sites.

Limits: the only stores affected are epoch-65 stores that builds between 539121b17 (09-22 14:38) and 41aeaeac0 (09-23 00:55) wrote into, which means dev or staging stores on the unreleased branch. Upgrades from 0.8.0 are still refused at startup because their epoch is below 65. The failure is loud (a Tier 1 ValueError giving HTTP 500), not silent. It bricks every existing session in an affected store with no startup message pointing to the recreate step, and that is the outcome the convention exists to prevent. Medium is fair, with low arguable given how narrow the window is.
verdicts.evidence:
- The old writer: `git show 41aeaeac0 -- src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py` shows the removed completion_gates_meta_value returning `{}` (no blocker) or an advisor_signoff with no cause and no schema_version.
- The HEAD reader: src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py:273-276 (`version = raw["schema_version"] if ... else None; if type(version) is not int or version != 2: raise ValueError("Tier 1: completion_gates.schema_version must be 2")`) and :309-315 (cause must be a string that parses as AdvisorBlockCause).
- The epoch: src/elspeth/web/sessions/models.py:358 `SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65` and src/elspeth/web/sessions/schema.py:40 `_COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH = 65`. `git log 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db -- sessions/models.py sessions/schema.py` shows last changes at 539121b17, before 41aeaeac0.
- The precedent: models.py:346-348 (epoch 62, "reject earlier stores at startup before an old blocked envelope can fail during session reload"), and the 539121b17 commit message.
- Uncaught callers: execution/routes.py:1003, composer/compose.py:135, messages.py:216 (whose comment says "Parsed here, outside every try ... must propagate"), _helpers.py:998/2760, audit_readiness/service.py:564, shareable_reviews/service.py:434, execution/service.py:1272/1800/2794.
- The ruling: docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md:17, :111, :260 require old envelopes to fail validation and forbid migrations, compatibility code and data resets. None of it addresses the epoch fence.
- The CHANGELOG: 74c0ce0db states startup accepts an existing session DB at exactly epoch 65.
- Scope: 41aeaeac0 also changed tests/unit/web/sessions/test_schema.py:539 so that the epoch-61 envelope now fails on "schema_version must be 2". That shows the author knew earlier envelopes are now rejected wholesale, yet the epoch was not moved.

findings.title: Inspection confirmation must equal observed headers, stranding CSVs with blank or duplicate headers
findings.summary: transition_source_inspection_review now requires the submitted columns to equal facts.observed_headers, but the earlier checks at :1060/:1062 reject blank and duplicate columns. The CSV inspector keeps blank and duplicate header cells (it only warns), and the frontend's rename editor was removed, so no submission can pass.
findings.failure_scenario: In guided mode a user uploads a CSV whose header row is 'id,,name' or 'a,a,b', picks the csv plugin and submits options. The inspect_and_confirm turn appears. 'Looks right' sends the observed columns and fails with 'inspection columns must be non-empty' or 'must be unique'. Any other list fails with 'must match the observed headers'. The route accepts only edited_values and offers no back action, so the source step cannot be completed from this turn. Before the window, the 'Edit columns' editor let the user rename past it.
findings.evidence: stage_transitions.py:1058-1069. source_inspection.py _inspect_csv: headers = tuple(h.strip() for h in rows[0]) with warnings only for empty or duplicate headers. At HEAD, InspectAndConfirmTurn.tsx handleLooksRight sends payload.observed.columns verbatim, and the editor was removed in 07faf477e (compare with git show 7c986dc97:.../InspectAndConfirmTurn.tsx). sessions/routes/composer/guided.py:2798-2810 accepts only edited_values.
findings.suggested_fix: Retiring guided mode resolves this; do not invest in the guided lane for it. Only if guided ships in a release before it is retired: reject blank or duplicate observed headers in transition_source_schema_form (:991), so the user never enters an inspection_review turn they cannot complete.

verdicts.reason: The blank-header half of the finding holds and I confirmed it at 74c0ce0db. The duplicate-header half is wrong. With duplicate headers the inspect_and_confirm turn is never emitted: the payload validator requires unique columns and rejects the turn when it is built. That failure predates the window and was not introduced by it. For a header row such as 'id,,name', the pinned code leaves no way to complete the turn. Before the window the removed rename editor allowed the user to replace the blank name and pass. The change is a deliberate ruling that inspection confirms the actual headers (docs/reviews/2026-09-22-chat-card-repairs.md:14-17). That ruling does not address blank headers, and the resulting dead end is unintended. Severity stays low because guided mode is being retired, the Guided radio is disabled, and only saved Guided defaults and the tutorial still reach this path.
verdicts.evidence:
Blank-header path, traced step by step:
(1) inspect_blob_content (source_inspection.py:267) calls _inspect_csv with columns=None. That sets headers = tuple(h.strip() for h in rows[0]) (:594), which gives ('id','','name'). The code only adds a warning (:626-627) and returns observed_headers=headers (:713).
(2) Nothing earlier rejects the empty name. _validated_inspection_facts (stage_transitions.py:210-220) checks only that the headers and inferred-type keys are the same set. _strict_str_tuple (source_inspection.py:1064) and freeze_guided_str_sequence (resolved.py:198-218) accept empty strings. SourceIntent.__post_init__ (state_machine.py:382-420) does not check emptiness.
(3) The turn is emitted. _build_inspect_and_confirm_turn (emitters.py:854) sends columns=list(observed_headers). validate_current_turn runs when the turn is built (guided.py:679) and calls _validate_inspect_payload (protocol.py:1426). That uses _current_string_sequence(unique=True), which calls _current_text_error with the default nonempty=False (protocol.py:1283), so '' passes.
(4) The user cannot answer the turn. The frontend (InspectAndConfirmTurn.tsx at HEAD) offers only 'Looks right', which sends payload.observed.columns unchanged. The server rejects that with 'inspection columns must be non-empty' (stage_transitions.py:1060-1061). Any other list fails the new equality check at :1068-1069. The route (guided.py:2798-2810) accepts only edited_values.columns. The chat path (guided_chat_atomic.py:932-936) resubmits columns through the same transition, so it cannot pass either.
(5) Before the window, commit 7c986dc97 had no equality check (diff adds only :1068-1069). Its InspectAndConfirmTurn.tsx had handleRenameColumn (line 138), so the user could rename the blank column and pass.

Duplicate-header correction: _inspect_csv keeps ('a','a','b'), but _validate_inspect_payload rejects it with unique=True (protocol.py:1330-1331). _append_server_turn_record (guided.py:678-681) then raises InvariantError('Constructed current-schema turn is invalid'). The turn therefore never appears. This failure is independent of the window's change, so the finding's claim that 'Looks right' fails with 'must be unique' is misdescribed.

findings.title: ABSENT-preflight flagged notice promises a re-review 'on your next message' that the END gate now skips
findings.summary: _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_PUBLISHED_NOTICE (no_tool_policy.py:168-172) and the comment at :160-167 assume a block on an unchanged turn persists nothing. Since 41aeaeac0, messages.py:845-847 and compose.py:591-593 save a new state row whenever completion_gate_decision_changes() is true, even on an unchanged graph. A flagged_final_pass or flagged_no_repair block with runtime_preflight None (cause GRAPH_REJECTED) is therefore saved, and advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph skips the review on the next unchanged message. The copy is still chosen by preflight shape, not by cause, which contradicts the rewritten hints entry and Task 5 of the plan ('graph-rejection notices should retain their pipeline-change guidance').
findings.failure_scenario: Wired, Stage-1-valid pipeline; the prior row has no fact or a PASSED/UNAVAILABLE fact. The user asks a prose-only question and the model does not mutate, so the preflight is None. The advisor flags twice, so the turn blocks as flagged_final_pass with the ABSENT shape. Chat says 'validation and the advisory review run again on your next message', and the route saves a graph_rejected fact. The user resends without editing the pipeline: the gate logs composer_advisor_end_gate_skipped, no review runs, and completion stays withheld. The saved blocker's detail (which embeds the UNVERIFIED notice) says 'next message' while its suggestion (service.py:11388) says 'after your next pipeline change', and merge_completion_gates shows that detail again on every later turn.
findings.evidence: completion_gates.py:381-398 skips on an unchanged version, GRAPH_REJECTED and a matching fingerprint; service.py:3707 returns a None preflight only when the version did not move; service.py:8621-8627 maps the flagged reasons to GRAPH_REJECTED; messages.py:845-847 saves a row on a decision change; tests/unit/web/sessions/test_advisor_recovery_routes.py:123 saves a first block on an unchanged graph; test_no_tool_policy_segments.py:858-891 still pins this notice in the 'unchanged turn' family with the old premise in its comment; docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md Task 5 step 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_PUBLISHED_NOTICE to '...run again after your next pipeline change.', keeping the not-re-verified clause. Rewrite the :160-167 comment to state the cause-keyed rule. Move the constant to _NOTICES_FOR_A_PERSISTED_BLOCK in the segments test and fix that test's comment. The withheld twin and the finalize suffix are derived from it and follow automatically.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this finding. I traced the whole path at 74c0ce0db and every step is reachable. The comment at no_tool_policy.py:160-167 rests on the claim that "a fact persists only with a new state row, which only a mutating turn writes". Commit 41aeaeac0, which is in the window, made that claim false. Both routes now save a new row when the review decision changes, even if the version did not move. So an ABSENT-preflight block caused by a flag is saved as GRAPH_REJECTED, and the END gate then skips the review on the next unchanged turn. The notice still tells the user the review runs again "on your next message". The maintained hint says graph-rejection copy must require a pipeline change, so this is not a recorded ruling that allows the wording. The test_no_tool_policy_segments.py:858-891 test pins the stale wording and repeats the stale premise in its comment. The other ABSENT notices are correct: the UNREPAIRABLE_UNVERIFIED notice maps to MESSAGE_REJECTED, and the unavailable/malformed notices map to transient causes that are re-reviewed. Only the flagged_final_pass and flagged_no_repair arms, which map to GRAPH_REJECTED, are wrong. Completion stays withheld, which is the intended behaviour, so the harm is misleading instructions that send the user round a resend loop with no fresh review. Medium severity stands.
verdicts.evidence:
- service.py:3707-3745 (_reuse_or_recompute_runtime_preflight): returns None when the version did not move, there is no last preflight, there is no blob ref, and the graph is either unwired or Stage-1-valid. A prose-only turn on a wired, valid pipeline therefore reaches the ABSENT shape.
- service.py:6737-6747: the END gate skips only when advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph is true. When the prior row has no fact, the review runs.
- service.py:8621-8627: flagged_final_pass and flagged_no_repair both map to AdvisorBlockCause.GRAPH_REJECTED. The fact's for_graph is completion_gate_fingerprint(state).
- service.py around 8682-8692 (`elif runtime_preflight is None`): a rendered verdict (verdict.ok) goes to _compose_advisor_signoff_unverified_message.
- no_tool_policy.py:1136-1152: that function appends the _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_*_SUFFIX, derived from no_tool_policy.py:168-172. The notice says "validation and the advisory review run again on your next message."
- execution/completion_gates.py:238-248: completion_gate_decision_changes is true when the prior signoff was None and the new decision is blocked.
- messages.py:845-847 (compose.py:591-593 does the same): `elif result.state.version != state.version or completion_gate_decision_changes(...)` saves a new state row even when the version is unchanged. tests/unit/web/sessions/test_advisor_recovery_routes.py:122 (test_unchanged_graph_first_block_and_changed_failure_cause_are_saved) covers this.
- execution/completion_gates.py:381-398: on the next unchanged turn, version equal, cause GRAPH_REJECTED and a matching fingerprint mean the gate returns True, logs composer_advisor_end_gate_skipped, and no review runs.
- docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md:28-40 says: "Both routes save changed review outcomes in a new fenced snapshot even when the graph is unchanged ... graph rejection requires a pipeline change."
- tests/unit/web/composer/test_no_tool_policy_segments.py:858-891 puts _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_PUBLISHED_NOTICE in _NOTICES_FOR_AN_UNCHANGED_TURN_BLOCK and asserts "on your next message", with a comment built on the outdated premise.

findings.title: Durable blocker detail says the composer's summary was withheld, but END-gate blocks now publish it (known open item M-6)
findings.summary: _advisor_signoff_blocked_wording defaults notice to _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_NOTICE (service.py:11315), and the ABSENT arm passes _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_NOTICE (service.py:10956). Both are the withheld twins, built at no_tool_policy.py:144 and :173 by appending ADVISOR_PROSE_WITHHELD_PUBLIC_DISCLOSURE. The END gate sets prose_withheld=False (service.py:8611) and publishes the reply, so the readiness blocker detail, the failed advisor_signoff check and the saved completion_gates.advisor_signoff.detail all falsely say 'ELSPETH withheld the composer's own summary of this exchange'.
findings.failure_scenario: Green-preflight turn, advisor FLAGs. Chat shows the model's reply and the published notice. The Checks/readiness panel, GET state, execution readiness and the shareable review read the saved fact through merge_completion_gates (completion_gates.py:343) and tell the user the summary was withheld, directly contradicting the reply and the reviewer note shown on the same screen.
findings.evidence: service.py:8611 prose_withheld = False; service.py:8628-8641 turns the detail into AdvisorSignoffGateFact.detail; service.py:11315 notice default; service.py:10956; docs/reviews/2026-09-22-advisor-reviewer-note-final-review.md:508-520 records this as open with the operator, not ruled correct.
findings.suggested_fix: Default notice to _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_PUBLISHED_NOTICE and pass _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_PUBLISHED_NOTICE in _advisor_signoff_unverified_validation. Case 5 does its own genuine withholding and does not go through this helper, so it is unaffected.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this finding; the defect is real at 74c0ce0db. `_advisor_blocked_result` sets `prose_withheld = False` (service.py:8611), so the composer's reply is published. It then calls `_advisor_signoff_blocked_wording` at service.py:8628 without passing `notice`, so the default `_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_NOTICE` applies (service.py:11315). That constant is the published notice with `ADVISOR_PROSE_WITHHELD_PUBLIC_DISCLOSURE` appended (no_tool_policy.py:144). For the rendered-flag reasons (flagged_final_pass, flagged_no_repair, flagged_unrepairable at service.py:~11355-11385), the notice goes into `detail`. `detail` is stored as `AdvisorSignoffGateFact.detail` (service.py:8634-8641) and reused as the failed-check detail by the pending, red and unverified validation builders. The unverified builder passes `_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_NOTICE` (service.py:10956), which also carries the disclosure (no_tool_policy.py:173). The only `prose_withheld=True` producers are at service.py:1440 and 1481. Those are case 5 and the other remaining withholding arms, and they do not reach this helper. No earlier guard strips or rewrites the sentence.

This is not a deliberate ruling. recent-code-hints.md:80-89 records the 2026-09-22 ruling that blocked turns publish the reply and that "the notice composers select their `_PUBLISHED_` twins". That covers the chat composers only; the wording helper's default was never switched. The same entry says the leftover withheld arms are "kept pending an operator ruling, not by design". The final review (docs/reviews/2026-09-22-advisor-reviewer-note-final-review.md, M-6) lists this item as still open with the operator, not ruled correct.

Two narrowings. First, the unavailable and malformed reasons build their own `detail` without the notice, so only rendered-flag blocks show the false sentence. Second, the tests that pin `_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_NOTICE` check chat segments on genuinely withheld paths or check that the notice is absent from the message. None pins the durable `detail`, so nothing makes the current wording deliberate. The user-facing contradiction is real and persists across page loads, but it is wrong wording rather than data loss or a security issue, so medium, at the low end.
verdicts.evidence: service.py:8611 `prose_withheld = False`; service.py:8628-8641 wording call without `notice`, result stored in AdvisorSignoffGateFact(detail=...); service.py:11315 `notice: str = _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_NOTICE`; service.py:~11370-11385 flagged arms return f"{_advisor_flagged_header(...)} {notice}" or f"{notice} {findings}"; service.py:10952-10958 unverified builder passes `_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_NOTICE`; service.py:11435 pending builder uses the default; no_tool_policy.py:128-130 disclosure text "ELSPETH withheld the composer's own summary of this exchange"; no_tool_policy.py:144 and :173 withheld = published + disclosure; completion_gates.py:343 `detail = fact.detail if current else ...`; recent-code-hints.md:80-89 ruling says the notice composers use the `_PUBLISHED_` twins and the leftover withheld arms await an operator ruling "not by design"; final-review.md M-6 records the item as open.

findings.title: NUL in unadmitted planner prose makes the all-or-nothing planner audit cohort unwritable on PostgreSQL
findings.summary: The prose-reply extractor bounds the text by length and checks UTF-8 but does not reject NUL (\x00). The prose is staged and written as raw message content inside the single atomic planner audit write, and PostgreSQL text columns reject NUL.
findings.failure_scenario: The planner returns a text-only reply whose JSON content contains \u0000, and the reply is nudged (PROSE_REPLY). Later the plan succeeds. On PostgreSQL, add_messages_atomic fails on the saved-prose row, so every LLM-call, attempt and invocation row of the request is lost. The user gets AuditIntegrityError 'pipeline planner audit persistence failed before proposal creation'. Under psycopg2 the error is instead a raw ValueError that escapes the except SQLAlchemyError mapping. SQLite deployments do not show the failure.
findings.evidence: pipeline_planner.py:1627-1633 accepts any bounded str. The staging is at 4133. service.py:4867-4874 writes withheld.content raw as AuditMessageDraft.content in the one add_messages_atomic call, and :4884 maps only SQLAlchemyError. Before 19f882b8d the planner audit write held only hashes, metadata and tool projections, which canonical_json escapes. Driver behaviour was not executed (read-only brief).
findings.suggested_fix: Return "" from _unadmitted_prose for NUL-bearing text, as for oversized text. Alternatively reject or escape NUL in WithheldReply.__post_init__ or withheld_reply_envelope so every withheld-reply site is covered.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute it. I traced the code path at 74c0ce0db and nothing on it rejects, strips or escapes NUL. The unadmitted prose goes from the provider response into messages.content inside the single atomic planner-audit write. PostgreSQL text columns reject NUL, so that one row makes the whole cohort fail. The only NUL/control-character guards in web/ cover other data: interpretation values (validation.py:249/277), guided blob refs and CSV cells. None applies to chat or audit message content. Severity stays low because a provider has to actually emit a NUL character in a text-only reply that gets the PROSE_REPLY nudge. The same unguarded-NUL gap probably affects other assistant-content writes too, but I did not check those, so this site may be one instance of a wider class. I also did not run either PostgreSQL driver: the driver behaviour below is from library knowledge, not execution.
verdicts.evidence:
- pipeline_planner.py:1618-1633: `_unadmitted_prose` checks only that the content is a str and passes `require_bounded_text`.
- bounded_json.py:148-154 and :41-53: `require_bounded_text` → `consume_text` checks only string length, total length and UTF-8 encodability. NUL passes.
- pipeline_planner.py:4130-4133: on a PROSE_REPLY it calls `recorder.record_withheld_reply("planner_prose_unadmitted", _unadmitted_prose(response))`.
- audit.py:264-275: this drops blank text only.
- withheld_replies.py:52-54: `WithheldReply.__post_init__` checks for a non-blank str only.
- withheld_replies.py:57-67: the envelope carries only a sha256 of the content, so the envelope itself is safe.
- service.py:4867-4874: `withheld.content` is written raw as `AuditMessageDraft(content=...)`.
- _persist_payload.py:91-129: `AuditMessageDraft` does not validate content.
- service.py:4876-4884: there is one `add_messages_atomic` for the whole cohort (LLM-call, attempt, invocation and withheld rows), and the except maps only SQLAlchemyError to AuditIntegrityError.
- A grep for `\x00`, `\u0000` or chr(0) under web/sessions and web/composer found no guard for message content. The only hits are guided_blob_refs.py:69/110, guided/stage_transitions.py:487 and tools/sources.py:146. `_FORBIDDEN_CONTROL_CHARS_RE` (validation.py:249) is used only at validation.py:277, which covers interpretation values.
- pyproject.toml:123-129: both drivers ship. psycopg3 raises DataError, which SQLAlchemy wraps as SQLAlchemyError, so the user gets the AuditIntegrityError. psycopg2 raises a bare ValueError ("A string literal cannot contain NUL"), which is not a DBAPI Error and escapes the except. I did not execute either driver.

findings.title: Staged planner_prose_unadmitted row is not bound to the physical call that produced it
findings.summary: The saved row holds only origin, schema and content hash. Blank and oversized replies are skipped, the rows are appended after all call and attempt rows, and ComposerLLMCall has no response hash, so the kept text cannot be traced to a planner_call_ordinal or provider_request_id.
findings.failure_scenario: Three planner turns produce prose: an empty reply (attempt prose_nudged, not staged), a reply over 65,536 characters (prose_nudged, not staged), then a truncated prose reply (staged). The audit cohort then holds three prose-class attempts and one withheld row. An auditor cannot tell which call produced the saved words.
findings.evidence: pipeline_planner.py:4133 stages (origin, content) only, although call.planner_call_ordinal is in scope. withheld_replies.py:57-66 builds the envelope, service.py:4867-4874 appends the rows after the other drafts, and audit.py:272-273 skips blank content.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry planner_call_ordinal, and optionally a truncation flag, on WithheldReply for the planner origin and write it into the envelope.

verdicts.reason: I checked every factual claim at 74c0ce0db and all of them hold. Nothing links the staged planner_prose_unadmitted row to the physical call that produced it. Blank and oversized PROSE_REPLY calls leave no row, so matching rows to calls by position in the cohort is unreliable, and an auditor has no way to verify the match. I found no guard, no other binding field and no recorded ruling that says unbound rows are intended. The reply-withholding review asked only that the words be recoverable, and they are: the text is kept in full. That is why the impact stays low. The gap is attribution. No evidence is lost or corrupted, and an auditor can often narrow the match using completion_tokens and error_message. The same unbound envelope is used for every withheld origin, but for the planner origin the ambiguity is sharper, because its rows are appended after all call and attempt rows rather than next to the turn they came from.
verdicts.evidence: pipeline_planner.py:4129-4133 stages only (origin, _unadmitted_prose(response)), although `call` and its planner_call_ordinal are in scope. findings.title: Model-catalog budget cut 32 KiB to 8 KiB to fit a test ratchet; the shipped catalog carries 3 of 503 slugs
findings.summary: b08fe591d set _MODEL_CATALOG_MAX_CANONICAL_BYTES to 8 KiB. Its own comment says this sizes the aid to fit the 119,398-byte 'initial-scaffold gate', which is the test-side _FIXED_SCAFFOLDING_MAX_CANONICAL_BYTES ratchet (106 KiB x 1.10). That ratchet's comment says it moves only by operator ruling and must not absorb growth by trimming load-bearing aids. After the LiteLLM 1.102 bump, the catalog now drops both azure and openrouter.
findings.failure_scenario: A deployment has no usable llm operator profile, and the user asks for an Azure or OpenRouter model. Before the window the slug was carried in the aid and bound with no discovery turn, which is the function's stated purpose. Now models_omitted lists azure and openrouter, model.catalog becomes discoverable, and the planner spends an extra list_models provider turn (re-sending the ~112 KB request) before it can bind. The per-turn saving is about 6.4 KB, so one added turn outweighs roughly 17 turns of savings.
findings.evidence: Measured at the pinned tree (PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src; elspeth.__file__ confirmed inside the worktree). At the 8 KiB cap the catalog is 1,846 B and carries bedrock only, with azure (232) and openrouter (268) omitted. At 9 KiB it is 8,289 B and carries azure and bedrock. Uncapped it is 15,212 B. Either raise _FIXED_SCAFFOLDING_BASELINE_BYTES for the LiteLLM 1.102 inventory and restore a cap that carries azure, or record a ruling that profile-less deployments pay the discovery turn. Then update the recent-code-hints ceiling inventory and the stale docstrings (F1).

verdicts.reason: I could not refute the finding. The behaviour change is real and reachable, and I found no recorded ruling for it. Before the window the cap was 32 KiB with whole-lists-or-none. At the pinned tree the uncapped catalog is 21,665 B, so the old code would have carried azure, bedrock and openrouter. b08fe591d set the cap to 8 KiB and defers the largest lists first. Azure alone is 7,650 B canonical, which cannot fit under 8,192 B once the base catalog is added. pyproject.toml now requires litellm>=1.102.0, so every deployment on this tree drops azure, whatever size its openrouter snapshot is. The source comment at planner_authoring_aids.py:1180-1181 takes the cap straight from the test ratchet: 119,398 = int(106 KiB × 1.10), which is _FIXED_SCAFFOLDING_MAX_CANONICAL_BYTES at test_pipeline_planner.py:193. The ratchet comment (test_pipeline_planner.py:141-146) says growth is never "absorbed by ... trimming load-bearing teaching text to fit". recent-code-hints.md:1667 still says 32K. I found no ruling in the commit's own docs changes, recent-code-hints or CHANGELOG. Two things argue against the finding, and together they lower the severity. It is not a correctness bug: omitted providers carry a details_via marker, the guidance at :2071-2073 says to follow it, the manifest makes model.catalog discoverable, and list_models stays advertised (test at :1917-1931), so no wrong slug can be bound. Also, the ratchet text names "teaching text", not identifier lists. The 09-03 band ruling (:163-167) lets a change move within the 10% band on its own merits, and staying inside the band is what this commit did. The pre-window comment already argued that carrying the whole inventory costs more than the discovery turns it saves. So the cost is at most one extra list_models turn, and it could be batched with other discovery calls. It applies only to deployments with no operator profile that bind an azure or openrouter slug; the profile path in _model_custody_rules at :717-722 is the recommended one. Some of the finding's numbers are wrong for this tree. I measured azure at 277 and openrouter at 458, not 232 and 268. The capped catalog is 1,824 B, and the uncapped one is 21,665 B, not 15,212. findings.title: Literal-prompt rules disagree: ask before adapting vs adapt then disclose vs keep unchanged
findings.summary: The new rule (aids:677-679, skill:177-180) says a required adaptation of a supplied literal prompt needs the user's decision first. The adjacent older rule (aids:680-684) says adding row variables is an adaptation to name in the reply, including when the turn stops at review cards. Skill:576-580 says to keep a user-supplied 'prompt' unchanged, while skill:588-591 says the user template must pass the upstream fields.
findings.failure_scenario: The user says: use the prompt 'Is this complaint urgent?'. The prompt references no row field, so a working node needs {{ row.complaint }} added. Depending on which rule the model follows, it stops to ask, adds the variable and discloses it, or ships the prompt verbatim. The verbatim version passes validation, because nothing rejects a template with no row reference, and then every row gets the same context-free prompt.
findings.evidence: The three texts are quoted in the report. state.py _validate_llm_prompt_roles_present and the template-name check do not require a row reference. No session evidence of misbehaviour, hence PLAUSIBLE.
findings.suggested_fix: State the precedence once, in both the aid and the skill. For example: adding row-variable references or output instructions around a supplied literal is allowed and must be named in the reply; changing the literal's own characters needs the user's decision first.

verdicts.reason:
The finding quotes the texts correctly, but read together they do not conflict. The new rule (aids:677-679, skill:177-180) is the precedence statement the finding asks for. It says to keep the supplied literal, and when a required adaptation would change it, to explain the change and get the user's decision first. That settles the C-vs-D tension the finding raises: skill:576 says to keep the user prompt unchanged, and skill:588-589 says the template passes upstream fields. When the literal has no row field, D cannot be met without an adaptation, and A says to ask first. The older rule (aids:680-684) is about disclosure, not permission. It says how to describe the saved prompt in the reply and requires naming any adaptation, including adaptations to prompts the model wrote from the user's words that were not a supplied literal (it also covers 'rewording a question'). Nothing in it lets the model skip A's ask-first step.

Of the three outcomes in the failure scenario, two are safe. 'Ask first' is what A requires. 'Append {{ row.complaint }} with the literal kept character-for-character, then disclose it' is a defensible reading of A (the literal's characters are unchanged) plus B. The harmful outcome is shipping the static prompt verbatim, and no rule allows it: skill:588-591 requires the template to pass the upstream fields and declare them, and A covers the adaptation case. The finding also says 'nothing rejects a template with no row reference'. That is true only in the narrow sense that no check blocks it. A non-blocking validation advisory flags exactly this case. The reviewer admits there is no session evidence of misbehaviour, and I could not trace a concrete path where the rules push the model toward a harmful result.
verdicts.evidence:
- Pinned HEAD: 74c0ce0db336e8ed67c6f532d070e7553fcd5059.
- src/elspeth/web/composer/planner_authoring_aids.py:677-679 (added in the window): "If a required adaptation would change the supplied literal, explain the needed change and obtain the user's decision before making it." This is the precedence rule.
- planner_authoring_aids.py:680-684 (older text): "Compare the actual saved prompt text with the user's words before describing it ... Adding row variables, rewording a question, or adding output instructions is an adaptation. Name those adaptations." This governs the reply's description, not permission to adapt.
- src/elspeth/web/composer/skills/pipeline_composer.md:177-180 repeats rule A under 'Requested Workflow Integrity'.
- pipeline_composer.md:576-580: 'keep it unchanged' appears inside the both-roles rule, and its point is not to move the user's text into the system role.
- pipeline_composer.md:588-591: 'The user template passes the actual upstream fields the node needs ... declare them in required_input_fields'. No rule tells the model to ship a static prompt.
- src/elspeth/web/execution/_validation_diagnostics.py:758-812 (_find_static_llm_prompt_advisories) flags any single-prompt llm transform whose template has no 'row' name.
- src/elspeth/web/execution/_validation_runtime.py:656-685 emits CHECK_STATIC_LLM_PROMPT_ADVISORY with the text "interpolates no row data, so every row receives an identical prompt ... add a 'row.*' reference".

findings.title: Absent-preflight graph_rejected block says the review re-runs "on your next message", but it is now persisted and the next message skips the review

verdicts.reason: I could not refute it; the path holds at 74c0ce0db. Take a wired, Stage-1-valid pipeline with no blob reference, and a turn that changes nothing. In that case _reuse_or_recompute_runtime_preflight returns None (service.py:3707-3745). If the advisor then FLAGs, the reason is flagged_final_pass or flagged_no_repair, and both map to cause GRAPH_REJECTED (service.py:8620-8626). The decision is AdvisorGateBlocked, bound to completion_gate_fingerprint(state) (8634-8642), and the ABSENT arm (8683-8698) builds the chat and blocker text from the UNVERIFIED notice. That notice says the review runs "again on your next message" (no_tool_policy.py:168-172). The prior row has no fact, so completion_gate_decision_changes (completion_gates.py:238-248) returns True, and both routes save a new state row with the blocked fact (messages.py:845-847 into _state_data_from_composer_state with advisor_gate_decision; compose.py:591-593 is the same). On the next message, the routes parse that fact (messages.py:216, compose.py:135) and pass it in as completion_gates. The turn changes nothing, so state.version == initial_version. The fact is GRAPH_REJECTED and its fingerprint matches, so advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph returns True (completion_gates.py:381-397). The END gate then falls through without a review (service.py:6741-6748), so the promise of a review on the next message is false. The comment at no_tool_policy.py:157-167 and the test tuple at test_no_tool_policy_segments.py:858-887 still say an ABSENT block "persists nothing". That premise was true before 41aeaeac0 and is no longer. The same commit rewrote the recorded ruling in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md to say that "Both routes save changed review outcomes in a new fenced snapshot even when the graph is unchanged" and that "graph rejection requires a pipeline change". So the ABSENT GRAPH_REJECTED copy now contradicts the ruling, and is not a deliberate case the ruling covers. The same blocker also contradicts itself: its suggestion (service.py:11385-11388) says "after your next pipeline change", while its detail embeds the UNVERIFIED notice, which says "on your next message". I lowered severity to low. The defect is wrong and self-contradictory copy on one turn; there is no data, audit or authz impact. The user is not blocked, because a pipeline change still triggers a review. The durable fact's own detail uses the default PENDING notice, which says "after your next pipeline change", so the skipped turns re-show accurate wording.

verdicts.reason:

(b) Confirmed. When `reason == "flagged_unrepairable"`, the durable fact's `detail` falls back to the default `_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_NOTICE` (service.py:8628-8642, 11315, 11375-11378). That notice says "Review the pipeline; validation and the advisory review run again after your next pipeline change". The cause is `MESSAGE_REJECTED` (8621-8627). `advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph` (completion_gates.py:381-397) stands aside only for `GRAPH_REJECTED`, so the next message does re-review and the sentence is false. The "after your next pipeline change" wording is new in the window (b77d64fcf/90d3c04f0; the old notice said "on your next message"). It also contradicts the recorded 2026-09-22 ruling that "message rejection asks for rewording" (recent-code-hints.md:28-44). Both routes persist a changed decision on an unchanged graph (messages.py:845-872). `merge_completion_gates` (completion_gates.py:337-338) then serves `fact.detail` after a reload.

(c) Confirmed but already known. `prose_withheld = False` (8611), yet the fact carries the WITHHELD twin (no_tool_policy.py:144). The final review names this exact gap as L16 and M-6 (docs/reviews/2026-09-22-advisor-reviewer-note-final-review.md:508-536): escalated to the operator, not ruled correct. It is not specific to the durable fact. The in-turn green and red blockers (11435-11441, `_advisor_signoff_blocked_validation`) and the absent-shape blocker (10949-10957, `_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_NOTICE`, also a withheld twin) carry the same sentence.

(a) Misdiagnosed. The mismatch between the in-turn and durable wording on the absent shape is real. Before the window, the durable detail was copied from the runtime blocker (old completion_gates.py:188-199); now it is built from the PENDING notice. But for the rendered-FLAG graph-rejection reasons (`flagged_final_pass` / `flagged_no_repair`, cause `GRAPH_REJECTED`), the persisted "after your next pipeline change" is the true statement. The next unchanged turn skips the END gate (service.py:6741). The in-turn unverified notice's "run again on your next message" is the false one. Its supporting comment, "Such a block persists nothing" (no_tool_policy.py:158-165), is contradicted by the persistence at messages.py:845 and by the gate's own comment at service.py:6738-6740 ("their outcome can now persist without editing the graph"). So the suggested fix, building the fact from the shape's notice, would make the durable text wrong for graph rejection. It would help only on the `MESSAGE_REJECTED` path. For the provider-failure reasons (`unavailable` / `malformed`), the wording is notice-independent (11390-11402), so there is no mismatch.

Severity is low, not medium. The durable suggestion ("Reword your chat message ... then resend") gives the correct clearing action. The user is misinformed about when review re-runs, but is not blocked.

- service.py:8621-8642: the `cause` map sends `flagged_unrepairable` to `MESSAGE_REJECTED`; `_advisor_signoff_blocked_wording(...)` is called with no `notice=`.
- service.py:11315: the default is `notice: str = _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_NOTICE`.
- service.py:11375-11378: the `flagged_unrepairable` branch returns `notice` (plus findings) as `detail`, with the suggestion "Reword your chat message...".
