findings.evidence: 539121b17 bumped 64->65 because the parser refused an envelope without note. `git show 5bcd983c9:src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py` has `return {}` at lines 199/202/234 and no schema_version, and at that commit _COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH=65 and SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH=65. At HEAD, schema.py:40 is still 65 and CHANGELOG says startup accepts an existing epoch-65 DB. Plan doc :17 rules that old-format envelopes must fail validation. The refusal is therefore intended, but it is not fenced by the epoch.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump to epoch 66 using the same sweep as 539121b17 (both constants, pins, runbooks, website, CHANGELOG), or record an explicit ruling plus CHANGELOG/runbook text that early-65 stores must be recreated. Update the stale test_epoch_61_is_rejected_before_reading_old_advisor_gate_grammar comment as well.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute the mechanism. The pinned code refuses exactly what the epoch-65 builds before 41aeaeac0 wrote, and the epoch did not move. At 5bcd983c9, `completion_gates_meta_value` returned `{}` on clean turns and wrote `advisor_signoff` with no `cause`. At 74c0ce0db, `parse_completion_gates` (completion_gates.py:274-276) raises "schema_version must be 2" on a mapping with no version. Both SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH (models.py:358) and _COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH (schema.py:40) are still 65. The parse calls run outside any try, at compose.py:135 and messages.py:216, so an early-65 store passes startup and then fails every request.

This breaks the project's own convention. 539121b17 bumped 64 to 65 for the same kind of change (an envelope the strict parser now refuses), and the schema.py:36-39 comment gives that reason. 74c0ce0db, which came after 41aeaeac0, then added CHANGELOG text saying startup accepts "an existing database matching the exact current schema epoch (session 65)". For early-65 stores that text is now false.

I rate it low rather than medium because few stores can hit it. The recorded ruling in the plan doc (:17) and in recent-code-hints says "Gate envelopes require schema version 2 and a cause; no old-format compatibility is provided", so the refusal is intended. The only gap is that the epoch does not fence it. Only stores created by unreleased, unpushed intermediate builds are affected: roughly the 10 hours between 5bcd983c9 (2026-09-22) and 41aeaeac0 (2026-09-23 00:55). The CHANGELOG upgrade path starts from released predecessors (0.8.0, below epoch 65), and those are still rejected at startup. The practical exposure is a dev or staging store, such as the live service if it was restarted on an epoch-65 build in that window. I could not check that without reading outside the pinned worktree.
verdicts.evidence:
Traced in the pinned worktree:
- **Parser.** src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py:274-276 has `version = raw["schema_version"] if "schema_version" in raw else None; if type(version) is not int or version != 2: raise ValueError("Tier 1: completion_gates.schema_version must be 2")`. Lines 295-298 require `cause` as a string.
- **Old writer.** `git show 41aeaeac0` removes `completion_gates_meta_value`, which returned `{}` when there was no preflight or no blocker. It also changes `completion_gates_meta_from_facts` from `return {}` to `{"schema_version": 2}`, and `CompletionGatesDict` gains `schema_version` and `cause`.
- **Epoch unchanged.** models.py:358 has `SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65`. schema.py:36-40 has `_COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH = 65`, and its comment still gives only the `note` key as the epoch-65 reason. `git log 539121b17^..74c0ce0db` on models.py shows no bump after 539121b17.
- **Uncaught call sites.** compose.py:135 and messages.py:216 call `parse_completion_gates(state_record.composer_meta)`, and the comments there say it is outside every `try` on purpose.
- **Order of commits.** `git log --ancestry-path 539121b17..74c0ce0db` gives 5bcd983c9 (the epoch-65 merge, old writer), then 41aeaeac0, then 74c0ce0db.
- **CHANGELOG.** 74c0ce0db adds: "Startup accepts an empty database or an existing database matching the exact current schema epoch (session 65...)".
- **Ruling.** docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md:17 says: "pre-release, no backwards compatibility; old-format gate envelopes must fail validation". The recent-code-hints diff in 41aeaeac0 says: "Gate envelopes require schema version 2 and a cause; no old-format compatibility is provided."
- **Stale test comment.** tests/unit/web/sessions/test_schema.py:539-541 was updated to expect "schema_version must be 2" for epoch-61 rows. It never covers an early-65 row, and no test fences one.

findings.title: Removed check name makes pre-upgrade share links 500 instead of 401
findings.summary: Dropping managed_identity_policy from the ValidationCheckName Literal makes AuditReadinessSnapshot.model_validate_json raise an uncaught pydantic ValidationError for share blobs minted before 364801194. _parse_blob only checks top-level keys, and the route catches only InvalidToken and PayloadNotFoundError.
findings.failure_scenario: A share link minted between 471d867fb and 364801194^. Its blob passes _BLOB_KEYS, and its validation_result.checks includes a passing managed_identity_policy row. After the upgrade the recipient opens the link and the token and digest verify. shareable_reviews/service.py:635 then raises a ValidationError (literal_error), which becomes an unhandled 500 instead of the designed 401 'unsupported share snapshot shape' or 404 'ask for a fresh link'. Links live 30 days, and the payload store and signing key survive a session-DB recreate.
findings.evidence: shareable_reviews/service.py:692-711: _parse_blob validates only frozenset(parsed) == _BLOB_KEYS and its docstring says older blob shapes get no fallback reader. routes.py:175-184 catches only InvalidToken and PayloadNotFoundError. No app-level ValidationError handler exists (app.py only handles RequestValidationError). Runbook staging-session-db-recreation.md:121 and :309 say the payload store is never deleted and the signing key is independent. config.py:684 sets a default lifetime of 30 days.
findings.suggested_fix: In resolve_token, catch pydantic ValidationError from the audit_readiness and composition_snapshot parses and raise InvalidToken, or version the blob and reject by version in _parse_blob.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this. I traced the path myself and it is reachable. 364801194 is inside the window and removes "managed_identity_policy" from the ValidationCheckName Literal (schemas.py:34-64; that Literal is the one the finding cites at :44). ValidationCheck.name is typed with that Literal under the strict, extra="forbid" base model (schemas.py:155, 186).

Before the removal, validate_managed_identity_policy emitted a PASSING ValidationCheck(name=CHECK_MANAGED_IDENTITY_POLICY) row for every composition that reached that phase (364801194^:_validation_materialization.py:627-637). A mark-ready composition's snapshot therefore carries that row. The check has existed since c9f3fe165 (2026-06-22), so the exposure is every blob minted from June up to 364801194, not only blobs minted after 471d867fb.

resolve_token (service.py:598-649) does four things in order. It verifies the token with the config key (app.py:660, which survives a session-DB recreate). It retrieves the blob. It runs _parse_blob, which checks only the top-level key set, the username and the compartment (service.py:692-711). It then calls AuditReadinessSnapshot.model_validate_json on validation_result (audit_readiness/models.py:90) at service.py:635. That call raises a pydantic ValidationError (literal_error on checks[i].name). The route catches only InvalidToken and PayloadNotFoundError (routes.py:175-184). None of app.py's handlers covers a pydantic ValidationError: they handle RequestValidationError (:2080) and OSError (:2039), among others. The result is a 500.

The _parse_blob docstring (service.py:696-698) says an older blob shape gets no fallback reader. Its explicit mapping of unsupported shapes to InvalidToken shows the intended answer is a 401, so the 500 is a real mismatch with that intent, not a recorded ruling.

Supporting evidence that the class is wider: 6a34007fb, also in the window, adds a REQUIRED `note: str | None` to ValidationReadinessBlocker (schemas.py:259-262). Any pre-upgrade blob with a non-empty readiness.blockers list fails the same way.

Why I lower the severity: the design already makes these links unusable ("no fallback reader"). The user-visible difference is a generic 500 with a server stack trace instead of a 401 "Invalid or expired share token". No data is exposed or corrupted, and the owner has to mint a new link in either case.
verdicts.evidence:
- schemas.py:34-64 (at 74c0ce0db): the Literal no longer contains "managed_identity_policy". `git diff 7c986dc97 74c0ce0db` shows it removed in 364801194.
- schemas.py:186: `name: ValidationCheckName` on the strict model.
- 364801194^:src/elspeth/web/execution/_validation_materialization.py:627-637: a passing check row is emitted on every clean run.
- `git log -S'"managed_identity_policy"'`: added in c9f3fe165 (2026-06-22) and removed in 364801194 (2026-09-21).
- audit_readiness/models.py:90: `validation_result: ValidationResult`.
- service.py:635: `AuditReadinessSnapshot.model_validate_json(...)` is not wrapped in any try.
- service.py:704-705: only top-level key-set mismatches become InvalidToken("unsupported share snapshot shape").
- routes.py:177-184: catches only InvalidToken and PayloadNotFoundError.
- app.py exception handlers (1240-2143): none covers pydantic.ValidationError.
- app.py:660: the signer key comes from settings.shareable_link_signing_key, so tokens stay verifiable across a deploy.
- Same class of break: schemas.py:259-262, where 6a34007fb adds the required `note` field to ValidationReadinessBlocker.

findings.title: Handoff branch ignores fact currency and says 'has not cleared' for an unreviewed graph
findings.summary: merge_completion_gates computes current/detail and then discards them in the new interpretation-handoff branch. It always emits the fixed 'has not cleared' wording, which breaks the module invariant that an advisor ruling is never attributed to content the advisor did not see.
findings.failure_scenario: The advisor blocks graph G1 and the durable fact is recorded for G1. A later save with no advisor decision (passes exhausted, orphan fall-through, recovery persist) moves the graph to G2, which has pending interpretation cards. /validate on G2 reports an advisor_signoff check saying the review 'has not cleared' for G2, which no reviewer saw. The non-handoff branch would use ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_DETAIL. Readiness gating is unaffected.
findings.evidence: completion_gates.py:342-343 computes current/detail. Lines 345-359 return early with handoff_detail regardless of current. Lines 54-57 state the attribution invariant.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a stale variant of the handoff wording when not current, or document why currency does not matter in this shape.

verdicts.reason: The code does what the finding says, but it does not break the invariant. The rule at completion_gates.py:54-57 is that the advisor's verdict is never repeated against content the advisor did not see. The interpretation-handoff branch (lines 346-359) repeats nothing from the fact for either a current or a stale graph: it drops fact.detail, suggestion and note and returns one fixed, verdict-free sentence. That sentence reads "has not cleared ... the advisory review remains outstanding". It is true of a graph no reviewer saw (no review has cleared G2 and one is still owed), so nothing is attributed to G2. The branch is deliberately neutral about currency, and the test covers the stale case. tests/unit/web/execution/test_completion_gates.py:194-249 runs the handoff merge with changed_graph=True and with every AdvisorBlockCause. For the stale case it checks that readiness is unchanged, that exactly one failed advisor check exists, and that the detail does not contain "completion remains withheld". The finding's comparison fails on that point. ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_DETAIL (lines 58-61) says "Composer completion remains withheld", which would contradict the handoff result's own readiness: this branch keeps completion_ready=True as the pending-handoff discriminator, as the in-turn builder does (service.py:11474-11520). Using that constant here would publish a false claim, and the test forbids the phrase. What is left is a wording preference: "has not covered this version" might read slightly better than "has not cleared" on a stale graph. That is a style nit, not a defect.
verdicts.evidence: completion_gates.py:342-343 computes current and detail. The handoff branch at :346-359 returns early with fixed handoff_detail, and it discards fact.detail even when current=True. So the branch never repeats a verdict, current or not, and that is all the invariant at :54-57 protects ("The verdict is not repeated"). The handoff_detail text at :356-357 says "has not cleared ... the advisory review remains outstanding". That is accurate for a graph no reviewer saw. ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_DETAIL at :58-61 contains "Composer completion remains withheld", which is false in the handoff shape because readiness (completion_ready=True) is kept at :359. The test test_persisted_advisor_fact_preserves_pending_handoff_until_reviews_resolve (tests/unit/web/execution/test_completion_gates.py:193-249) is parametrized over changed_graph in [False, True] and over every AdvisorBlockCause. At :236 it asserts that "completion remains withheld" is absent from the advisor check detail, so the stale handoff case was deliberately designed. The design plan (commit 41aeaeac0, docs plan line 204) says persisted failures must "retain the pending-interpretation handoff shape on reload: append advisor check evidence without replacing the review-card readiness discriminator". The finding itself says readiness gating is unaffected.

findings.title: completion_gates_meta_from_facts docstring and note comment describe old behaviour
findings.summary: The docstring says the serializer is used only by save paths with no advisor adjudication, but after 41aeaeac0 it serializes every turn-end save, including explicit decisions. The AdvisorSignoffGateDict.note comment (line 72) says the note is bounded at the parser, but parse_completion_gates enforces no bound.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer reads the docstring and changes completion_gates_meta_from_facts on the assumption that only recovery persists use it, which breaks turn-end persistence of CLEAN/BLOCKED decisions at _helpers.py:2763. Or they rely on parse_completion_gates to bound note length when it does not.
findings.evidence: _helpers.py:2763 calls completion_gates_meta_from_facts(resolve_completion_gate_facts(prior_facts, advisor_gate_decision, state)). The ADVISOR_NOTE_MAX_CHARS bound lives only in composer/service.py:11033/11119, and parse_completion_gates at :302-305 checks only for a non-empty str.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite both to describe current behaviour.

verdicts.reason: Half of this finding holds and half does not. The docstring half is correct. Commit 41aeaeac0 deleted `completion_gates_meta_value`, which used to be the serializer for compose saves. That makes `completion_gates_meta_from_facts` the only serializer, and the turn-end writer now uses it for explicit CLEAN/BLOCKED decisions. The docstring (blame 5166baab22, not updated) still says it is used "by save paths that carry NO advisor adjudication of their own (recovery persists…)" and that the fact is "parsed off the prior row first … then re-emitted unchanged". Both statements are now false for the main caller. The note-comment half misreads the code. "Bounded and sanitised at the parser (ADVISOR_NOTE_MAX_CHARS)" refers to the advisor-response parser `_parse_advisor_checkpoint_guidance`, which bounds the note through `_advisor_note_text`. It does not refer to `parse_completion_gates`, and that comment is accurate. Severity stays low because only a docstring is stale and runtime behaviour is correct.
verdicts.evidence:
Docstring confirmed stale:
- src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py:186-197 says the function serves only save paths with no adjudication and re-emits the prior row's fact unchanged.
- src/elspeth/web/sessions/routes/_helpers.py:2759-2763 is the turn-end writer. It calls `completion_gates_meta_from_facts(resolve_completion_gate_facts(prior_facts, advisor_gate_decision, state))`, and `resolve_completion_gate_facts` (completion_gates.py:212-233) replaces the prior fact with an explicit AdvisorGatePassed/Blocked decision. So this path serializes new adjudications, not prior facts.
- `git show 41aeaeac0` removed `completion_gates_meta_value`, which had been the compose-save serializer. The module docstring at lines 9-10 was updated to "serializes the effective facts", but the function docstring was not (`git blame -L 186,196` gives 5166baab22, 2026-08-02).
- Only the recovery helper at _helpers.py:985-998 matches the old description.

Note comment NOT stale (this part of the finding is refuted):
- completion_gates.py:71-72 (37fc43c00) says "bounded and sanitised at the parser (``ADVISOR_NOTE_MAX_CHARS``)".
- composer/service.py:9800-9808 says the note is populated on the FLAGGED arm of `_parse_advisor_checkpoint_guidance`, "bounded and sanitised by `_advisor_note_text`". That function is defined at service.py:9814 and calls it at :9891.
- service.py:11029-11033 reads "Bounded here, once, before any surface or row sees them", and :11119-11120 truncates to 600 characters.
- "The parser" in the comment therefore means the advisor checkpoint parser, and the claim is true. `parse_completion_gates` (completion_gates.py:302-305) was never presented as the place that bounds the note.

Net: the finding is a valid low-severity stale docstring at line 188 only. The suggested fix should rewrite that docstring and leave the line-72 comment alone.

findings.title: Operator execution_rate_limit governs the run but Landscape records the engine-default rate_limit
findings.summary: 24dccdd9e builds the RateLimitRegistry from self._settings.execution_rate_limit but leaves settings.rate_limit at the engine default. pipeline_config.config = audit_safe_resolved_config(settings) -> resolve_config(settings) persists rate_limit verbatim to Landscape and into the approval config hash. The operator telemetry and export policies are folded into settings precisely so Landscape records the effective policy.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator sets ELSPETH_WEB__EXECUTION_RATE_LIMIT={"services":{"azure_openai":{"requests_per_minute":30}}}. The run is throttled at 30/min, but its Landscape config records rate_limit default_requests_per_minute=60 with empty services, and the config hash is identical across runs made under different operator limits. Reproducing the run, or explaining its timing and capacity-retry failures, from the audit record gives the wrong throttle. Resumed runs take the resuming instance's limit, and nothing records it.
findings.evidence: service.py:3629-3636 (the comment itself says settings.rate_limit 'is only ever the engine default'); service.py:3442-3455 folds the telemetry and export policies into settings before PipelineConfig; the _approval_inputs_from_frozen docstring at :1141-1145 says operator settings 'also enter the Landscape run config'; preflight.py:597 calls resolve_config; core/config.py:3103-3137 fingerprints only secret-bearing free-form sections, not rate_limit.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply settings = settings.model_copy(update={'rate_limit': self._settings.execution_rate_limit}) both at :3451-3455 and in _approval_inputs_from_frozen at :1234-1236, then build the registry from settings.rate_limit. Intended consequence, the same as for telemetry and export: an operator change between approval and execution refuses the governed run via the :3552 hash recheck.

verdicts.reason: The finding holds at the pinned commit 74c0ce0db. 24dccdd9e is in the review window (it is at position 106 of `git log 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db`). It builds the run's RateLimitRegistry from WebSettings.execution_rate_limit (service.py:3631, 3636) but never folds that value into `settings`. `settings.rate_limit` therefore stays at the engine default, and that default is what reaches Landscape and the approval hash. Nothing upstream sets it: the composer YAML importer rejects `rate_limit` (yaml_importer.py:116), and operator_marked_config_dict only touches landscape.export (export_marking.py:12-26). Nothing downstream records the effective limit either: the orchestrator only passes the registry into the PluginContext (core.py:128/145, run_context_factory.py:92/155), and no core/landscape module refers to rate_limit. Before this commit the recorded default and the enforced default were the same. Since it, an operator override makes the recorded config wrong, and the config hash no longer changes when the operator changes the limit. No ruling in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md or elsewhere in docs mentions execution_rate_limit. Severity stays medium: row data is not changed, but the audit record states the wrong throttle, which affects timing and the capacity-retry outcomes the finding describes, and the operator-policy folding pattern shown below was applied inconsistently.
verdicts.evidence: service.py:3629-3631: the comment says "settings.rate_limit here is only ever the engine default", and the next line is `RuntimeRateLimitConfig.from_settings(self._settings.execution_rate_limit, ...)`, which feeds the registry at :3636. service.py:3442-3455 folds operator telemetry and export into `settings` before PipelineConfig; rate_limit is not folded. service.py:3543-3552 sets pipeline_config.config = audit_safe_resolved_config(settings, ...) and uses its stable_hash for the approval recheck. preflight.py:597 calls resolve_config(settings), and core/config.py:3251 is `settings.model_dump(mode="json")`, so the persisted dump includes rate_limit (the field at config.py:2203). service.py:1141-1145: the docstring says operator settings "also enter the Landscape run config"; :1234-1241 hashes the same config without rate_limit. web/config.py:503-511: the field is operator-owned, "never author-settable". yaml_importer.py:116 rejects `rate_limit` in a composition. A grep of src/elspeth/core/landscape finds no rate_limit reference, and the orchestrator only keeps the registry. `git log 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db` lists 24dccdd9e, so the change is inside the window.

findings.title: User-cancelled run with failed output finalization is never recovered (cancel_pending invisible to recovery)
findings.summary: A user cancel after the start permit sets saga_state=cancel_pending. The worker then moves status to cancelled, and transition_run_status rewrites saga_state only when the new status is running. If _finalize_output_blobs fails, the worker skips settlement and relies on peer recovery. But list_recoverable_run_records admits only status in (pending, running) or saga_state in (running, admission_refusal_pending), so this row is never a candidate. The window's new comment at service.py:4344-4345 claims unfinished outputs 'remain discoverable by peer recovery'.
findings.failure_scenario: The user cancels a running web run. During the GracefulShutdownError unwind the blob store raises an OSError, or one output blob fails to finalize. The run ends status=cancelled, saga_state=cancel_pending, and its output blobs stay pending permanently: no worker settlement, no recovery candidacy, and no other sweeper. The only callers of finalize_run_output_blobs are service.py:2439, service.py:4632 and recovery.py:175.
findings.evidence: run_cancellation_authority.py:64-65; repository.py:1794-1795; run_recovery_authority.py:145-161; service.py:4004-4046 (graceful path) and :4340-4345 (the new settlement and its comment). The unrecoverable state predates the window; the window's new settlement design and comment depend on the opposite being true.
findings.suggested_fix: Admit saga_state='cancel_pending' in list_recoverable_run_records, in both the SQL predicate and the locked recheck; project_terminal already maps INTERRUPTED to cancelled and appends the event once. At minimum, correct the :4341-4345 comment. Add a test: cancel after permit, make finalization fail, assert the run is listed as recoverable.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this. I traced every step at 74c0ce0db and the path is reachable as described.

1. The user cancel goes through ExecutionService.cancel (service.py:2858). That calls request_run_cancellation, which uses RepositoryRunCancellationAuthority.request (sessions/service.py:10558-10564). For a run past its permit, request writes saga_state="cancel_pending" and keeps status=running (run_cancellation_authority.py:64-65). It then sets the in-process shutdown event.

2. In the GracefulShutdownError handler (service.py:~4004), _finalize_output_blobs does not raise when finalization fails. OSError, SQLAlchemyError and the Blob* errors are in _FINALIZE_SUPPRESSED (service.py:4610-4616), and on those it returns False (4674-4691). A partial failure also returns False. So control reaches update_run_status(status="cancelled").

3. update_run_status calls transition_run_status (sessions/service.py:10687+). That function sets saga_state only when status=="running" (coordination/repository.py:1794-1795). The row therefore ends as status=cancelled with saga_state=cancel_pending.

4. The finally block settles only when both outputs_finalized and terminal_event_persisted are true (service.py:~4340). Here outputs_finalized is False, so mark_recovery_outputs_finalized is skipped.

5. Neither the SQL predicate nor the locked recheck in list_recoverable_run_records admits this row (run_recovery_authority.py:147 and :160). They require status in {pending, running} or saga_state in {running, admission_refusal_pending}. RunRecoveryService.recover (recovery.py:150) is the only consumer. Its _reconcile_terminal (recovery.py:175) is the only other place that finalizes outputs for a terminal run.

6. The only writer of cancel_pending is run_cancellation_authority.py:64, and no code anywhere reads it or moves a row out of it. The only other references are the enum (contracts.py:87) and the CHECK constraint (models.py:2527). No test covers recovery of a cancel_pending row; the only test hit is test_contracts.py, which just lists the enum. recent-code-hints.md has no recorded ruling on it.

The window added the settlement block and its comment, "unfinished outputs remain discoverable by peer recovery" (the + hunks in the 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db diff, service.py:4340-4345). For a cancel made mid-run, that claim is false.

One qualification narrows the finding without refuting it. If the cancel lands after the permit but while status is still pending, the later pending->running transition overwrites saga_state with "running" (repository.py:1795). That run stays recoverable. So the defect covers only a cancel made while status=running, which is the common case. The same stuck state also follows a normal completion that races a cancel_pending marker and then fails finalization.

Medium severity stands: output blobs stay pending permanently and no sweeper picks them up. The run's status and audit record are still correct.
verdicts.evidence:
Worktree the pinned review worktree at HEAD 74c0ce0db336e8ed67c6f532d070e7553fcd5059.
- src/elspeth/web/coordination/run_cancellation_authority.py:64-65: `saga_state="terminal_cancelled" if before_permit else "cancel_pending"`, `status="cancelled" if before_permit else run.status`.
- src/elspeth/web/coordination/repository.py:1794-1795: `if status == "running": values["saga_state"] = "running"`. No other saga write happens on transition.
- src/elspeth/web/execution/service.py:4610-4616: _FINALIZE_SUPPRESSED = (OSError, SQLAlchemyError, BlobNotFoundError, BlobQuotaExceededError, BlobStateError). At 4638-4643 these are caught, and at 4674-4691 the function returns False instead of raising.
- service.py GracefulShutdownError handler (~4004-4046): outputs_finalized = _finalize_output_blobs(...), then update_run_status(status="cancelled"), then the cancelled event with terminal_event_persisted=True.
- service.py:4340-4355 (added in the window): `if outputs_finalized and terminal_event_persisted:` guards mark_recovery_outputs_finalized. The comment at :4344-4345 reads "unfinished outputs remain discoverable by peer recovery."
- src/elspeth/web/coordination/run_recovery_authority.py:147 (`status.in_(("pending","running")) | saga_state.in_(("running","admission_refusal_pending"))`) and :160 (the same recheck). Neither admits cancelled + cancel_pending.
- grep over src/elspeth for cancel_pending/CANCEL_PENDING finds only models.py:2527 (CHECK), contracts.py:87 (enum) and run_cancellation_authority.py:64 (writer). No reader or sweeper exists.
- The only callers of finalize_run_output_blobs are service.py:2439, service.py:4632 and recovery.py:175. The last is reached only through list_recoverable_run_records (recovery.py:150).

findings.title: Saga settlement in finally raises SessionDerivedCustodyError when the failed status never landed, masking the original exception
findings.summary: The BaseException handler sets terminal_event_persisted=True whenever the failed event is persisted, including when _persist_failed_run_status swallowed an SQLAlchemyError or OSError (status still running) and on the signal path, where the status update is skipped. With outputs_finalized True, `finally` calls mark_recovery_outputs_finalized. Its UPDATE filters on terminal status, matches 0 rows and raises SessionDerivedCustodyError out of `finally`, replacing the re-raise of the original exception. The comment at :4347-4348 presents the mutation's status recheck as a gate, but it raises.
findings.failure_scenario: A pipeline crashes. The failed-status write hits a transient SQLite 'database is locked' error and the next event write succeeds. The Future's exception becomes SessionDerivedCustodyError ('session-scoped derived record is unavailable'), and _on_pipeline_done logs a custody-integrity class in exactly the case its docstring calls 'the ONLY place the failure surfaces'. The original class appears only later in exc_class_chain via __context__. A SystemExit raised inside the worker is likewise converted, so the callback's signal filter no longer applies. Recovery is unaffected.
findings.evidence: service.py:4306-4316, :4340-4355, :4419-4455 (the degraded return), :4284-4288 (skip on signal), :4711-4714, :4757; repository.py:1725-1740 raises when rowcount != 1; repository.py:5254-5283 (mutate does not wrap). No test in test_service.py:1016-1128 reaches the settlement with status still running.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the settle flag in the BaseException handler only when the failed status is durable (not a signal, status_update_exc_class is None, no IRTE), or track a separate terminal_status_persisted flag. Correct the :4347 comment. Add a test for the degraded-status path asserting the original exception propagates and no settlement call is made.

verdicts.reason: I traced the path at 74c0ce0db and could not refute it. Commit 6e377bdc4, inside the review window, added the settlement in `finally` and the `terminal_event_persisted = True` in the BaseException handler. `_persist_failed_run_status` catches SQLAlchemyError/OSError from `update_run_status` and returns only the class name, so the run row stays 'running'. The signal path skips the status update entirely. In both cases `run_already_terminal` stays False, so the failed event is still appended. `append_run_event` has no terminal-status precondition, so that append can succeed, which sets `terminal_event_persisted=True`. `_finalize_output_blobs` returns True when there is no blob service or every blob settled. `finally` then calls `mark_recovery_outputs_finalized`. Its UPDATE filters on terminal status, so it matches 0 rows and raises `SessionDerivedCustodyError`. `mutate` only closes the transaction facade and does not catch the error. The custody error leaves `finally` and replaces the pending `raise`, leaving the original exception only on `__context__`. `_on_pipeline_done` then logs `SessionDerivedCustodyError` as the top-level `exc_type`. For a SystemExit, the `isinstance(exc, (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit))` filter no longer suppresses the log. The comment at :4344-4345 describes the recheck as a gate, but the recheck raises, and the comment at :4341-4343 wrongly implies terminal status is already durable. Recovery is unharmed: the saga stays non-terminal and peers can still find the run. So low severity is right. The impact is a misleading operator diagnostic plus a stale comment.
verdicts.evidence:
- src/elspeth/web/execution/service.py:4203-4216: `status_update_exc_class = self._persist_failed_run_status(...)`. No exception is raised when the status write fails transiently.
- service.py:4436-4455 (`_persist_failed_run_status`): `except (SQLAlchemyError, OSError) as status_err: return type(status_err).__name__`, so the row stays 'running'.
- service.py:4284-4288: the signal path logs `skipping_status_update_on_signal` and makes no status write.
- service.py:4305-4316: `if not run_already_terminal: self._persist_and_broadcast_run_event(...); terminal_event_persisted = True`. This runs whether or not the status is durable.
- coordination/repository.py:1877-1920 (`append_run_event`): no run-status precondition.
- service.py:4340-4355: `if outputs_finalized and terminal_event_persisted:` calls `mutate(..., tx.runs.mark_recovery_outputs_finalized(run_id=run_uuid))`.
- coordination/repository.py:1725-1740: the UPDATE has `WHERE status IN SESSION_TERMINAL_RUN_STATUS_VALUES`, and `if result.rowcount != 1: raise SessionDerivedCustodyError`.
- coordination/repository.py:290-294: `SessionDerivedCustodyError(RuntimeError)` with the message 'session-scoped derived record is unavailable'.
- coordination/repository.py:5254-5283 (`mutate`): the only handling is `try/finally transaction._close()`, with no catch.
- service.py:4757-4763 (`_on_pipeline_done`): logs `type(exc).__name__` from the Future, and the SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt filter is on the top-level class.
- `git diff 7c986dc97 74c0ce0db` shows this settlement block and the `terminal_event_persisted` assignment as + lines from 6e377bdc4, so the finding is diff-anchored.

findings.title: Profile-only azure_ai_search nodes always fail Stage 1 with false guarantees: [(none)]
findings.summary: d3dba8a9b makes every web-authored azure_ai_search node carry only profile+index. Composer Stage 1 builds the plugin from those authored options; only the llm plugin gets an inert probe stub (_validation_probe.py:66). Construction fails, and because azure_ai_search is passes_through_input=True (ai_search.py:88), _effective_producer_vote reports that the node guarantees no fields, so every downstream required-fields consumer is rejected and the planner cannot repair it.
findings.failure_scenario: csv source (guaranteed_fields=[question]) -> azure_ai_search{profile: search-prod, index: docs, query_field: question, output_prefix: policy} -> llm{profile, required_input_fields: [question, policy__rag_context]}: state.validate() is_valid=False with schema_contract_violation 'Producer (azure_ai_search) guarantees: [(none)]'. The identical pipeline with a raw endpoint/api_key binding is_valid=True. This is the exact RAG shape the plugin's own composer_hints teach.
findings.evidence: Scratch run against the worktree (elspeth.__file__ in worktree, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, worktree status clean after): '== profile-bound search -> profiled llm is_valid: False / ERR schema_contract_violation ... Producer (azure_ai_search) guarantees: [(none)]. Missing fields: [policy__rag_context, question]' vs '== raw search (control) -> profiled llm is_valid: True'. A field_mapper consumer fails the same way. recent-code-hints.md:1590-1606 records the llm fix and requires proving provider independence before stubbing another profiled plugin; legacy issue tracker elspeth-bc527113e7 (P1, triage) tracks the roster but predates azure_ai_search becoming profiled.
findings.suggested_fix: In web/composer/_validation_probe.py, add an azure_ai_search arm that mirrors the llm arm: when 'profile' is present and none of AZURE_AI_SEARCH_PRIVATE_BINDING_OPTION_NAMES is present, drop 'profile' and set an inert endpoint (https://validation-probe.search.windows.net) and a placeholder api_key. The output contract depends only on output_prefix/schema (rag/core.py:174); the endpoint feeds only the limiter name and the searcher, which is built in on_start. Add a Stage-1 regression test and add the plugin to the elspeth-bc527113e7 roster.

verdicts.reason: The finding holds. I reproduced it at the pinned commit. A profile-only azure_ai_search node (profile plus index, no endpoint) cannot be built by the Stage 1 probe. Because the plugin is a known pass-through plugin, `_effective_producer_vote` returns (True, frozenset()) for it, so any downstream consumer that declares required fields is rejected with 'guarantees: [(none)]'. The identical pipeline with a raw endpoint/api_key binding passes. Nothing earlier guards this: Stage 1 runs on the authored state before lowering, and `prepare_validation_probe_options` stubs only plugin == "llm". The recorded ruling in recent-code-hints does not make this deliberate. It names this exact defect class for llm, and it says another operator-profiled plugin must first be proved provider-independent before it gets a stub. That is an unfinished obligation, not a decision to let azure_ai_search fail.
verdicts.evidence:
Code path at 74c0ce0db:
- `src/elspeth/web/composer/_validation_probe.py:66`: the stub arms only when `plugin == "llm" and "profile" in prepared`. azure_ai_search options pass through unchanged, still carrying `profile` and no `endpoint`.
- `src/elspeth/plugins/transforms/azure/ai_search.py:43`: `endpoint: str = Field(...)` is required, so construction raises ValueError('Invalid configuration for transform ...').
- `ai_search.py:88`: `passes_through_input = True`, so the plugin is in `_known_pass_through_plugins()`.
- `src/elspeth/web/composer/state.py:2101`: `ValidationProbeCache._construct` builds the plugin from `prepare_validation_probe_options(holder.options, plugin=plugin)`.
- `state.py:4987-5054`: `_effective_producer_vote_uncached` catches the config-probe exception and, because `is_known_pass_through` is true, returns `True, frozenset()`.
- `src/elspeth/web/plugin_policy/profiles.py:1515`: `_AzureSearchProfileResolver` is registered whenever `azure_search_profiles` is set.
- `profiles.py:1316`: lowering refuses authored private options, so every web-authored node has this profile-only shape.

Reproduction: in-memory python heredoc against the worktree, run with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPATH set to the worktree src. `elspeth.__file__` resolved inside the worktree, no files were written, and `git status` was clean afterwards. The pipeline was a csv source (guaranteed_fields=[question]) -> azure_ai_search{profile, index, query_field: question, output_prefix: policy, schema observed} -> field_mapper{required_input_fields: [question, policy__rag_context]} -> csv output. Output:
- profile-bound search: `is_valid False`, with `ERR schema_contract_violation ... Producer (azure_ai_search) guarantees: [(none)]. Missing fields: [policy__rag_context, question]` and the warning `Computed contract probe for node 'search' failed during preview (ValueError)`.
- raw endpoint/api_key control: `is_valid True`.

The ruling at `docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md:1591-1609` records the llm fix (5d48f67c0). For any further operator-profiled plugin it requires proving provider independence before adding a stub (roster tracked in elspeth-bc527113e7). It does not exempt azure_ai_search.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this. I reproduced the defect myself at the pinned worktree. There is no recorded ruling that makes the failure intended: recent-code-hints.md:1590-1606 only says to prove the output contract is provider-independent before adding a stub for another profiled plugin. It does not say to leave profiled plugins unstubbed, and nothing downstream repairs the vote. On the web every azure_ai_search node is profile-only, because the plugin declares WebConfigAuthority.OPERATOR_PROFILED and lowering refuses authored private options. So the raw-endpoint control that validates is not a shape a web author can produce. Every web RAG pipeline that feeds a required-fields consumer is falsely rejected. The downstream llm will almost always be one, because llm/base.py:611 makes omitting required_input_fields an error when the template reads row fields, and a RAG prompt reads {prefix}__rag_context. One part of the claim is overstated: "the planner cannot repair it" is not strictly true. The llm opt-out `required_input_fields: []` (base.py:606-609) would get past the check, but only by accepting runtime risk. Even so, this blocks the plugin's own taught pairing (composer_hints: "pair it with an llm transform that reads {output_prefix}__rag_context"), so high severity stands.
verdicts.evidence:
- **Stub is llm-only.** _validation_probe.py:67 adds the inert binding only when `plugin == "llm"`. For azure_ai_search, prepare_validation_probe_options returns the authored options unchanged: `{'profile':'search-prod','index':'docs','query_field':'question','output_prefix':'policy','schema':{...}}`.
- **Construction fails.** create_transform under plugin_preflight_mode raises `ValueError: endpoint: Field required / profile: Extra inputs are not permitted`, and `_is_config_probe_exception(e)` is True. `endpoint` is a required field at ai_search.py:31.
- **The failure becomes zero guarantees.** ai_search.py:88 sets `passes_through_input = True`, so state.py:4985-5044 takes the known-pass-through fail-closed arm and returns `(True, frozenset())`.
- **Stage 1 reproduction.** Script run with PYTHONPATH=worktree/src and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1; the worktree was clean afterwards. The pipeline was csv (guaranteed_fields=[question]) -> azure_ai_search{profile, index, query_field=question, output_prefix=policy} -> field_mapper{required_input_fields=[question, policy__rag_context]}. It returned `is_valid=False` with `schema_contract_violation ... Producer (azure_ai_search) guarantees: [(none)]. Missing fields: [policy__rag_context, question]`. The same pipeline with endpoint and api_key returned `True []`.
- **Web can only author profile-only nodes.** ai_search.py:92 sets `web_config_authority = WebConfigAuthority.OPERATOR_PROFILED`. Commit d3dba8a9b says lowering refuses authored private options. profiles.py:1515 registers _AzureSearchProfileResolver whenever azure_search_profiles is configured.
- **No window fix.** In 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db, _validation_probe.py was touched only by 5bc4b56c9 (prompt editing), and recent-code-hints has no azure_ai_search ruling.
- **Why the llm consumer is affected.** llm/base.py:611 makes omitting required_input_fields an error when the template has row references, so the downstream llm declares them.

findings.title: Azure Search rejection prose still uses LLM provider/model/pacing repair wording
findings.summary: The window added an Azure arm to the lowering-error dispatch but did not route azure_ai_search away from the LLM-family prose in the unexpected-option branch (validation.py:490-500). The dispatch exists (comment at :38-40) so that non-LLM profiled plugins get repair language the planner can act on.
findings.failure_scenario: A planner authors {profile: search-prod, index: docs, endpoint: https://x.search.windows.net}. The finding reads "option(s) not authorable on a profile-bound node: ['endpoint']. The operator profile supplies provider/model/credential/pacing settings — remove them." The option is named, so repair still works, but the explanation describes an LLM provider binding rather than the search-service binding.
findings.evidence: validation.py:41-44 _STORAGE_PROFILED_COMPONENT_KINDS lists only aws_s3 and textract; validation.py:497-500 is the fallback wording; profiles.py:1515 adds azure_ai_search to the profiled roster in this window.
findings.suggested_fix: Add service-binding wording for PluginId('transform','azure_ai_search') (e.g. 'the operator profile supplies the Azure AI Search endpoint and authentication') in the unexpected and private_profile_option arms.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this finding. The path is reachable with the stated inputs. The Azure AI Search public profile schema leaves out every private binding option and sets additionalProperties False. So a node carrying {profile, index, endpoint} fails schema validation, and `endpoint` is reported as unexpected. azure_ai_search is not in _STORAGE_PROFILED_COMPONENT_KINDS, so the message falls through to the LLM-family wording "provider/model/credential/pacing settings". Nothing earlier in the path strips the option or rewrites the message. _normalized_profile_findings only changes error_code. No other module consumes AZURE_AI_SEARCH_PRIVATE_BINDING_OPTION_NAMES, so no earlier guard exists. The finding understates one point. The Azure lowering code does raise private_profile_option (profiles.py:1316-1317), but the schema check fires first (validation.py:476-509, `continue`), so that arm's wording (validation.py:529-539) is effectively unreachable for Azure Search. The live defect is the unexpected-option arm. Severity stays low. The message names the offending option and tells the planner to remove it, so the repair loop still converges. Only the explanation is wrong: it describes an LLM provider/model/pacing binding, not the search service's endpoint and authentication.
verdicts.evidence:
- validation.py:38-44 (pinned 74c0ce0db): the comment says profiled plugins whose binding is not LLM-family need their own repair wording. The map lists only source:aws_s3 and transform:aws_textract_document_analysis.
- validation.py:486-500: when there are unexpected names and the plugin is not in the storage map, the message reads "option(s) not authorable on a profile-bound node: {unexpected}. The operator profile supplies provider/model/credential/pacing settings — remove them."
- profiles.py:1223: author_names leaves out AZURE_AI_SEARCH_PRIVATE_BINDING_OPTION_NAMES (endpoint, api_key, use_managed_identity, client_id, api_version; contracts/azure_ai_search.py:5-13).
- profiles.py:1248-1253: the public schema has additionalProperties False, so an authored `endpoint` becomes a schema error and lands in `unexpected`.
- profiles.py:1515: transform:azure_ai_search is registered with _AzureSearchProfileResolver. It arrived in window commit d3dba8a9b, which also added the profile_index_not_admitted arm (validation.py:545-550) but did not add Azure Search to the wording map.
- validation.py:760-767: _normalized_profile_findings only rewrites error_code, never the message.
- profiles.py:1316-1317: lowering raises private_profile_option for Azure Search, but the schema check (validation.py:476-509) fails first, so the private_profile_option wording arm (validation.py:529-539) is effectively unreachable for this plugin.
- grep over src/ finds no other use of the private-name set and no alternate rejection wording for azure_ai_search.

findings.title: Azure example_use hard-codes an index the only profile's pin may reject
findings.summary: public_summary's new Azure arm teaches 'index: approved-documents' even when exactly one closed-pin profile is available, which is the case where public_schema turns index into a closed enum of that pin.
findings.failure_scenario: The only profile is 'hr' with indexes=('hr-policies',). The planner copies the example and the Draft202012 check rejects it with "option(s) failing the public profile schema: ['index']", costing a repair turn.
findings.evidence: profiles.py:1256-1260 sets index enum for a sole closed pin; profiles.py:1611-1621 example is fixed text; example_alias already derives from available_aliases.
findings.suggested_fix: When one profile is available and its pin is closed, use its first pinned index in example_use; otherwise keep the placeholder.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at 74c0ce0db. The Azure arm of public_summary derives the profile alias from available_aliases, but the index is the fixed literal 'approved-documents' (profiles.py:1611-1621, added in the window by d3dba8a9b). When exactly one profile is available and its pin is closed, public_schema turns index into a closed enum of that pin (profiles.py:1253-1257). validation.py:475-503 runs Draft202012Validator over the authored options and reports "option(s) failing the public profile schema: ['index']". The example does reach the planner: the planner discovery digest leaves example_use out (recent-code-hints 2026-08-26 and planner_authoring_aids.py:1746), but the list_transforms inventory response includes it (inventory_response_contracts.py:294, used by composer/tools/transforms.py). No recorded ruling covers this. The only nearby test checks the S3 example (test_profiles.py:986-993). Mitigations: the profile description and the schema enum both list the admitted indexes, so the planner has the correct answer in front of it. The cost is at most a repair turn, which keeps this at low severity. The problem is actually a little wider than reported: with several profiles, available_aliases[0] may itself be a closed pin that does not admit 'approved-documents'.
verdicts.evidence: profiles.py:1253-1257: `if len(available) == 1 and not isinstance(available[0].indexes, str) and "index" in safe_properties: index_choices = list(available[0].indexes); safe_properties["index"]["enum"] = index_choices`. profiles.py:1611-1621: `example_alias = available_aliases[0] if available_aliases else ...` followed by the fixed text `"    index: approved-documents\n"`. validation.py:475-503: Draft202012Validator(public_schema).iter_errors(public_options) produces `option(s) failing the public profile schema: {failing}`. inventory_response_contracts.py:294 puts `"example_use": value.example_use` into the transform inventory payload, which composer/tools/transforms.py imports. git log 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db shows the lines were added by d3dba8a9b (diff_anchored=true). docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md has no ruling on this.

findings.title: Saving a review-only outcome makes proposals staged in the same turn stale
findings.summary: The new persist condition `result.state.version != state.version or completion_gate_decision_changes(...)` writes a new composition_states row through save_composition_state when only the advisor outcome changed. Pending proposals bind to the previous row id (tool_batch.py:1647 base_state_id; the set_pipeline PresentBase.state_id), so a proposal staged in the same turn is stale as soon as the response lands.
findings.failure_scenario: The session uses manual approval and holds a non-empty graph G at row S1 with no prior gate fact. The composer stages approval-required proposal P (base S1) and ends with no tool call. The END gate flags G and returns AdvisorGateBlocked, so completion_gate_decision_changes(None, Blocked, G) is True and the route saves S2. The SPA's proposalBaseChanged (actionableProposals.ts:12-19) marks P obsolete. Accept returns 409 proposal_base_state_changed (proposals.py:367-381); for set_pipeline, BASE_CONFLICT (pipeline_commit.py:403-404) auto-rejects P. The same thing happens when a prior transient block flips to CLEAN, or CLEAN flips to transient. The user must ask ELSPETH to rebase a proposal it just produced.
findings.evidence: compose.py:591-593 elif predicate; compose.py:675-682 save_composition_state (comment at 677-679 still says 'after the LLM composer returns a newer state version'); service.py:6672 END gate runs on any non-empty state, skipping only on a prior graph_rejected fact for the same graph; service.py:6980-6982 AdvisorGatePassed; tool_batch.py:1647 base_state_id=current_state_id; pipeline_settlement.py:304-331 rejects on BASE_CONFLICT; test_advisor_recovery_routes.py has 0 'proposal' hits. The sibling defect is at messages.py:845-872. Before the window an unchanged-version freeform turn never saved a row (the guided-transition arm at compose.py:686-711 is the only earlier exception).
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the review-only snapshot when the turn left a pending proposal based on pre_send_state_id (e.g. last_mutation_was_pending_proposal) and let the next row carry the fact, or rebase pending proposals whose composition_content_hash is unchanged onto the new row in the same save. Add a route test that stages a proposal in a turn whose advisor outcome flips, then accepts it.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this. I traced the path at 74c0ce0db and it is reachable with no guard in the way. When a proposal is staged, the turn's version does not change: tool_batch.py returns `updated_state=state`. The END gate has no check for pending proposals. It runs on any non-empty state and skips only when the stored fact is a graph_rejected for the same graph (service.py:6746-6760). The window's new `elif` in compose.py:591-593 then saves a new composition_states row with save_composition_state. Nothing in append_state (coordination/repository.py:829-900) moves pending proposals onto that new row. Accepting the proposal then compares its stored base state id against the current row id, so the proposal is stale. The recorded ruling in recent-code-hints ("Both routes save changed review outcomes in a new fenced snapshot even when the graph is unchanged") approves the save itself. Neither that ruling nor the plan docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md mentions proposals (grep finds 0 hits), so the side effect was not decided on purpose. One detail to tighten: with no prior fact, an AdvisorGatePassed result does NOT cause a save. resolve_completion_gate_facts gives CompletionGateFacts(None), which equals the default previous value (completion_gates.py:238-248). Only three triggers cause a save: blocked with no prior fact, a transient block that turns CLEAN, and a CLEAN result that turns into a block. The reviewer's scenario uses Blocked and is correct.
verdicts.evidence: compose.py:591-593 saves a new row when `result.state.version != state.version or completion_gate_decision_changes(...)`. compose.py:675-682 calls save_composition_state, and its comment still says "after the LLM composer returns a newer state version". compose.py:130 and :207 pass pre_send_state_id to compose as current_state_id. tool_batch.py:1593-1600 builds the set_pipeline PresentBase from current_state_id. tool_batch.py:1647 sets `base_state_id=UUID(current_state_id)`, and tool_batch.py:1658 returns `updated_state=state`, so the version is unchanged. service.py:6746 returns fall_through only for an empty state or an exhausted pass budget, and service.py:6752 skips only through advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph. _try_terminate_no_tools (service.py:6085-6300) never checks last_mutation_was_pending_proposal; that check is used only in no_tool_finalize.py:172. completion_gates.py:238-248 treats None followed by Blocked as a change, and None followed by Passed as no change. coordination/repository.py:829-900 append_state only inserts the row and does not rebase proposals. proposals.py:367-381 returns 409 proposal_base_state_changed when `current_record.id != proposal.base_state_id`. pipeline_commit.py:403-404 raises BASE_CONFLICT when the state id differs, even if the content hash is the same, and pipeline_settlement.py:307/330 maps that to 409. Frontend actionableProposals.ts:12-19 marks a non-pipeline proposal obsolete when base_state_id differs from the current state id. The ruling text in recent-code-hints approves the advisor-only save but says nothing about pending proposals, and the plan doc has no proposal or base_state guidance.

findings.title: Server-route opt-out rows hashed and stored with actor 'composer-llm'
findings.summary: 889913b1a widened the V2 hash domain to null LLM provenance for surfaces no LLM raised. The review_disabled opt-out branch still hashes actor='composer-llm' (pending_interpretation.py:2089), and the repository writes the same actor (repository.py:1256) beside surface_origin state_revert, yaml_import or e2e_seed. The row falsely attributes auto-acceptance to the composer LLM.
findings.failure_scenario: A session has 'stop asking' enabled and the user imports a YAML pipeline with an unresolved interpretation site. The yaml_import surfacing (state.py:955) reaches plan()'s review_disabled branch (:2071) and writes a terminal OPTED_OUT/AUTO_INTERPRETED_OPT_OUT row: surface_origin=yaml_import, null model fields, actor='composer-llm', and an arguments_hash binding actor='composer-llm'. The audit then says the composer LLM accepted a draft that came from an imported file.
findings.evidence: pending_interpretation.py:2071-2094 opt-out branch with the hardcoded actor; coordination/repository.py:1256 actor='composer-llm' and :1266 surface_origin=command.surface_origin.value; models.py:1569-1581 opt-out CHECK admits a non-null surface_origin; surface_pending_interpretation_reviews_for_state has no review_disabled short-circuit. The actor literals predate the window; the nullable-provenance widening at :94-98, with its CHECK changes, is what makes these rows writable (they returned 500 before, per the commit message).
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the opt-out actor from surface_origin (e.g. 'composer-llm' only for COMPOSER_LLM, 'system:<origin>' otherwise) in both plan() and the repository insert. Otherwise, pin the intended sentinel in a test.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this. I traced the path at 74c0ce0db and every server route can reach the opt-out branch. The YAML import (state.py:953-971) and the E2E seed (state.py:1132-1146) build their drafts with surface_origin YAML_IMPORT or E2E_SEED and all four LLM provenance fields set to None. They persist through save_composition_state_with_interpretations (sessions/service.py:10001). That method runs each draft through the same repository create_or_reconcile_pending, then _SessionPendingInterpretationPlanner.plan (repository.py:1118). State revert (state.py:143-156) goes through surface_pending_interpretation_reviews_for_state and then create_pending_interpretation_event. None of these callers checks review_disabled. The repository reads it straight from the sessions row (repository.py:1090-1094), so a session that has opted out and then imports YAML into the same session, via POST /{session_id}/state/yaml on an existing session, reaches plan()'s opt-out branch (pending_interpretation.py:2071-2094). That branch hashes actor='composer-llm' alongside null provenance. The repository's OPTED_OUT arm (repository.py:1182-1210) never checks surface_origin. It inserts actor='composer-llm' with surface_origin=command.surface_origin.value (repository.py:1256, 1266), and ck_interpretation_events_opt_out_shape (models.py:1569-1581) only requires a non-null surface_origin. The result is a terminal OPTED_OUT row with surface_origin=yaml_import, null model fields and actor 'composer-llm'. That contradicts the documented meaning of the sentinel (sessions/service.py:8599-8601: "the row was created by the composer LLM, not a user"). It is the same kind of false provenance that 889913b1a set out to remove. Pending rows have their actor overwritten at resolution, but opt-out rows are born resolved, and the immutability trigger freezes the actor, so the wrong actor is permanent and bound into arguments_hash. I found no recorded ruling covering this. Severity stays low for three reasons. The same row's surface_origin column records the true origin, so a careful auditor can see the contradiction. The actor literal predates the window. And triggering it takes an opted-out session plus a server-route surfacing. One more point beyond the finding: the automatically created session-level opt-out marker (repository.py:1228) and superseded pending rows from server routes also keep actor='composer-llm'.
verdicts.evidence: pending_interpretation.py:2071-2094 (review_disabled branch; actor="composer-llm" hardcoded at :2089; model_* taken from the command, None for server routes); pending_interpretation.py:94-98 (window widening to str|None); coordination/repository.py:1090-1111 (review_disabled read from the sessions row), :1118 (plan call), :1182-1210 (OPTED_OUT validation, no surface_origin check), :1256 actor="composer-llm", :1266 surface_origin=command.surface_origin.value; routes/composer/state.py:837-848 (import onto an existing session_id), :953-971 (YAML_IMPORT drafts with None provenance, then save_composition_state_with_interpretations), :1132-1146 (E2E_SEED), :143-156 (STATE_REVERT through surface_pending_interpretation_reviews_for_state); composer/service.py:2161-2240 (surfacer, no review_disabled short-circuit); sessions/service.py:8599-8603 (the sentinel is documented as 'created by the composer LLM', overwritten at resolution, which never happens for rows born OPTED_OUT); models.py:1569-1581 (opt-out shape CHECK accepts any non-null surface_origin); git log 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db contains 889913b1a, whose message says these routes returned HTTP 500 before it

findings.title: Docstring claims ModifyResponseException handling matches _explain_run_diagnostics
findings.summary: The window swapped GuardrailInterventionNormalStringError (absent from litellm 1.102.0) for ModifyResponseException and kept the claim that this matches `_explain_run_diagnostics`. No such method exists; ComposerServiceImpl.explain_run_diagnostics catches only APIError, BudgetExceededError, BlockedPiiEntityError and GuardrailRaisedException.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer who trusts the docstring assumes guardrail ModifyResponseException is absorbed on the run-diagnostics path too. It is not: a guardrail intervention there escapes the except clause, while the guided step-chat path absorbs it.
findings.evidence: _guided_step_chat.py:1023-1028 docstring; composer/service.py:3946 explain_run_diagnostics, except clause at :3984-3990; the installed litellm 1.102.0 has no GuardrailInterventionNormalStringError; ModifyResponseException MRO is (Exception, BaseException).
findings.suggested_fix: Drop or correct the 'matching _explain_run_diagnostics' clause. Make no further investment in the guided lane.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at the pinned commit 74c0ce0db. The docstring at src/elspeth/web/sessions/_guided_step_chat.py:1023-1028 says the absorbed set, now including ModifyResponseException, "mirrors the project canonical in composer/service.py" and matches "_explain_run_diagnostics". Neither claim holds. No `_explain_run_diagnostics` exists anywhere in src/: the only hits are this docstring line, protocol.py:1642 and the public `explain_run_diagnostics` at service.py:3946. That method's except clause at service.py:3984-3990 catches only LiteLLMAPIError, BudgetExceededError, BlockedPiiEntityError and GuardrailRaisedException. ModifyResponseException's MRO is (Exception, BaseException, object), so none of those four catches it. In service.py, neither ModifyResponseException nor GuardrailInterventionNormalStringError appears at the pinned commit or at 7c986dc97. The "matching" claim was therefore already false before the window. Commit 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db edited this exact docstring line (GuardrailInterventionNormalStringError -> ModifyResponseException) and kept the false clause, so the finding is correctly diff-anchored. The impact is documentation only, in a guided file that is being retired, so the severity stays low.
verdicts.evidence:
- The window diff (git diff 7c986dc97 74c0ce0db) changes _guided_step_chat.py:1026 from "``GuardrailInterventionNormalStringError`` (direct ``Exception``" to "``ModifyResponseException`` (direct ``Exception``". Line 1028 ("absorbed, matching ``_explain_run_diagnostics``") is unchanged.
- `grep _explain_run_diagnostics src/` returns only _guided_step_chat.py:1028.
- service.py:3984-3990 reads `except (LiteLLMAPIError, BudgetExceededError, BlockedPiiEntityError, GuardrailRaisedException) as exc:`.
- `grep ModifyResponseException|GuardrailInterventionNormalStringError` over src/ at the pinned commit hits only _guided_step_chat.py:77, :87 and :1026. The same grep on service.py at 7c986dc97 finds nothing.

findings.title: Server-route interpretation surfaces still record actor='composer-llm'
findings.summary: 889913b1a added surface_origin so that server routes (state_revert, yaml_import, e2e_seed) stop claiming LLM provenance. The surfaced-row insert still hardcodes actor="composer-llm" for every origin, so the row contradicts itself.
findings.failure_scenario: A session has opted out of interpretation review. The operator imports YAML, and surface_pending_interpretation_reviews_for_state(surface_origin=YAML_IMPORT) reaches the opt-out branch (pending_interpretation.py:2071+, not gated by origin). The row is inserted born-resolved as auto_interpreted_opt_out with surface_origin='yaml_import', NULL provenance and actor='composer-llm'. resolve_pending_event never runs on it, so the durable audit row permanently attributes the auto-interpretation to the composer LLM. Pending rows that are later superseded keep the false actor as well.
findings.evidence: repository.py:1256 `actor="composer-llm"` (blame 3d4a8ee76d) sits next to `surface_origin=command.surface_origin.value` at :1267. The supersession updates (repository.py:1138, dead_site_supersession.py:135) do not touch actor. schemas.py:1010-1012 documents actor as originator:role:id or system:{component}.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive actor from command.surface_origin (e.g. system:yaml_import / system:state_revert / system:e2e_seed), or carry the actor on SessionPendingInterpretationCommand. Optionally add a CHECK tying actor to origin.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds at 74c0ce0db. The path is reachable and nothing guards it. The surfacing insert in `create_or_reconcile_pending` always writes `actor="composer-llm"`, whatever `surface_origin` says. It also hashes that same actor into the V2 `arguments_hash` on the opt-out branch. Server routes reach this writer directly. YAML import and the E2E seed get there through `save_composition_state_with_interpretations`, which calls `_RepositoryInterpretationMutations.create_or_reconcile_pending`. State revert gets there through `surface_pending_interpretation_reviews_for_state`, which leads to `create_pending_interpretation_event`. The opt-out decision in `pending_interpretation.py` checks only `snapshot.review_disabled` and never looks at the origin. The YAML import route has no guard against sessions that have opted out. The table's CHECKs accept an opt-out row with `surface_origin='yaml_import'` and no LLM provenance. So a YAML import into an opted-out session writes a row that is born resolved, has `surface_origin='yaml_import'` and names 'composer-llm' as actor. That actor is also bound into the row's `arguments_hash`.

I lowered the severity to low for three reasons. (1) The defect is older than the window. Line 1256 blames to 3d4a8ee76d, which is an ancestor of 7c986dc97, and 889913b1a fixed the four provenance columns but left actor alone, so this is a half-fix, not a regression. (2) The same row carries the truthful `surface_origin`, so an auditor can recover the real origin and no evidence is lost. (3) 'composer-llm' was already a sentinel that does not follow the documented `system:{component}` format, and it is written even for LLM-origin opt-out rows the system resolved on its own. It is an inconsistent label, not a hidden fact.

Two stale statements go with it. The docstring at `service.py:8599-8601` still says the row "was created by the composer LLM", which is false for these origins. And because actor is part of the hash domain, fixing it would change the hashes that server-route opt-out rows certify.
verdicts.evidence:
- `src/elspeth/web/coordination/repository.py:1243-1268` inserts `actor="composer-llm"` (line 1256) next to `surface_origin=command.surface_origin.value` (line 1267). The opt-out marker insert at `repository.py:1228` also writes 'composer-llm'.
- In `repository.py` the only uses of `surface_origin` are at lines 1007, 1239, 1267, 1394 and 1453, so the actor never depends on the origin.
- `src/elspeth/web/sessions/pending_interpretation.py:2071` returns PENDING only when `not snapshot.review_disabled`. Otherwise the opt-out branch builds the hash domain with `actor="composer-llm"` (line 2089). `surface_origin` appears nowhere in `pending_interpretation.py`, so the branch is never gated by origin.
- `src/elspeth/web/sessions/routes/composer/state.py:953-972` (YAML import) builds drafts with `surface_origin=YAML_IMPORT` and passes them to `save_composition_state_with_interpretations`.
- `src/elspeth/web/sessions/service.py:10001-10090` runs `interpretation_mutations.create_or_reconcile_pending(...)`.
- `import_state_yaml` / `seed_state_from_runtime_yaml` (`state.py:840-925`) have no guard on `review_disabled`.
- The CHECK `ck_interpretation_events_opt_out_shape` (`models.py:1569-1581`) allows a non-null non-LLM `surface_origin` with NULL provenance on an `auto_interpreted_opt_out` row.
- The service docstring at `service.py:8599-8604` says the "composer-llm" sentinel means "created by the composer LLM" and is overwritten only when the row is resolved.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 3d4a8ee76d 7c986dc97` succeeds, so the hardcoded actor predates the window.
- The 889913b1a commit message does not mention actor, and I found no ruling in `docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md`, so this is an oversight rather than a recorded decision.

findings.title: SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH is 65 but the history block ends at 64
findings.summary: 539121b17 changed only the literal. The epoch history in models.py has no entry for 65; its rationale (the required advisor_signoff.note key) was recorded only in sessions/schema.py.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator diagnosing why an epoch-64 store is refused reads the models.py history. The last entry they see is the 64 guided failure-code cut, and they misattribute the refusal to it.
findings.evidence: models.py:356-358: '# 64: guided operation failures distinguish ...' directly above 'SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65'. The only change 539121b17 made to models.py is 64->65.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a '# 65:' entry naming completion_gates.advisor_signoff.note (elspeth-032ec69c41) and the pre-1.0 delete/recreate policy.

verdicts.reason: The fact is right: models.py has no '# 65:' entry. The claimed failure does not lead to any wrong outcome, and the comment is incomplete rather than false. (1) When an epoch-64 store is refused, the error message tells the operator what to do. schema.py:327-333 raises "Session DB schema version 64 does not match SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH=65 ... Delete the session DB file and restart." The fix is the same whichever epoch caused the mismatch, so misreading the cause changes nothing the operator does. (2) The reason for epoch 65 is written down in two places an operator or developer would look. The first is next to the coupled constant the startup check compares against (schema.py:37-40). The second is the operator runbook that 539121b17 updated: docs/runbooks/staging-session-db-recreation.md now says "Session epoch 65 makes completion_gates.advisor_signoff.note a required key...", and its current-cutover heading says epoch 65. (3) The models.py history block has never been a complete list. It already skips a numbered 56 entry: models.py:333 is an unnumbered "# Coupled cut: ..." line followed by "# 57 →". The block is also written in at least two formats ('#   55 ->' and '# 60:'), so an operator cannot read 'last entry = current epoch' from it. The only concrete issue left is a documentation-completeness nit at 539121b17's own hunk. Adding the '# 65:' line would be tidy but fixes no defect that affects anyone.
verdicts.evidence: models.py:356-358 at 74c0ce0db has '# 64: guided operation failures distinguish ...' directly above 'SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65'; `git show 539121b17 -- models.py` shows that only the literal changed from 64 to 65. schema.py:37-40: '# Epoch 65 adds the required ``completion_gates.advisor_signoff.note`` key (elspeth-032ec69c41) ... _COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH = 65'. schema.py:327-333 contains the refusal message, which prescribes delete-and-restart and does not ask for a diagnosis. docs/runbooks/staging-session-db-recreation.md (539121b17 hunk @@ -48): '+Session epoch 65 makes `completion_gates.advisor_signoff.note` a required key ...', and its heading reads '(session epoch 65 and Landscape epoch 43)'. models.py:333 has the unnumbered '# Coupled cut: sparse proposal display ...' line, and grep finds no numbered 56 entry, which is an earlier gap in the history.

findings.title: cost_unavailable copy blames pricing config for malformed provider cost metadata
findings.summary: COST_UNAVAILABLE is raised whenever provider_cost is None. That includes malformed usage.cost, missing token counts, impossible subtotals and unknown service_tier. The user-facing detail nonetheless says to configure or correct model pricing, and the epoch-64 comment claims a distinction from malformed provider content that the code does not make.
findings.failure_scenario: The provider returns usage.cost=-1, or omits usage.prompt_tokens. The planner raises COST_UNAVAILABLE and the user sees 503 'Ask an administrator to configure or correct model pricing'. The admin finds pricing correct and gets no pointer to the provider response.
findings.evidence: pipeline_planner.py:4063-4066 raises COST_UNAVAILABLE with 'cost metadata is missing or malformed'. core/llm_pricing.py provider_cost_from_captured_usage / calculate_missing_provider_cost return None for malformed or incomplete provider metadata. The models.py:356-357 comment says the code distinguishes cost accounting from malformed provider content.
findings.suggested_fix: Word the detail to cover both causes (missing pricing, or unusable provider cost/usage metadata), or route the malformed-metadata cases to invalid_provider_response. Align the epoch-64 comment with whichever you choose.

verdicts.reason: The path is reachable. A usage.cost of -1 goes through validated_provider_cost and comes back None. A response with no usage.cost and no prompt_tokens goes through calculate_missing_provider_cost and also comes back None. In both cases COST_UNAVAILABLE is raised and the user sees the "configure or correct model pricing" message. Three parts of the finding still fail. (1) The code does not contradict the epoch-64 comment. It contrasts "cost accounting" with "malformed provider content", and content here means the proposal and tool payload. The cost check deliberately runs after the call and before any parsing. A missing completion_tokens count, or anything malformed in the content, goes to MALFORMED_RESPONSE, which becomes invalid_provider_response. The reviewer read "content" as if it meant "cost metadata". (2) Commit 101824e7d chose on purpose to send malformed cost metadata to cost_unavailable, and it wrote that choice down. Its runbook says: "Explicit null, boolean, string, negative, non-finite, or overflowing costs remain unavailable. An unsupported requested model or failed pricing calculation also remains unavailable." Its CHANGELOG says the aim is to point administrators at the cost setup rather than ask users to retry. (3) The claim that the admin "gets no pointer to the provider response" is false. The same commit added a runbook section for cost_unavailable. It tells the admin to check provider_cost_source (public, private, calculated or unavailable), model_requested against model_returned, and whether prompt_tokens and completion_tokens were reported. Those fields separate a pricing problem from a provider metadata problem. What is left is a minor wording gap in the admin guidance, for provider behaviour that is rare in practice, such as a negative cost. That is not a concrete defect.
verdicts.evidence:
- The mapping exists as the finding describes, and the freeform mirror has identical text. See src/elspeth/web/sessions/routes/guided_operations.py:93-96 and routes/_helpers.py:2894-2897.
- pipeline_planner.py:4063-4066 raises COST_UNAVAILABLE when call.provider_cost is None. Lines 4067+ send a missing completion_tokens count to MALFORMED_RESPONSE. All of this happens before parsing, as the "post-call and pre-parse" comment at 4061-4062 says.
- core/llm_pricing.py:77-78 and 527-541: a negative, bool, or non-finite usage.cost gives None. llm_pricing.py:424-434: a missing prompt_tokens or completion_tokens count, an impossible subtotal, or an unknown service_tier also gives None. llm_response_parsing.py:545/573 feeds this value into call.provider_cost.
- models.py:356-357: "64: guided operation failures distinguish unavailable cost accounting from malformed provider content". This is accurate, because cost failures and content failures take different codes.
- Commit 101824e7d, docs/runbooks/azure-llm-composer-troubleshooting.md, section "Composer cost admission". It says explicit null, boolean, string, negative, non-finite, or overflowing costs "remain unavailable", then lists the diagnostics for "If cost admission still fails": provider_cost_source, model_requested/model_returned, and prompt_tokens/completion_tokens. The CHANGELOG hunk in the same commit states the design goal: "missing model pricing directs administrators to repair pricing instead of asking users to retry an invalid provider response."

findings.title: cost_unavailable missing from the permanent/transient split; clients offer Retry, and each retry is another provider call that cannot be priced
findings.summary: The GuidedOperationFailureCode comment (protocol.py:184-190) says the vocabulary carries a PERMANENT-vs-TRANSIENT split that clients read to decide whether to retry. cost_unavailable was added at :195 with no classification. The server treats it as needing an administrator, like admission_refused ('Ask an administrator to configure or correct model pricing before trying again', 503). The frontend retry gates exclude only policy_blocked and admission_refused.
findings.failure_scenario: The deployment's planner model has no pricing, so the provider's cost metadata comes back None. The user sends a message and gets a 503 'ask an administrator', but MessageBubble still shows Retry. pipeline_planner.py:4060-4066 raises COST_UNAVAILABLE after the provider call returns, so each click makes another billed provider call that cannot be priced. It fails the same way every time until pricing is repaired, and nothing limits the number of clicks.
findings.evidence: protocol.py:184-195. frontend/src/components/chat/MessageBubble.tsx:284 and frontend/src/stores/sessionStore.ts:3838-3839 both suppress retry only for policy_blocked/admission_refused. sessionStore.ts:2325-2359 copies apiErr.failure_code onto local_failure_code. routes/_helpers.py:2894-2897, guided_operations.py:93-96 and guided_plan.py:142-149 carry the admin-action copy. pipeline_planner.py:4060-4066 has the comment 'Cost enforcement is intentionally post-call and pre-parse'.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark cost_unavailable as permanent in the protocol comment. Add it to the retry-suppression predicates in MessageBubble.tsx:284 and sessionStore.ts:3839 alongside admission_refused. Consider exporting a single permanent-code set that both gates use.

verdicts.reason:
The path is reachable at 74c0ce0db, and I found nothing earlier that guards against it.
