When the planner has no pricing, `provider_cost` comes back None after the provider call returns, and the planner raises COST_UNAVAILABLE. The freeform route maps that to failure_code "cost_unavailable" and returns a 503 whose text says to ask an administrator. The body also carries `failure_code`. The store copies it onto the failed message, and MessageBubble still shows Retry because it hides the button only for policy_blocked and admission_refused. Nothing in the frontend checks cost_unavailable, the planner_code COST_UNAVAILABLE or service_setup_failed to hide Retry. Each click is another recorded provider call that fails the same way while pricing is still missing.

I am lowering the severity to low for three reasons:
1. It is not a regression in when Retry appears. Before 101824e7d, COST_UNAVAILABLE was grouped under invalid_provider_response, and that text said "Retry the request." The window corrected the text but did not update the retry checks.
2. The protocol comment's permanent-vs-transient list was never complete. quota_exceeded, integrity_error, custody_error and admission_refused are not classified in it either, so the missing entry in the comment is weak evidence of a half-wired change. The real mismatch is between the frontend retry checks and the server's text.
3. Every retry needs a manual click, and a user can resend the same text anyway. Removing the button fixes a contradictory UI but does not cap spending.

What remains is a real half-wired change: a new enum value that the server treats as needing an administrator, while the client still offers Retry.
verdicts.evidence:
- **Pinned code path:** pipeline_planner.py:4062-4066 checks cost after the call has returned (`recorder.record_llm_call(call)`, then it raises COST_UNAVAILABLE). _helpers.py:2983-2984 maps COST_UNAVAILABLE to "cost_unavailable". _helpers.py:2894-2897 returns 503 with "Ask an administrator to configure or correct model pricing before trying again." _helpers.py:3019-3024 and 3051 put `failure_code` in the response body.
- **Frontend:** sessionStore.ts:2325-2359 copies apiErr.failure_code onto `local_failure_code`. MessageBubble.tsx:284 renders Retry unless the code is policy_blocked or admission_refused. sessionStore.ts:3838-3839 uses the same two-code check for guided.
- **Search result:** grep of frontend/src (tests excluded) finds cost_unavailable only in guidedDecoder.ts:2313 and types/guided.ts:183, with no retry suppression anywhere.
- **Before the window:** in 101824e7d, COST_UNAVAILABLE was removed from `_FREEFORM_PLANNER_INVALID_PROVIDER_CODES`. Before that change it went out as invalid_provider_response with "Retry the request.", so Retry was already offered.
- **Comment coverage:** the protocol.py:184-190 comment classifies only 5 codes; quota_exceeded, integrity_error, custody_error and admission_refused are also unclassified there.
- **Recorded rulings:** docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md has no ruling on cost or pricing retries.

findings.title: Pending-interpretation DTOs accept a composer_skill_hash the DB digest CHECK rejects
findings.summary: SessionPendingInterpretationCommand (protocol.py:1558) checks only that composer_skill_hash is an exact string, and blank is allowed. PreparedInterpretationEventDraft (protocol.py:2270-2279) checks only that it is non-empty. validate_surface_provenance checks only None/not-None. Only the DB CHECK ck_interpretation_events_composer_skill_hash_format (models.py:1621) enforces the lower-sha256 shape, and no pre-INSERT code checks it.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes surface_origin=COMPOSER_LLM, or relies on the protocol default at protocol.py:4382, with a non-digest hash such as '' or a route label. The command constructs, the planner binds the value into the v2 arguments_hash, and the INSERT raises IntegrityError, which surfaces as an unclassified HTTP 500 instead of an AuditIntegrityError at construction. 889913b1a's message records this exact path turning three routes into 500s. The commit removed the label producers but left the DTO checking less than the table. This is latent: current producers pass a real digest or None.
findings.evidence: protocol.py:1558 and :2270-2279. contracts/composer_interpretation.py:169-201. models.py:1621 (_lower_sha256_constraints on interpretation_events.composer_skill_hash). grep for is_lower_sha256_hex near skill_hash in src/ returns no hits.
findings.suggested_fix: When composer_skill_hash is not None, require is_lower_sha256_hex in both DTOs, raising AuditIntegrityError, so the Python writer checks the same shape as the DB CHECK.

verdicts.reason: The code is described correctly, but no path reaches the failure it claims. A non-digest composer_skill_hash could reach the DTOs only if a producer supplied one, and I checked every producer at 74c0ce0db. Each passes one of three things: a hashlib.sha256(...).hexdigest(), a value read back from a DB column that has the same lower-sha256 CHECK, or None for the server routes. No Tier-3 or request input can set the field. The finding itself says the defect is latent. The protocol default of COMPOSER_LLM cannot introduce a bad hash either: with any provenance field set to None, validate_surface_provenance raises AuditIntegrityError. That leaves a future-producer hypothetical. It is a mismatch between Tier-1 owned data and the DTO checks, and the DB CHECK already fails closed on it. The doctrine for a Tier-1 anomaly is to crash, and the IntegrityError does crash, so no user-visible regression, audit gap or trust-boundary crossing exists. At most this is a hardening nit: the DTO checks less than the table does.
verdicts.evidence:
- The DTO checks match the description. At protocol.py:1558, composer_skill_hash only has to be an exact str and is not in nonblank_text_fields. At protocol.py:2270-2279 it only has to be non-empty. validate_surface_provenance (contracts/composer_interpretation.py:169-201) checks only None versus not-None. The shape CHECK is at models.py:1621.
- Producers, all traced:
  - composer/service.py:2502: `self._composer_skill_hash: str = hashlib.sha256(self._composer_skill_text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()`. This feeds service.py:2984, :3082 and :8025, and tool_batch.py:1242, :1344, :1541, :1653 and :2327 (ctx.service._composer_skill_hash). Through tools/sessions.py:3136 it reaches create_pending_interpretation_event.
  - pipeline_planner.py:3654: `skill_hash = hashlib.sha256(rendered_skill.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()`, passed on at :3711.
  - sessions/routes/composer/proposals.py:472: proposal.composer_skill_hash, read from composition_proposals. That column has its own lower-sha256 CHECK, ck_composition_proposals_composer_skill_hash_format (models.py:996).
  - sessions/service.py:674, :7734, :11881, :12570: proposal.skill_hash. :10036 and :11575: draft.composer_skill_hash, which comes from those same sources.
  - coordination/repository.py:1232 and :1387: None, for the server routes.
- The labels the finding cites from 889913b1a ('state_revert' and the others) were removed in that commit, which added surface_origin. Server routes now pass None, and validate_surface_provenance rejects any non-None value for them.
- protocol.py:4382 default: COMPOSER_LLM with a missing field raises AuditIntegrityError at construction (composer_interpretation.py:192-195). This is the fail-closed behaviour the docstring states.
- The only reachable IntegrityError would need a future caller to invent a hash. That is a Tier-1 programming error, and crashing on it is the doctrinal response.

findings.title: Completion-gate envelope format changed at epoch 65 without an epoch bump
findings.summary: 41aeaeac0 made completion_gates.schema_version==2 and advisor_signoff.cause required in the strict Tier-1 parser, but neither SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH nor _COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH moved past 65. That epoch was already stamped by 539121b17-era code, which wrote `{}` (clean) or a no-cause blocked fact on every compose save. The schema.py comment still says epoch 65 is only about the note key.
findings.failure_scenario: A session DB stamped at epoch 65 by code from 539121b17 up to 41aeaeac0 (the operator deployed one at 2026-09-22 23:28 AEST) is upgraded to 74c0ce0db. Startup accepts it because user_version==65 and the column shape is unchanged. Any session with a prior compose turn has completion_gates={} on its head row, so parse_completion_gates raises ValueError: compose.py:135 and messages.py:216 return HTTP 500, execute raises CompletionGateIntegrityError, /validate, audit readiness and shareable reviews raise, and the recovery handlers' _durable_completion_gates raises inside a try that catches only SQLAlchemyError. The session is unusable.
findings.evidence: git log 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db -G'^SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = |^_COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH = ' lists only 101824e7d (63->64) and 539121b17 (64->65). 539121b17 is an ancestor of 41aeaeac0, and 41aeaeac0^:models.py already has SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65. At 5bcd983c9, completion_gates.py writes `return {}` with no schema_version or cause. At HEAD, completion_gates.py:274-276 raises when schema_version is absent and :310-312 raises when cause is absent. schema.py:327 admits user_version == SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH. The hints entry says 'no old-format compatibility is provided' but does not mention the epoch.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH and _COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH together to 66 and name the envelope-v2 change in both comments. Move the full pin set (tests/unit/web/sessions, tests/unit/docs, tests/unit/architecture, tests/unit/website, README, CHANGELOG cutoff line, runbooks, website/get-started.html). Deployed epoch-65 stores must be recreated.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this. I traced the path at 74c0ce0db and confirmed it. 41aeaeac0 changed the completion_gates JSON format: `schema_version == 2` is now required, and `advisor_signoff.cause` is required on a blocked fact. The session epoch was not bumped. Code that stamped stores at epoch 65 (539121b17 through 5bcd983c9, i.e. 41aeaeac0^) wrote `{}` for a clean turn and a blocked fact with no cause. HEAD's startup sentinel still accepts user_version 65, so it opens those stores. The strict parser then raises on the old rows. The call sites that raise are not guarded: compose.py:135 is deliberately outside every try. The project has already bumped the epoch for exactly this kind of JSON-format change: epoch 62 (the suggestion key) and epoch 65 (the note key). The schema.py comment for epoch 65 gives the same reasoning that applies here. The hints entry says 'no old-format compatibility is provided'. That ruling means no dual-read. It does not waive the epoch bump, which is the mechanism that turns 'no compatibility' into a startup rejection instead of 500s at session load. I could not verify the claimed 23:28 AEST deployment. The defect does not depend on it: any store stamped at epoch 65 by 539121b17..41aeaeac0^ code reaches the failure.
verdicts.evidence:
- `git log 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db -G'^SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = |^_COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH = '` lists only 539121b17 and 101824e7d. HEAD has models.py:358 `SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65` and schema.py:40 `_COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH = 65`. 41aeaeac0^:models.py:358 is already 65, and 539121b17 is an ancestor of 41aeaeac0.
- At 41aeaeac0^, _helpers.py:2772-2781 writes `COMPLETION_GATES_META_KEY: completion_gates_meta_value(...)` on every adjudicating compose save. That function returns `{}` on a clean turn and a blocked dict without `cause` (diff hunk removing `completion_gates_meta_value`).
- At HEAD, completion_gates.py `parse_completion_gates` does `version = raw["schema_version"] if "schema_version" in raw else None; if type(version) is not int or version != 2: raise ValueError(...)`, and raises when `cause` is absent. So `{}` now raises, although before 41aeaeac0 it meant 'not withheld'.
- schema.py `_assert_on` (around lines 325-332) rejects only `user_ver not in {0, SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH}`, so an epoch-65 store passes startup.
- These callers do not catch the error: compose.py:131-135 (comment: 'Parsed here, outside every try ... must propagate'), messages.py:216, execution/routes.py:1003, execution/service.py:1272/1800/2794, audit_readiness/service.py:564, shareable_reviews/service.py:434, and _helpers.py:998 (`_durable_completion_gates`), which the recovery handlers call at 3184/3342/3591.
- Precedent, models.py epoch history: '62: durable advisor completion gates require a nullable backend suggestion. Semantic-only JSON grammar cut: reject earlier stores at startup before an old blocked envelope can fail during session reload.' schema.py:36-39 says epoch 65 exists because 'the strict parser refuses an envelope without it, so rows written at epoch 64 cannot be read forward'. That is the same situation 41aeaeac0 created, without the bump.
- The 41aeaeac0 hints diff adds 'Gate envelopes require schema version 2 and a cause; no old-format compatibility is provided' and says nothing about the epoch or rejection at startup.

verdicts.reason: The defect is real, and I found no recorded ruling that excuses it. The project's own precedent says this kind of change needs an epoch bump. Commit 539121b17 moved the epoch from 64 to 65 for a smaller change of the same kind: one new required key (`advisor_signoff.note`) in this envelope. Its message gives the reason: "the Tier-1 parser refuses an envelope written without it, so an epoch-64 store cannot be read forward." 41aeaeac0 then added two required keys, `schema_version` (which must be 2) and `advisor_signoff.cause`, and did not bump the epoch. The hints entry says "Gate envelopes require schema version 2 and a cause; no old-format compatibility is provided". That rules out reading the old format. It does not rule out the epoch bump, which is the mechanism that makes "no compatibility" fail at startup instead of mid-request. The schema.py:36-40 comment still says epoch 65 is only about the note key, so it is now stale. There is a real store at risk: the local elspeth-web service started at 2026-09-22 23:28:43 AEST, and data/sessions.db was modified 4 seconds later. At that moment the first-parent head of release/0.8.1 was 5bcd983c9, which is epoch 65 with the old writer that persists `{}`. So the running deployment's store is stamped 65 by old-format code. Deploying 74c0ce0db over it passes the `user_ver in {0, SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH}` check at schema.py:327. Every session whose head row has `completion_gates={}` would then raise ValueError in each caller of `parse_completion_gates`. I lower the severity from high to medium for three reasons. First, 0.8.1 is unreleased, and the released upgrade path (0.8.0, epoch below 65) is still refused at startup, as the corrected CHANGELOG cutoff in 74c0ce0db says. Second, only intermediate dev or local builds between 539121b17 and 41aeaeac0 are exposed. Third, the failure is loud (errors and HTTP 500s, not silent corruption) and is fixed by recreating the store. Even so, the one deployment that does exist would lose every existing session with a compose turn, and startup gives the operator no warning.
verdicts.evidence:
- **Old writer (5bcd983c9):** `completion_gates_meta_value` returned `{}` on every clean or None-preflight compose save and a blocked dict with no `cause`. 41aeaeac0 removed it (see the 41aeaeac0 diff of src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py).
- **Strict parser at HEAD:** src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py, `parse_completion_gates` (def at :251), raises "Tier 1: completion_gates.schema_version must be 2" when `schema_version` is absent. It also raises when `cause` is not a str.
- **Epochs at HEAD:** `_COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH = 65` at src/elspeth/web/sessions/schema.py:40. The comment at :36-39 names only the note key. `SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH` is also still 65.
- **Startup check:** schema.py:327 admits `user_ver in {0, SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH}`.
- **No later bump:** first-parent log 41aeaeac0..74c0ce0db has only the merge 23185f55a and the docs commit 74c0ce0db. 74c0ce0db edits the CHANGELOG cutoff to "below epoch 65" and "not minimum versions", and moves no epoch.
- **Precedent:** the 539121b17 message says "the Tier-1 parser refuses an envelope written without it, so an epoch-64 store cannot be read forward. Pre-1.0 policy: the store is recreated, not migrated."
- **Uncaught callers of `parse_completion_gates` at HEAD:** sessions/routes/composer/compose.py:135, sessions/routes/messages.py:216, execution/service.py:1272/1800/2794, execution/routes.py:1003, audit_readiness/service.py:564, shareable_reviews/service.py:434, sessions/routes/_helpers.py:998/2760.
- **Live deployment:** `systemctl show elspeth-web` gives ExecMainStartTimestamp=Tue 2026-09-22 23:28:43 AEST. data/sessions.db mtime is 2026-09-22 23:28:47. Release head at that time was 5bcd983c9 (22:55:29); 41aeaeac0 is dated 2026-09-23 00:55:04.
- **Not checked:** I could not read the DB's user_version directly because the auto-mode classifier denied a read of the production DB.

findings.title: Recovery persist after a mid-turn tool write erases the durable advisor block fact
findings.summary: _durable_completion_gates carries forward the current head's gate envelope. After any mutating tool call the head is a compose-loop mid-turn row whose composer_meta has no completion_gates key (service.py:2736-2740, stored verbatim by _insert_composition_state). The carry-forward therefore yields {'schema_version': 2}, which means 'no gates withheld', and the recovery save persists it. This contradicts the window's new invariant comment at _helpers.py:2758-2759 and the helper's own docstring.
findings.failure_scenario: The head row R0 holds a blocked advisor_signoff fact. The next compose turn makes a mutating tool call (mid-turn row R1 without the key), then hits ComposerConvergenceError, a plugin crash or a runtime-preflight failure. _handle_convergence_error (or a sibling handler) writes R2 with completion_gates={'schema_version':2}, and /validate stops withholding completion_ready for a graph no advisor reviewed. On a generic 502 with no recovery persist, R1 stays the head with the same effect. The old code lost the fact the same way, so this is not a regression.
findings.evidence: composer/service.py:2736 composer_meta={'validation_lane':'authoring_only', ...}; sessions/service.py:6569-6581 inserts composer_meta verbatim; get_current_state orders by version desc; completion_gates.py:269-270 returns None for a missing key, and completion_gates_meta_from_facts(None) returns {'schema_version': 2}; _helpers.py:3184/3342/3591 pass that value as prior_completion_gates.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the turn-start completion_gates value into each authoring_only mid-turn row. Alternatively, have the recovery handlers use the turn-start state record the route already holds rather than re-reading the moving head.

verdicts.reason: I traced the path at 74c0ce0db and could not refute it. Mid-turn tool-call rows are committed to the database during the turn (one `persist_compose_turn` call per LLM round). Their `composer_meta` is built fresh and never includes `completion_gates`. The recovery handlers then look up the durable fact by re-reading the current head, which is now that mid-turn row, instead of the state the turn started from. `parse_completion_gates` returns None for the missing key, so the recovery row is saved with `{'schema_version': 2}`, which means "no gates withheld". That breaks the carry-forward promised in the helper's own docstring and in the ruling that "a green runtime preflight alone cannot clear it". The normal turn-end path is not affected: messages.py:216 and compose.py:135 parse the turn-start record. Only the recovery helper re-reads the moving head. The fact is not re-derived anywhere, so the loss is permanent until a later turn gets a new advisor verdict. `completion_ready` is enforced beyond display: shareable_reviews/service.py:455 and audit_readiness/service.py:646 both check it. Medium severity stands. The helper dates from 2026-08-02 (5166baab22), so this is not a regression in the window, and `diff_anchored=false` is correct.
verdicts.evidence:
- composer/service.py:2736-2740 builds the mid-turn `composer_meta` from scratch as `{'validation_lane':'authoring_only', ingress?, chat_ingress_inputs?}`. It has no `completion_gates` key and never goes through `merge_composer_meta_updates`.
- composer/turn_audit.py:256-260 attaches that payload to every tool outcome where `post_version > pre_version`. turn_audit.py:273 then calls `persist_compose_turn_async`, once per LLM round, so the row is committed before any later convergence, crash or preflight failure.
- sessions/service.py:6812-6832 inserts each payload through `_insert_composition_state`. At line 6581 that writes `composer_meta=_enveloped_state_column(state.composer_meta)` verbatim, with no merge from the prior row. `current_state_id` advances to the new row.
- routes/_helpers.py:981-998: `_durable_completion_gates` reads `service.get_current_state(session_id)`, which is the moving head (now the mid-turn row). It returns `completion_gates_meta_from_facts(parse_completion_gates(meta))`.
- execution/completion_gates.py:269-270: a missing key returns None. Lines 197-198: None serializes to `{'schema_version': 2}`.
- routes/_helpers.py:3184 (convergence), 3342 and 3591 (sibling recovery handlers) pass that value as `prior_completion_gates`. At 2760-2763 it is used in place of `composer_meta`. With `decision=None`, `resolve_completion_gate_facts` (completion_gates.py:222-223) keeps "no fact", and the result is persisted.
- execution/completion_gates.py:339-340: `merge_completion_gates` returns the recompute unchanged when there is no fact, so `completion_ready` is no longer withheld. The pending wording at lines 56-59 exists precisely so a carried fact keeps withholding on a graph the advisor never reviewed. The erasure removes that.
- Consumers that enforce `completion_ready`: shareable_reviews/service.py:455 and audit_readiness/service.py:646.
- The normal path is correct by contrast: sessions/routes/messages.py:216 and composer/compose.py:135 parse the turn-start `state_record`, not the head.
- No recorded ruling exempts mid-turn rows. docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md (2026-09-22 entry) says a green runtime preflight "cannot clear" the fact, and only `advisor_gate_decision` may replace it.
- Test gap: tests/unit/web/sessions/test_completion_gate_roundtrip.py:214-238 tests `_durable_completion_gates` only with the blocked row itself as the head. No test puts a mid-turn row on top first.
- Git blame puts `_durable_completion_gates` at 5166baab22 (2026-08-02), before the window.

findings.title: COST_UNAVAILABLE progress mapping not consumed by the recompose route
findings.summary: 101824e7d added COST_UNAVAILABLE->service_setup_failed and a 503 'ask an administrator' mapping, and wired send_message to use them. The recompose PipelinePlannerError arm (compose.py:429-437) still hardcodes reason='provider_unavailable' and 'Retry the request'. The comment above _FREEFORM_PLANNER_PROGRESS_REASONS ('only codes whose ACTOR is the planner') no longer describes this entry, whose actor is deployment pricing configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: Pricing for the composer model is missing and the user retries via recompose. The progress stream says the composer model returned an unusable plan and invites a retry, blaming the provider. At the same time the HTTP 503 body says retrying won't help until an admin fixes pricing. Telemetry attributes the failure to provider_unavailable.
findings.evidence: messages.py:655-672 branches on COST_UNAVAILABLE and calls freeform_planner_progress_reason(exc.code). compose.py:429-437 publishes reason='provider_unavailable' with fixed retry copy; git log -L shows that block last changed 2026-08-03.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the recompose arm mirror messages.py:655-672 using freeform_planner_progress_reason(exc.code) and the COST_UNAVAILABLE evidence/likely_next copy, and amend the map's comment.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at 74c0ce0db. 101824e7d changed four places: it added COST_UNAVAILABLE->"service_setup_failed" to the progress map (_helpers.py:2954), added the cost_unavailable 503 "Ask an administrator..." HTTP entry (_helpers.py:2894-2897), added the failure-code branch (_helpers.py:2983-2984), and added COST_UNAVAILABLE-specific evidence and likely_next copy in send_message (messages.py:655-672). The recompose PipelinePlannerError arm (composer/compose.py:421-445) was left out of that commit. It still publishes reason="provider_unavailable" with the evidence "The composer model did not return a usable pipeline plan." and "Retry the request...". That arm's own comment (compose.py:423-426) says it must translate the error "identically or the two routes drift on failure UX". The path is reachable. Recompose (compose.py:86-90) calls composer.compose (line 202), which goes through service._plan_and_stage_empty_pipeline (service.py:4099). There the planner raises PipelinePlannerError(code="COST_UNAVAILABLE") whenever provider_cost is None (pipeline_planner.py:4063-4066). No guard catches it before the recompose arm. The same arm then calls the shared _handle_planner_failure, so the HTTP body is 503 cost_unavailable with the admin copy while the progress event blames the provider and invites a retry. One refinement: the durable disposition row and the HTTP failure_code both correctly say cost_unavailable. Only the progress-event reason says provider_unavailable, so the finding's claim that telemetry attributes the failure to provider_unavailable is true of the progress reason only. The drift also covers other codes: the recompose arm never adopted freeform_planner_progress_reason for any code, and that part predates the window. The window made it worse by adding a code whose correct handling is 'do not retry'. The comment on the map ('only codes whose ACTOR is the planner') is mildly stale for a pricing-configuration fault. The effect is limited to wrong progress-stream copy and reason on one route. The HTTP response is correct, so low severity stands.
verdicts.evidence: src/elspeth/web/sessions/routes/composer/compose.py:421-437: `except PipelinePlannerError as exc:` ... `evidence=("The composer model did not return a usable pipeline plan.",), likely_next="Retry the request; if it keeps failing, simplify it or check the composer provider.", reason="provider_unavailable"`. The following _handle_planner_failure call (compose.py:438-445) returns 503 with "Ask an administrator to configure or correct model pricing" (_helpers.py:2894-2897, 2983-2984, 3019-3020). messages.py:655-672 branches on exc.code == "COST_UNAVAILABLE" and uses reason=freeform_planner_progress_reason(exc.code). Neither is done in compose.py. `git show 101824e7d --stat` shows compose.py was not in that commit. Raise site: pipeline_planner.py:4066. Reachability: compose.py:202 composer.compose -> service.py:4099 _plan_and_stage_empty_pipeline.

findings.title: Guided accept provenance refusal fires after the accept settlement is durable
findings.summary: The new check that the planner provenance is complete sits after service.accept_guided_pipeline_proposal has committed. It reads authority.row, which was fetched long before the accept (4970/5003) and does not change across it. The check could therefore run before any durable write, but it fails closed only after the side effects.
findings.failure_scenario: A proposal row with NULL composer provenance (corrupt, legacy or imported row) is wire-confirmed. The accept commits the new state and completes the operation. The guard then raises AuditIntegrityError, so no interpretation_events are surfaced: no Accept card renders and /execute fails with UnresolvedInterpretationPlaceholderError. The generic handler at 5767 then calls fail_guided_operation_with_audit on an operation that has already completed, which can escalate to 'Guided RESPOND could not record its terminal failure' (5826).
findings.evidence: guided.py:5168-5194 is the accept settlement and guided.py:5215-5225 is the new guard. The comment at 5198-5211 says skipping the surfacing pass after the durable settlement 'would orphan the session in exactly the failure this pass exists to prevent'. The same guard in the RESPOND replay arm (3115-3121) is a post-hoc repair, so there it is correctly post-commit. Reachability is theoretical: the models.py:433-444 all-or-none CHECK and the asserts at service.py:11878-11886 and 12567-12575 guarantee provenance on guided rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the four-field None check, with the same AuditIntegrityError, to before the accept_guided_pipeline_proposal call, for example beside the validate_state preflight at 5140. Keep the planner_row locals for the post-commit surfacing call.

verdicts.reason: The finding describes the placement correctly: the four-field None check at guided.py:5215-5225 does run after accept_guided_pipeline_proposal commits. But the failure scenario it describes cannot happen. A proposal row with NULL composer provenance cannot reach that settlement. The route loads authority.row at guided.py:4670 through service.get_authoritative_pipeline_proposal, which calls get_authoritative_composition_proposal. That calls _classify_authoritative_composition_proposal, which calls _restore_authoritative_pipeline_proposal (service.py:3104). That function already raises AuditIntegrityError("pipeline proposal composer provenance is incomplete") when any of the five provenance fields is None (service.py:2350-2357). So a corrupt, legacy or imported row fails at 4670, before admit_guided_pipeline_confirmation, record_guided_pipeline_dispatch and accept_guided_pipeline_proposal write anything durable. Inside the accept transaction, service.py:13547 restores the authority again and would reject the row a second time before commit. The post-commit check therefore works only as type narrowing for the Optional fields on CompositionProposalRecord. It never fires after the durable write, and the chain of no Accept card, UnresolvedInterpretationPlaceholderError and "could not record its terminal failure" never starts. Moving the check earlier would only duplicate the pre-commit refusal at service.py:2350. The only fair criticism left is cosmetic: the comment and check suggest a live post-commit failure mode that the earlier restore already rules out.
verdicts.evidence: guided.py:4670-4674 `authority = await service.get_authoritative_pipeline_proposal(...)`. service.py:7785-7800 get_authoritative_pipeline_proposal calls get_authoritative_composition_proposal, which calls _classify_authoritative_composition_proposal, which calls _restore_authoritative_pipeline_proposal at service.py:3104. service.py:2350-2357: `if None in {row.composer_model_identifier, row.composer_model_version, row.composer_provider, row.composer_skill_hash, row.tool_arguments_hash}: raise AuditIntegrityError("pipeline proposal composer provenance is incomplete")`. accept_guided_pipeline_proposal restores the authority again inside its write transaction before commit (service.py:13547). The post-commit guard at guided.py:5215-5225 therefore sees only rows whose provenance has already been checked to be complete. It was added by 889913b1a to replace the stand-in labels "guided-planner" and "unknown"; the stand-ins were unreachable for the same reason.

findings.title: /validate repair surfacer stamps composer_llm provenance on surfaces owed by a server route (state revert)
findings.summary: 889913b1a introduced InterpretationSurfaceOrigin so rows record what raised a surface, and moved state revert, YAML import and E2E seed to server origins with NULL LLM provenance. It tagged ComposerServiceImpl.surface_pending_interpretation_reviews unconditionally as COMPOSER_LLM, using the current deployment's self._model (as both identifier and version), provider-or-'unknown' and skill hash. That method is the /validate backstop (execution/routes.py:969, :991), which calls no LLM and repairs surfacing debt on any state, whichever route created it. The revert route surfaces after its commit (state.py:791), and state.py:690-698 documents that an attempt can die in between.
findings.failure_scenario: The user reverts to state S. revert_state_for_guided_operation commits the reverted state R, which has pending interpretation_requirements, and terminalizes the operation. The surfacing call at state.py:791 then fails (transient DB error on the repair lease, worker restart or cancellation), and the route returns 5xx. The user reloads, and the SPA calls POST /validate?state_id=R. execution/routes.py:991 reaches service.py:3073, which inserts the missing events with surface_origin='composer_llm', model_identifier=model_version=<current composer_model>, provider=<current provider or 'unknown'> and composer_skill_hash=<current skill hash>. The audit trail then claims that the composer LLM, under the current skill, raised the revert's review surfaces, although no LLM ran. If the guided replay repair (_repair_reverted_surfacing_debt, state.py:689-716) had run first, the same sites would carry state_revert and NULL provenance, so the recorded provenance depends on which repair ran first. The user later resolves the user_approved rows, which carries the false origin into the hashed resolved row.
findings.evidence: service.py:3073-3084 at the pin: `surface_origin=InterpretationSurfaceOrigin.COMPOSER_LLM, model_identifier=self._model, model_version=self._model, provider=self._availability.provider or "unknown", composer_skill_hash=self._composer_skill_hash`. git blame shows line 3078 is 889913b1af (in the window). execution/routes.py:944-954 says 'both arms run the backend surfacer in repair mode over the state they are about to validate'. state.py:148-153 shows that the revert's own surfacing uses STATE_REVERT with None provenance. state.py:690-698 documents the post-commit gap in which surfacing dies. The InterpretationSurfaceOrigin docstring (composer_interpretation.py:96) scopes COMPOSER_LLM to the compose loop, its repair pass or a guided commit.
findings.suggested_fix: Stop hard-coding the origin in the backstop. Either add a closed-enum origin for the /validate repair (for example VALIDATE_REPAIR with NULL provenance: contract, the ck_interpretation_events_surface_origin CHECK, the frontend type and an epoch bump), or derive the origin from the validated state's recorded provenance and pass COMPOSER_LLM only for compose-produced states. Add a regression test in which the revert's post-commit surfacing fails, then /validate runs, and assert that the resulting rows are not composer_llm.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this. The path is reachable at the pin as described. At service.py:3078 (blamed to 889913b1a, in the window), ComposerServiceImpl.surface_pending_interpretation_reviews always passes surface_origin=COMPOSER_LLM, the current deployment's self._model, provider-or-'unknown' and the skill hash. It never looks at which route produced the state. Both arms of /validate (execution/routes.py:969 and :991) call this method with only_missing_evidence=True for any state, and nothing checks the state's origin first.

The revert route is the one server route whose surfacing is not atomic. YAML import builds its events inside the save transaction with prepare_pending_interpretation_event_drafts_for_state(YAML_IMPORT) at state.py:953-960. Revert commits R in revert_state_for_guided_operation (state.py:767-775), leaves the lease guard, and only then calls _surface_reverted_interpretation_reviews (state.py:790-794). That function takes a fresh COMPOSE lease (state.py:135-141), which is its own point of failure. The route's own docstring (state.py:690-698) records that an attempt can die in that gap.

Evidence is keyed per composition_state_id (_surfaced_evidence_keys(current_state_id=...), service.py:2195-2200). R is a new state id, so all of its surfaceable sites count as missing. If the SPA validates R before anyone retries the revert, the backstop writes those sites as composer_llm with the current model's provenance. If the revert is replayed first, the same sites get STATE_REVERT with NULL provenance (state.py:689-716). So the recorded provenance depends on which repair runs first.

The enum docstring (composer_interpretation.py:96-98) says COMPOSER_LLM means 'the compose loop, its repair pass, or a guided commit', and that revert debt is STATE_REVERT. The backstop therefore contradicts the contract the same commit introduced. I found no recorded ruling in recent-code-hints about the /validate backstop's origin.

I lowered the severity because stamping the model name on this path is not new. Before the window, lines 3079-3082 (f3db92c006) already stamped self._model on backstop repairs of revert debt, while the revert route stamped 'state_revert' labels. The window added an explicit origin column and left this one caller unconverted, so the change is half-wired and not a regression. The trigger is also narrow: the revert's post-commit surfacing has to fail, and then /validate has to run before the revert is retried.
verdicts.evidence: service.py:3073-3084 (origin hard-coded to COMPOSER_LLM, self._model used as both identifier and version, provider-or-'unknown'); service.py:2192-2201 (repair evidence keyed on current_state_id, so a new reverted state id has no evidence); service.py:2350-2366 (writes carry the passed origin and provenance); execution/routes.py:944-954, 966-973, 988-996 (the /validate backstop covers any state, with no origin check); sessions/routes/composer/state.py:767-775 (revert commit), 790-794 (surfacing after the commit), 135-156 (separate COMPOSE lease acquire, STATE_REVERT with NULL provenance), 689-716 (replay repair uses STATE_REVERT), 690-698 (docstring admits death between commit and surfacing); state.py:953-960 (YAML import is atomic via prepared drafts, so revert is the only non-atomic server route); contracts/composer_interpretation.py:96-98 (COMPOSER_LLM scoped to compose, compose repair and guided commits; STATE_REVERT covers revert debt); git blame at 74c0ce0db: line 3078 comes from 889913b1af, lines 3079-3082 from f3db92c006 (2026-07-22, so the model stamping predates the window).

findings.title: Envelope format changed without an epoch bump: old epoch-65 rows 500 every send/recompose at the new Tier-1 parse
findings.summary: 41aeaeac0 made parse_completion_gates require schema_version==2 and a cause, and rejects the `{}` envelope that the previous writer stored on every compose save. SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH stayed 65, so the startup epoch gate accepts stores holding old-format rows. The parse added at messages.py:216 (and compose.py:135) runs before any write and outside every try, so every compose request on such a session raises an unhandled ValueError.
findings.failure_scenario: A session DB is stamped epoch 65 by a binary between 539121b17 and 41aeaeac0^, and a session's head composition_states row has composer_meta.completion_gates == {} from a compose save. After upgrading to 74c0ce0db the startup check passes, but POST /messages raises ValueError('Tier 1: completion_gates.schema_version must be 2') at messages.py:216 and returns a bare 500 with no slog, progress event or failure_code. The same happens on /recompose, /validate, execute, audit readiness and shareable reviews. The session can never compose a new row to recover.
findings.evidence: At 41aeaeac0^, completion_gates_meta_value returned {} for clean saves and {advisor_signoff:{status,detail,suggestion,for_graph,note}} without cause or schema_version. At HEAD, completion_gates.py:212-214 raises on any envelope that lacks schema_version 2. `git show 41aeaeac0^:.../models.py` and `git show 74c0ce0db:.../models.py` both have SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65, and 539121b17 (the epoch-65 bump for the required note key) is an ancestor of 41aeaeac0^. No exception_handler(ValueError) exists under src/elspeth/web. The plan at docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md:17/111 rules out compatibility and a DB reset, which is probably why the epoch bump was skipped. The report argues the ruling should have used the epoch gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH to 66 with the usual coupled literal sites, or explicitly record that epoch-65 stores written before 41aeaeac0 are unsupported and must be recreated.

verdicts.reason: I confirmed the defect at 74c0ce0db. The recorded ruling does not cover it. The ruling (plan docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md:17 and :111; recent-code-hints.md:38) forbids backwards compatibility and says old-format envelopes must fail validation. It says nothing against an epoch bump. The project's pre-1.0 way to enforce "no compatibility, recreate the store" is the epoch gate. Commit 539121b17 shows this: it bumped the epoch 64 to 65 for the same envelope, one commit family earlier, because "the Tier-1 parser refuses an envelope written without it, so an epoch-64 store cannot be read forward". Commit 41aeaeac0 makes the same kind of change and leaves the epoch at 65. Old stores are therefore not refused cleanly at startup. They fail on every request instead. I lowered the severity from high to medium for three reasons. Only stores stamped epoch 65 by code in a roughly 10-hour window are exposed: 539121b17 landed 2026-09-22 14:38 and 41aeaeac0 landed 2026-09-23 00:55. The code sits on a pre-release, local, unpushed release branch. A user can escape by starting a new session.
verdicts.evidence:
1. The route parse runs before any write and outside every try. messages.py:216 runs `prior_completion_gates_facts = parse_completion_gates(state_record.composer_meta) if state_record is not None else None`, and compose.py:135 has the same call. The comment at those lines says the parse sits outside every `try` on purpose, so any ValueError it raises propagates to the caller.
2. The new parser rejects the old envelopes. At completion_gates.py:274-276 the parser reads `version = raw["schema_version"] if "schema_version" in raw else None` and raises `ValueError("Tier 1: completion_gates.schema_version must be 2")` when the version is missing or not 2. That rejects both `{}` and the old envelope without a cause.
3. The old writer produced exactly those envelopes. At 41aeaeac0^, completion_gates.py:186-203 (`completion_gates_meta_value`) returned `{}` when runtime_preflight was None or had no advisor blocker. Otherwise it returned `{"advisor_signoff": {...}}` with no schema_version and no cause. Its docstring says it "overwrites the key on every compose-preflight save", so nearly every composed session in such a store has a head row that the new parser rejects.
4. The epoch did not move. SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65 appears at models.py:358 at HEAD and at 41aeaeac0^. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 539121b17 41aeaeac0^` reports that 539121b17 is an ancestor.
5. The precedent is in this window. The message of 539121b17 reads: "completion_gates.advisor_signoff.note became a required key ... the Tier-1 parser refuses an envelope written without it, so an epoch-64 store cannot be read forward. Pre-1.0 policy: the store is recreated, not migrated." The shape change in 41aeaeac0 is the same kind of change, and it has no bump.
6. The failure reaches more than the two compose routes. Other callers of parse_completion_gates also raise on such rows: _helpers.py:998 and :2760, execution/service.py:1272, :1800 and :2794, execution/routes.py:1003, shareable_reviews/service.py:434, and audit_readiness/service.py:564.
7. The ruling text does not settle it. The plan's line 17 forbids a "database reset" and its line 111 forbids "migrations, compatibility branches or reset existing data as part of implementation". Neither forbids an epoch bump, which only makes the operator recreate the store at deploy. That matches the 539121b17 policy.
8. Why medium and not high: exposure is limited to epoch-65 stores written between 2026-09-22 14:38 (539121b17) and 2026-09-23 00:55 (41aeaeac0), on a local release branch. New sessions are unaffected. The fix is still what the finding proposes: bump to 66 with the coupled literal sites (_COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH and the pins), or explicitly record that pre-41aeaeac0 epoch-65 stores must be recreated.

verdicts.reason: I traced the defect myself at 74c0ce0db and could not refute it. Before 41aeaeac0, every compose save wrote the completion_gates key: `{}` for a clean turn, or an advisor_signoff dict with no schema_version or cause. At HEAD, parse_completion_gates raises on both shapes. SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH is still 65, so the startup check accepts epoch-65 stores that hold these rows. The recorded ruling ("no old-format compatibility") only covers rejecting old envelopes. It does not choose a runtime 500 over a refusal at startup. The project's own precedent is to bump the epoch for exactly this kind of cut: epoch 62 was bumped "to reject earlier stores at startup before an old blocked envelope can fail during session reload", and 539121b17 bumped to 65 because "the Tier-1 parser refuses an envelope written without it". An epoch bump is neither a migration nor a compatibility branch, so the plan's ban on those does not rule it out. I lowered the severity to medium because only stores stamped from commits between 539121b17 (09-22 14:38) and 41aeaeac0 (09-23 00:55) are affected, 0.8.1 is unreleased, and pre-1.0 policy already recreates stores. One detail in the finding is wrong: the parse call at messages.py:216 was already there at 41aeaeac0^. What 41aeaeac0 changed is the grammar the parser enforces.
verdicts.evidence:
- Old writer at 41aeaeac0^ (src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py:186-216): `completion_gates_meta_value` returns `{}` when preflight is None or unblocked. Otherwise it returns {"advisor_signoff": {status, detail, suggestion, for_graph, note}} with no schema_version and no cause.
- Old save path at 41aeaeac0^ (_helpers.py:~2772-2782): every compose save sets `COMPLETION_GATES_META_KEY: completion_gates_value` unconditionally.
- New parser at HEAD (completion_gates.py:266-275): if the key is present, a missing or wrong schema_version raises `ValueError("Tier 1: completion_gates.schema_version must be 2")`. That covers `{}`. Lines ~307-313 raise when cause is missing.
- Epoch unchanged: models.py:358 at HEAD has `SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65`. The schema.py:37-40 comment still says epoch 65 is the note-key cut.
- Precedent: models.py comment for epoch 62 reads "Semantic-only JSON grammar cut: reject earlier stores at startup before an old blocked envelope can fail during session reload." The message on 539121b17 gives the same rationale for 65.
- Call site: messages.py:216 at HEAD calls `parse_completion_gates(state_record.composer_meta)` outside every try, on purpose ("a corrupt envelope is Tier 1 and must propagate"). The only exception handlers in web/ cover SessionOperationFence*, AuditIntegrityError, CorruptPreferencesError and AuditStoryIntegrityError (app.py:1238-1329, session_operation_handlers.py:23-28). None covers ValueError, so the request fails with a bare 500.
- Ruling: recent-code-hints.md (41aeaeac0) says "Gate envelopes require schema version 2 and a cause; no old-format compatibility is provided." The plan (docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md, "Do not add migrations, compatibility branches or reset existing data") rules out migrations, compatibility branches and resetting data. Neither addresses the epoch gate.
- HEAD commit 74c0ce0db (CHANGELOG) says startup accepts "an existing database matching the exact current schema epoch (session 65)", but it does not mention that epoch-65 stores written before 41aeaeac0 now fail at request time. The operator guidance is therefore incomplete.

findings.title: Recompose planner-failure progress event lacks the COST_UNAVAILABLE branch added to send_message
findings.summary: 101824e7d gave the send_message route (messages.py:659-668) and the guided route COST_UNAVAILABLE-specific progress wording. The recompose mirror still reports 'model did not return a usable pipeline plan' / 'Retry...check the composer provider' with a hardcoded reason='provider_unavailable', despite its own comment that the two routes must translate PipelinePlannerError identically.
findings.failure_scenario: Model pricing is not configured. Send returns 503 cost_unavailable with the correct advice to ask an administrator. The user clicks Retry and /recompose hits COST_UNAVAILABLE again. The progress snapshot now blames the provider and says to retry, though retrying cannot fix a pricing-configuration error. The HTTP 503 body is still correct because _handle_planner_failure is shared.
findings.evidence: compose.py:423-425 comment: 'must translate PipelinePlannerError identically or the two routes drift on failure UX'. compose.py:434-436 is unchanged (blame 251879d05). messages.py:661/666 has the conditional wording and uses freeform_planner_progress_reason, which maps COST_UNAVAILABLE to service_setup_failed (_helpers.py:2954).
findings.suggested_fix: Copy the COST_UNAVAILABLE conditional evidence/likely_next into compose.py and replace the hardcoded reason with freeform_planner_progress_reason(exc.code).

verdicts.reason: I confirmed the drift at 74c0ce0db. The recompose route calls the same `composer.compose` as send_message (compose.py:202). Its `except PipelinePlannerError` arm (compose.py:421-448) still publishes the generic progress event: evidence "The composer model did not return a usable pipeline plan.", likely_next "Retry the request; ... check the composer provider." and a hardcoded reason="provider_unavailable" (compose.py:434-436, blamed to 251879d059 on 2026-07-20). Commit 101824e7d, inside the window, added COST_UNAVAILABLE-specific wording only to messages.py:659-668 and the guided route. It also added the COST_UNAVAILABLE -> service_setup_failed entry to the `_FREEFORM_PLANNER_PROGRESS_REASONS` table (_helpers.py:2954), but only messages.py:672 calls `freeform_planner_progress_reason`, so recompose never uses that mapping. COST_UNAVAILABLE is reachable: pipeline_planner.py:4066 raises it whenever the provider call carries no cost (call.provider_cost is None). I found no guard, normaliser or recorded ruling that excludes recompose. The comment at compose.py:423-425 says the two routes must translate this identically, and the progress event is where they now differ. I lowered the severity to low. The HTTP outcome is correct on both routes: `_handle_planner_failure` is shared and returns 503 cost_unavailable with the "ask an administrator to configure pricing" detail (_helpers.py:2908-2911, 2997-2998), and the durable disposition row carries the right code. Only the progress snapshot's evidence, likely_next and reason are wrong: they blame the provider and tell the user to retry. The hardcoded reason is older than the window; it is the same drift left behind when elspeth-ad5628ecda fixed the reason on the send path only. That older gap makes the drift wider, not a reason to dismiss the finding.
verdicts.evidence:
- compose.py:202 `result = await composer.compose(`: recompose calls the same compose path as send_message.
- compose.py:421-436: the `except PipelinePlannerError` arm uses fixed wording and `reason="provider_unavailable"`. git blame gives 251879d059 for lines 425-438, so this text is older than the window.
- messages.py:659-672 (in-window diff 101824e7d): the evidence and likely_next wording branches on `exc.code == "COST_UNAVAILABLE"`, and the reason comes from `freeform_planner_progress_reason(exc.code)`.
- _helpers.py:2953-2967: `_FREEFORM_PLANNER_PROGRESS_REASONS` maps `"COST_UNAVAILABLE": "service_setup_failed"`. The comment above it says the freeform raise site used to hardcode provider_unavailable (elspeth-ad5628ecda).
- grep for `freeform_planner_progress_reason` in src/ finds only its definition (_helpers.py:2963) and the call at messages.py:672. compose.py never calls it.
- pipeline_planner.py:4066 raises `PipelinePlannerError(..., code="COST_UNAVAILABLE")` when `call.provider_cost is None`, so the path can be reached.
- _helpers.py:2997-2998 plus `_FREEFORM_PLANNER_FAILURE_HTTP["cost_unavailable"]`: the shared `_handle_planner_failure` returns the correct 503 body on both routes, so only the progress snapshot drifts. That is why the severity drops to low.

findings.title: Server-route surfaces still recorded with actor='composer-llm', hash-sealed on opt-out rows
findings.summary: The window threads surface_origin (STATE_REVERT/YAML_IMPORT/E2E_SEED) through service.py into the one pending-interpretation writer, but that writer still writes actor="composer-llm" on every surfaced row (repository.py:1256), and the review-disabled auto-resolve arm hashes actor="composer-llm" into arguments_hash (pending_interpretation.py:2089). Neither depends on the origin. The docstring of _prepare_or_create_pending_interpretation_event (service.py:8599-8607) still says the row 'was created by the composer LLM', and :8580 names the compose-loop tool handler as the only caller. Both are now false for three of the four origins.
findings.failure_scenario: The session has opted out of review (interpretation_review_disabled=true). The user sends POST /api/sessions/{id}/state/yaml with an LLM node that has a prompt-template review site. The route builds YAML_IMPORT drafts with NULL provenance and calls save_composition_state_with_interpretations (service.py:10025-10043), and the planner takes the opt-out arm. The resulting row is born resolved and immutable: interpretation_source='auto_interpreted_opt_out', choice='opted_out', surface_origin='yaml_import', all four provenance columns NULL, actor='composer-llm', and arguments_hash covers actor='composer-llm'. The audit trail says the composer LLM auto-interpreted a draft no LLM saw in this request, which is the false attribution the commit set out to remove, moved into another column and sealed in the hash. test_routes.py:8717 exercises this exact path and does not assert actor. The state-revert repair reaches the same arm.
findings.evidence: repository.py:1256 `actor="composer-llm"` next to `surface_origin=command.surface_origin.value` (:1267). pending_interpretation.py:2089 `actor="composer-llm"` in the opt-out hash-domain call. routes/composer/state.py:953-970 (YAML_IMPORT, NULL provenance) and state.py:143-157 (STATE_REVERT) do not check review_disabled. service.py:8599 docstring: 'The ``actor`` column on the pending row is set to the sentinel "composer-llm" — the row was created by the composer LLM, not a user.' contracts/composer_interpretation.py:257-260 claims opt-out rows are populated 'because the LLM auto-interpreted'. There is no ruling in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md. Pending rows are unaffected long-term because resolve_interpretation_event overwrites actor.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the actor sentinel from surface_origin: keep 'composer-llm' only for COMPOSER_LLM and use an actor naming the server route (or the requesting principal) for the others. Pass the same value to both the insert (repository.py:1256) and the opt-out hash arm (pending_interpretation.py:2089) so the hash matches the column. Update the service.py:8580/8599 docstring and the contract docstring, and assert actor in the opt-out YAML-import test.

verdicts.reason: I traced the path and could not refute it. The YAML-import route builds YAML_IMPORT drafts with all four provenance fields NULL and passes them to save_composition_state_with_interpretations. That method prepares each draft through _prepare_or_create_pending_interpretation_event(_prepare_only=True) and runs it through the shared repository writer. When review_disabled is true, the planner takes the opt-out arm and hashes the literal actor="composer-llm". The repository then inserts actor="composer-llm" next to surface_origin=command.surface_origin.value. Nothing on the way checks review_disabled or origin to change the actor. The test test_post_state_yaml_opt_out_returns_the_final_durable_head drives this exact path: it expects no pending rows afterwards, so opt-out rows are born resolved. It never asserts actor. docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md has no ruling on the actor sentinel, and grep finds no 'composer-llm' or 'surface_origin' entry there. The service docstring at :8599-8602 and the contract docstring ('because the LLM auto-interpreted') are now false for server-route origins. I lowered the severity from medium to low for three reasons. (1) The actor literal was already there before the window; commit 889913b1a did not add it and only failed to finish the attribution clean-up. (2) The same row now carries surface_origin='yaml_import' or 'state_revert' with NULL provenance, so an auditor sees a self-contradictory row rather than a convincingly false one. (3) Pending rows get their actor overwritten when they are resolved. Only rows born resolved under opt-out keep the sentinel permanently, and it is sealed into arguments_hash.
verdicts.evidence:
Paths are relative to the pinned worktree at 74c0ce0db.
- src/elspeth/web/coordination/repository.py:1256 `actor="composer-llm"` sits in the same insert as :1267 `surface_origin=command.surface_origin.value`. The opt-out gate at :1183-1193 checks review_disabled, the hash shape and appended_state, but never looks at the origin or the actor. The session-level marker at :1228 is also `composer-llm`, and that one is shared by every origin.
- src/elspeth/web/sessions/pending_interpretation.py:2071-2094: once review_disabled is true, `_interpretation_hash_domain_v2(... actor="composer-llm" ...)` is called with no branch on surface_origin.
- src/elspeth/web/sessions/routes/composer/state.py:952-970 (YAML_IMPORT, provenance None) calls service.save_composition_state_with_interpretations. The state-revert repair at state.py:143-157 (STATE_REVERT, provenance None) calls surface_pending_interpretation_reviews_for_state.
- src/elspeth/web/sessions/service.py:10025-10045 runs each draft through _prepare_or_create_pending_interpretation_event(_prepare_only=True, surface_origin=draft.surface_origin). :10089-10091 then runs create_or_reconcile_pending, the same writer.
- service.py:8580 docstring: 'Called from the compose-loop tool handler'. :8599-8602: 'set to the sentinel "composer-llm" — the row was created by the composer LLM'. Both are false for the yaml_import, state_revert and e2e_seed origins.
- contracts/composer_interpretation.py:257-260 says opt-out rows are populated 'because the LLM auto-interpreted'.
- tests/unit/web/sessions/test_routes.py `test_post_state_yaml_opt_out_returns_the_final_durable_head` opts out, imports YAML with an LLM prompt_template, and asserts that pending == []. That only holds if the opt-out rows were written. It does not assert actor.
- Commit 889913b1a changed repository.py by only 6 lines, adding surface_origin; the actor literal is older than the window.
- models.py:1541-1580: the CHECKs constrain surface_origin and provenance but not actor.

findings.title: Logging out in one tab no longer logs out the other tabs
findings.summary: responseOwnsCredential logs out only when the request carried a Bearer token that equals both the store token and localStorage. authHeaders() reads the token from localStorage. So after another tab removes the token, this tab's requests go out with no header, get a 401, and never trigger logout.
findings.failure_scenario: Alice is signed in in tabs A and B. She logs out in tab A, which runs localStorage.removeItem('auth_token'). Tab B's store still holds token T1 and user alice. Its 30s mailbox poll, or any click, is sent with no Authorization header, and middleware.py:91-103 answers 401. authFetch recorded credential.token=null, so responseOwnsCredential is false and parseResponse skips logout(). Tab B keeps rendering alice's authenticated shell, with her sessions, composition and mailbox still on screen. Every request 401s indefinitely until a manual reload. Before the window, the check `token !== null` logged tab B out and cleared its caches.
findings.evidence: client.ts:251-255 now gates logout on responseOwnsCredential(response, store.token). authSession.ts:27-29 requires credential.token !== null and credential.token === localStorage.getItem('auth_token'). client.ts:98-108 authHeaders reads localStorage. No 'storage' listener exists for auth_token: grep finds only preferencesStore.ts:470 (the intro key) and useTheme.ts:127. The 8 cases in client.auth-races.test.ts are all same-tab; none changes localStorage independently of the store. The parseResponse docblock at client.ts:186-190 still promises 'any API call returning 401 triggers authStore.logout()'. The WebSocket path (executionStore.ts:814-817) still logs out unconditionally, so only a tab with a live run stream recovers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a window 'storage' listener on auth_token that calls logout() when newValue becomes null and re-runs loadFromStorage() when it changes. Alternatively, treat a 401 on a request that sent no credential or a different one, while this tab's store holds a token and the generation is current, as a lost login and log out. Add a regression test that clears localStorage without touching the store, and update the parseResponse docblock.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this finding and confirmed the failure path myself. Commit 7d981d6cf changed the 401 check. Before, the client logged out on any 401 while the store held a token. Now it logs out only when the request carried a Bearer token that matches both the store token and localStorage. A request sent after another tab has cleared localStorage carries no Authorization header, so its 401 never logs this tab out. Nothing else in the app picks up a logout made in another tab: no 'storage' listener watches auth_token, loadFromStorage runs only once on mount, and nothing reloads on focus or visibility change. Logout in tab A does not contact the server either. It only calls localStorage.removeItem, so tab B has no route back to a consistent state except a WebSocket 401 or a manual reload. The commit message and docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md record no ruling on cross-tab logout, so this is not a deliberate decision. Medium stays right: tab B leaks no data beyond what was already on its screen, but the tab is stuck showing a signed-in shell whose every request fails.
verdicts.evidence: authSession.ts:15-18 sets credential.token from the request's own Authorization header, or null when it has none. authSession.ts:25-29 returns false when credential.token is null and also requires it to equal localStorage.getItem('auth_token'). client.ts:98-108 (authHeaders/getToken) reads localStorage and leaves out the header when the token is missing. client.ts:251-255 calls logout() only if responseOwnsCredential(response, store.token) is true. At the base commit 7c986dc97, client.ts:257-261 called logout() whenever useAuthStore.getState().token !== null. authStore.ts:92-125: logout() only clears localStorage and state, with no call to the server. authStore.ts:127-150 loadFromStorage is called only from hooks/useAuth.ts:20 on mount. The only 'storage' listeners in the source tree, excluding tests, are preferencesStore.ts:470 and useTheme.ts:127; neither handles auth_token. There is no visibilitychange handler. auth/middleware.py:90-103 raises HTTP 401 when the Authorization header is missing. All API modules (client.ts, people.ts, workflow.ts, auditReadiness.ts, shareableReviews.ts) send requests through authFetch, so the whole REST surface is affected. The parseResponse docblock at client.ts:186-190 still says 'any API call returning 401 triggers authStore.logout()', which is now stale.

findings.title: Inserted blocks orphaned the doc comments of personDisambiguator and deleteAdminUser
findings.summary: 793d0f95a inserted new code between two functions and their JSDoc. PROVIDER_LABEL (people.ts:98-110) now sits between personDisambiguator's doc (people.ts:97) and the function, and DELETE_ADMIN_USER_REASON_MAX_LENGTH (client.ts:578-579) now sits between deleteAdminUser's old doc (client.ts:577) and the function. Each comment now documents the wrong symbol.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer hovering over PROVIDER_LABEL sees two stacked docblocks, the first describing the disambiguator line. Hovering over DELETE_ADMIN_USER_REASON_MAX_LENGTH shows 'Delete a local-auth account. Backend returns 204 No Content.' personDisambiguator itself has no documentation.
findings.evidence: people.ts:97 `/** The line that tells two people with one name apart: never the name again. */` is followed directly by PROVIDER_LABEL's own docblock at 98-102. client.ts:577 `/** Delete a local-auth account. Backend returns 204 No Content. */` is followed by the constant's docblock at 578.
findings.suggested_fix: Move each orphaned comment back directly above its function (personDisambiguator at people.ts:112, deleteAdminUser at client.ts:586), or merge it into the new docblock.

verdicts.reason: I confirmed this at the pinned commit 74c0ce0db, and the window introduced it. In people.ts, commit 793d0f95a put the PROVIDER_LABEL block between personDisambiguator's one-line doc and the function. findings.title: flex-wrap on blocker rows moves the Ask button to its own line; the comment says layout is unchanged
findings.summary: b5e458d1d added `.decision-panel-item--blocker { flex-wrap: wrap; }` so the reviewer note (flex-basis 100%) gets its own line. In a multi-line flex container, items are placed on lines by their hypothetical main size. For the `flex: 1 1 auto` text span that is its max-content width, so the text no longer shrinks beside the button. The comment claims rows without a note are untouched, and that is false.
findings.failure_scenario: Blocker with an advisor note: the DOM order is text, then note, then Ask button. The 100%-basis note forces line breaks before and after it, so even with short detail text 'Ask the composer about this' lands on a third line at the left edge instead of beside the text. Blocker without a note but with a detail sentence wider than the panel (about 400-600px chat column): the text fills line 1 and Ask drops to line 2, left-aligned. Before the window, the text wrapped inside its span and Ask stayed on the right. The button is still reachable, so nothing is blocked, but the layout changed for every such row.
findings.evidence: chat.css:2301-2306 `.decision-panel-item { display:flex; justify-content: space-between }`; chat.css:2313-2318 text `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0`; chat.css:2325-2336 new wrap rule plus note `flex: 1 1 100%`, with the comment 'a row without a note still has only its two children, so nothing wraps'. DecisionPanel.tsx:228-252 renders span, then optional note div, then Ask Button, in that order.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the wrap only when the row has a note, using a `decision-panel-item--has-note` modifier set in DecisionPanel when `row.note !== null`. Or render the note as a block after a flex wrapper around text + Ask. Fix or remove the comment.

verdicts.reason: The finding holds; I could not refute it. The `flex-wrap: wrap` rule sits on every blocker row, whether or not the row has a note. Nothing overrides the flex sizing of the text span or the Ask button. The Ask button renders in freeform mode, which is now the only mode. In a flex container that wraps, CSS Flexbox §9.3 step 5 assigns items to lines by their hypothetical main size. For a span with `flex: 1 1 auto` and `width: auto`, that size is the text's max-content width, and `min-width: 0` does not reduce it. So when the full detail text plus the gap plus the button is wider than the row, the button drops to its own line at the left instead of the text wrapping beside it. Before b5e458d1d the row did not wrap: the span shrank, its text wrapped inside it, and Ask stayed on the right. The new comment says a row without a note has only two children, so nothing wraps. That is false: two children can still wrap. In rows that have a note, the 100% basis also puts Ask on a third line. The button stays visible and clickable, so this is only a layout regression plus a comment that misdescribes the behaviour. Severity stays low.
verdicts.evidence: chat.css:2301-2307: `.decision-panel-item` sets `display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between` and does not wrap by default. chat.css:2313-2318: `.decision-panel-item-text` has `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0`. chat.css:2321-2323: the Ask button has `flex-shrink: 0`. chat.css:2325-2331: new in the window. The comment says "a row without a note still has only its two children, so nothing wraps", and `.decision-panel-item--blocker { flex-wrap: wrap; }` is applied to every blocker row. chat.css:2333-2336: the note has `flex: 1 1 100%`. A grep of the frontend CSS finds no other rule for .decision-panel-item-text or the Ask button that would limit the span's flex-basis. DecisionPanel.tsx:225: `className={`decision-panel-item decision-panel-item--${row.kind}`}` sets the blocker modifier whether or not a note exists. DecisionPanel.tsx:229-252 renders in this order: the text span (detail plus suggestion), then the optional note div, then the Ask Button. findings.title: Blocker `note` is consumed but not checked by the isValidationReadiness admission guard
findings.summary: 6a34007fb added `note: string | null` to ValidationReadinessBlocker, and b5e458d1d projects `note: blocker.note` into DecisionRow and renders it when `row.note !== null`. The shared type-guard in api/validationReadiness.ts:15-21, which POST /validate and the audit-readiness reload both use, still checks only code, component_id, component_type, detail and suggestion. It therefore asserts a `note` shape it never checks.
findings.failure_scenario: Readiness payload with a blocker that has no `note` key (for example a skewed backend from before 6a34007fb): the guard admits it, `row.note` is undefined, and `undefined !== null` is true, so every blocker shows the heading "Reviewer's note (the advisor's own words — not verified by ELSPETH):" over an empty paragraph. That falsely implies an advisor remark. A non-string note, such as an object, passes and throws 'Objects are not valid as a React child' in DecisionPanel. The backend Pydantic model currently makes note required (execution/schemas.py:262), so a matched deployment does not trigger this.
findings.evidence: api/validationReadiness.ts:15-21 has no note clause. types/index.ts:611 has `note: string | null`. decisionPanelRows.ts:164 has `note: blocker.note`. DecisionPanel.tsx:230 has `row.note !== null &&`. 6a34007fb added `note: null` to the fixtures in api/auditReadiness.test.ts and api/client.execution.test.ts but did not change the guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `(typeof blocker.note === "string" || blocker.note === null)` to the blockers `every(...)` predicate in api/validationReadiness.ts, following the suggestion clause.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at 74c0ce0db. isValidationReadiness is the only runtime admission for readiness blockers on both paths: POST /validate (client.ts:1391) and the audit-readiness reload (auditReadiness.ts:133). It checks every other blocker field, including a string-or-null clause for suggestion, but has no clause for the new `note` field. The TS type (types/index.ts:611) declares `note: string | null`, and decisionPanelRows.ts:164 projects `blocker.note` into the row. DecisionPanel.tsx:230 then uses `row.note !== null` to decide whether to render the "Reviewer's note (the advisor's own words — not verified by ELSPETH):" block. So if a blocker arrives without the key, `undefined !== null` is true and the panel shows the labelled heading over an empty paragraph. If the note is an object, the guard still admits it and React throws "Objects are not valid as a React child". The window added the field (6a34007fb) but never touched the guard: `git log 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db -- api/validationReadiness.ts` returns no commits. It is a real half-wired admission. Severity stays low because a matched deployment cannot trigger it. The backend Pydantic model makes `note` required with no default (execution/schemas.py:262), _StrictResponse forbids extra fields, and there is no exclude_none on any web route. So conforming responses always carry `note: null`. The epoch 64→65 bump also means no persisted pre-field readiness rows survive to reach the reload path. The failure needs a skewed or non-conforming backend, which is exactly the case this frontend guard exists to reject.

{row.note}

`. - Callers of the guard: api/client.ts:1391 (validate endpoint) and api/auditReadiness.ts:133 (reload `isValidationResult`). - Backend: execution/schemas.py:262, `note: str | None` is required with no default. _StrictResponse (schemas.py:155) has extra="forbid" and strict.
