findings.failure_scenario: Narrow chat dock, blocker detail 'Completion advisory review did not clear after the available attempts.' plus a suggestion: the text's max-content width + gap + 'Ask the composer about this' is wider than the panel. Before, the text wrapped beside a right-aligned button. Now the button drops to a second line, left-aligned. With a note the order is text / note / button, so the button ends up below the note.
findings.evidence: chat.css:2313-2318 (.decision-panel-item-text flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0), 2320-2323 (ask button flex-shrink: 0), 2325-2331 (new wrap + comment). DecisionPanel.tsx:226-251 renders span, optional note div, then Button. Per CSS Flexbox §9.3, items are collected into lines by outer hypothetical main size, which is the flex base size, i.e. max-content for flex-basis auto. min-width: 0 does not reduce it. Added in b5e458d1d.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `.decision-panel-item--blocker .decision-panel-item-text { flex: 1 1 0; }` so the text wraps internally beside the button, or scope the wrap to `.decision-panel-item--blocker:has(.decision-panel-reviewer-note)`. Correct the comment.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this finding. The code trace confirms it. Commit b5e458d1d added `flex-wrap: wrap` to every `.decision-panel-item--blocker`, whether or not the row has a note (chat.css:2329-2331). The text span has `flex: 1 1 auto` and `min-width: 0` (chat.css:2313-2318), so its flex base size is its max-content width. `min-width: 0` sets a lower clamp only, so it cannot shrink the size used to break items into lines. The Ask button has `flex-shrink: 0` (chat.css:2320-2323). When the detail and suggestion text is wider than one line beside the button, the flexbox line-breaking step (§9.3) puts the button on a second line. There, `justify-content: space-between` with a single item places it at the start, so it sits left-aligned (chat.css:2301-2307). The text then shrinks to fill the first line on its own. Before this commit the row did not wrap: the text wrapped internally and the button stayed on the right. Nothing prevents this layout. No media or container query overrides `.decision-panel-item`, and no other stylesheet touches it; the only hits are in chat.css. Blocker details are long sentences, e.g. no_tool_policy.py:141-143, which is about 190 characters. So in the chat dock the wrap is the usual case, not an edge case. The new comment says a row without a note has only two children, so nothing wraps. That is false, because wrapping depends on content width, not on the number of children. The finding misreads nothing. The effect is only visual: the button stays usable and nothing becomes inaccessible. So it stays at low severity.
verdicts.evidence: chat.css:2301-2307 (`.decision-panel-item` display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:center; no wrap before the window); chat.css:2313-2318 (`.decision-panel-item-text` flex:1 1 auto; min-width:0; overflow-wrap:anywhere); chat.css:2320-2323 (ask button flex-shrink:0); chat.css:2325-2331 (new comment claiming "nothing wraps" plus unconditional `.decision-panel-item--blocker { flex-wrap: wrap }`, added in b5e458d1d per `git diff 7c986dc97 74c0ce0db`). DecisionPanel.tsx:226-251 renders, for a blocker row: the text span, then the optional note div, then the Button, all as direct flex children of the li. No `.decision-panel-item` override exists anywhere else in the frontend CSS; the 760px media blocks at chat.css:2423 target other classes only. Example blocker-length text: no_tool_policy.py:141-143.

findings.title: Approvals history lost its keyboard-focusable scroller; the Approvals tabpanel is not focusable
findings.summary: 040b89986 removed the `graph-detail-table-scroll tabIndex=0 role=group` wrapper along with the Workflow-tab disclosure. ApprovalsView renders the bare table inside the `.artifact-workspace-panel` tabpanel, which has overflow: auto and no tabIndex, and the table has no focusable content. That conflicts with the project's recorded WCAG 2.1.1 ruling that scroll containers without controls must be focusable.
findings.failure_scenario: A session with several approved full prompts (pre-wrapped values) overflows the Approvals panel. A keyboard-only Safari user (or one on older Chromium) opens the Approvals tab. Tab moves past the panel and arrow keys switch tabs, so rows below the fold can't be scrolled into view. Before the window the same rows sat in a tabIndex=0 scroller on the Workflow tab.
findings.evidence: GraphApprovals.tsx:5-37 (table only). ApprovalsView.tsx:19-20. ArtifactWorkspace.tsx:603-611 (tabpanel, no tabIndex). workspace.css:314-322 (overflow: auto). Ruling precedent: chat.css:1113-1116, ChatPanel.tsx:3397, GraphOutputs.tsx:113. Chromium 130+ and Firefox auto-focus scrollers, so the impact is mainly Safari. recent-code-hints.md has no contrary ruling.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the Approvals tabpanel tabIndex={0} (the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern for a panel with no focusable content), or wrap ApprovalsTable in ApprovalsView in a focusable, labelled role=group container like GraphOutputs.tsx:113.

verdicts.reason: I traced the code path and it holds. At 74c0ce0db the Approvals artifact tab renders ApprovalsView. ApprovalsView puts the bare ApprovalsTable in a plain div with no tabIndex (ApprovalsView.tsx:18-22). The table contains only th/td/code/span/time elements, none of them focusable (GraphApprovals.tsx:5-37), and ApprovalsView adds no controls of its own (ApprovalsView.tsx:34-54). The element that actually scrolls is the tabpanel `.artifact-workspace-panel` (workspace.css:313-321: flex 1 1 auto, min-height 0, overflow auto). That tabpanel has role/id/aria/hidden/inert attributes but no tabIndex (ArtifactWorkspace.tsx:601-636). The only tabIndex in the file is the roving tabindex on the tab buttons (ArtifactWorkspace.tsx:518). No custom keyboard-scroll handler exists: grep for PageDown/scrollBy finds none, and --scroll-owner is a CSS naming contract only. So a keyboard-only user in a browser that does not auto-focus scroll containers cannot reach approval rows below the fold. That conflicts with the project's own WCAG 2.1.1 idiom for content-only scrollers (chat.css:1113-1119, and the removed graph-detail-table-scroll tabIndex=0 role=group wrapper). recent-code-hints.md has no ruling on approvals or scrollers. One correction to the attribution: the Approvals tab never had a focusable scroller. It was added in the window by 6a50bab15, and 543ed1d68 swapped its list for the table 'given the whole panel instead of a 12rem scroller'. What 040b89986 did was remove the Workflow-tab disclosure, which was the only remaining keyboard-reachable scroller for the same rows. All three commits are in 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db, so the defect is diff-anchored either way. The severity stays low: the impact falls mainly on Safari, since recent Chromium and Firefox make scrollers keyboard-focusable, and nothing is lost or corrupted.
verdicts.evidence: GraphApprovals.tsx:5-37 (table only, no focusable descendants). ApprovalsView.tsx:18-22 (the `<div className="graph-detail-table approvals-view-table">` wrapper has no tabIndex or role) and :34-54 (no controls). ArtifactWorkspace.tsx:601-636 (tabpanel div, no tabIndex); :518 (the only tabIndex, on the tab buttons); :143 (the approvals tab returns <ApprovalsView/>). workspace.css:313-321 (.artifact-workspace-panel overflow: auto, --scroll-owner: artifact); :333-339 (.approvals-view-table). inspector.css:382-390 (.graph-detail-table-scroll max-height 12rem, overflow auto, focus-visible ring: the idiom the window dropped). The 040b89986 diff removes `<div className="graph-detail-table-scroll" tabIndex={0} role="group" aria-label="Approvals table">`, with the comment 'keyboard-focusable by the same WCAG 2.1.1 ruling as the chat dock'. 543ed1d68's message says 'The tab gives the table the whole panel instead of the 12rem scroller'. chat.css:1113-1119 records the WCAG 2.1.1 ruling for content-only scrollers.

findings.title: Clearing a JSON field is treated as invalid JSON, so an optional JSON knob cannot be cleared
findings.summary: onChange wraps every keystroke in JsonDraft. JsonDraft("") fails JSON.parse, and fieldHasError returns true for any draft that failed to parse. An empty or whitespace-only editor is therefore reported as invalid JSON, not as unanswered.
findings.failure_scenario: The user opens Edit on an optional json-object knob (for example the JSON sink's headers), selects everything and deletes it. The form shows the alert 'Invalid JSON object — enter an object with named properties.' and disables both Continue and 'Done editing'. The only ways out are typing {} (which is then submitted as a real value) or typing the literal null (which gets omitted at submit). The form never explains that null is how to clear a field.
findings.evidence: Line 761: onChange={(event) => onChange(new JsonDraft(event.target.value))}. Line 464: if (!value.parsed.ok) return true. Line 308: 'Done editing' is disabled whenever any visible field has an error. Before the window, a json-value field sent "" silently, and a json-object field passed the local check and was then rejected by the backend's _validate_knob_value.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a whitespace-only draft as unanswered, meaning a parsed value of null. Requiredness then still blocks required fields, and handleContinue already omits a null optional non-nullable field. At minimum, change the error text to say that null unsets the field.

verdicts.reason: The mechanics are described correctly. Every keystroke becomes a JsonDraft (SchemaFormTurn.tsx:761). JsonDraft("") fails JSON.parse (lines 47-53). fieldHasError returns true on a failed parse (line 464). 'Done editing' (line 308) and Continue (via fieldsNeedingAttention at line 135) are then disabled. But the finding's headline claim is false: an optional JSON knob can be cleared. The window's code documents JSON null as the unanswered representation (lines 466-468), and handleContinue omits a null optional non-nullable field (lines 150-163). Also, the form's own empty state for a json-object with no default or prefill is `{}` (emptyForKind, lines 400-401, applied in initialValues at 385-389). So typing `{}` returns the field to exactly the state it started in, not to 'a real value' it never had. The claimed regression is not one either. Before the window, a cleared json-object sent "" to the backend, which rejected it (the finding says so itself), and a cleared json-value silently submitted the string "". Blocking empty text locally is therefore stricter and more correct. It does not stop a user from continuing. What remains is that the error text does not mention null or {} as the way to unset a field. That is a wording nit on a lane being retired, not a defect that blocks a user or corrupts data.
verdicts.evidence: Pinned HEAD is 74c0ce0db. In SchemaFormTurn.tsx: line 761 is `onChange={(event) => onChange(new JsonDraft(event.target.value))}`. Lines 462-472 are `if (!value.parsed.ok) return true; ... if (parsed === null) return false;`, with the comment 'An unanswered optional knob uses null and is omitted at submission when non-nullable'. Lines 150-163 are handleContinue, where `if (value === null && !isRequiredNow(field, values) && !field.nullable) continue;` omits a cleared-by-null optional field. Lines 385-389 are initialValues, which wraps emptyForKind in a JsonDraft, and emptyForKind returns `{}` for json-object and `[]` for json-array (lines 400-403). So `{}` or `[]` is the form's own blank state, and `null` is the documented unset. Pre-window code, from `git diff 7c986dc97 74c0ce0db`: the old onChange did `try { JSON.parse } catch { onChange(event.target.value) }`, and the old fieldHasError flagged json-object only when `value.trim() !== ""`. Empty text was therefore sent to the backend as "" and rejected there, or, for json-value, accepted as the string "". The window's change moved that to a local, explicit block. Recovery works through `{}` or `null`. Only the error message's wording could be improved.

findings.title: JSON textarea no longer opens pretty-printed
findings.summary: initialValues seeds each JSON field with JsonDraft(JSON.stringify(v)), which has no indentation. jsonText returns the draft's text as-is, so the 2-space pretty branch now runs only when the value is undefined.
findings.failure_scenario: A prefilled schema object such as {"mode":"observed","fields":[...]} opens in the Edit textarea as one long line. Before the window it opened as 2-space-indented JSON. The summary view is unaffected because CodeBlock pretty-prints. This makes the value harder to review and edit but does not block anything.
findings.evidence: At 7c986dc97, jsonText at lines 781-783 returned JSON.stringify(value ?? emptyForKind(kind), null, 2). At the pinned commit, line 388 is new JsonDraft(JSON.stringify(values[field.name])) and line 814 is if (value instanceof JsonDraft) return value.text.
findings.suggested_fix: Seed the draft with JSON.stringify(values[field.name], null, 2).

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this finding. At the pinned commit, `initialValues` (SchemaFormTurn.tsx:377-391) always wraps each JSON-kind field in `new JsonDraft(JSON.stringify(v))` with no indent argument. It does this for prefilled values, for default values and for `emptyForKind` values. The textarea gets its text from `jsonText` (line 755). `jsonText` returns `value.text` whenever the value is a JsonDraft (line 814), so the 2-space `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` branch at line 815 can no longer run for any field that `initialValues` seeded.

No other path undoes this. The two `setValues` paths (lines 86 and 113) only touch `path` and `on_validation_failure` or store what the user typed. Neither re-formats a JSON field.

The base commit pretty-printed these values. At 7c986dc97 the state held parsed objects, and `jsonText` (lines 781-783) returned `JSON.stringify(value ?? emptyForKind(kind), null, 2)` for every value that was not a string.

The change came in 07faf477e ("bind chat cards to authoritative review state"). Its review doc, docs/reviews/2026-09-22-chat-card-repairs.md, says at line 32 only that JSON fields "retain raw editor text independently of parsed values". I found no ruling that the text should start compact, in that doc or in recent-code-hints.md. The regression is cosmetic and nothing is blocked. The file is in the guided lane that is being retired, so low severity stands.
verdicts.evidence:
- Pinned 74c0ce0db, SchemaFormTurn.tsx:387-389: `if (isJsonField(field)) { values[field.name] = new JsonDraft(JSON.stringify(values[field.name])); }` runs for every JSON field, with no indent argument.
- Line 755: `value={jsonText(value, field.kind)}`.
- Line 814: `if (value instanceof JsonDraft) return value.text;`. The pretty-print branch at line 815 now runs only when the value is not a JsonDraft, which never happens for a seeded JSON field.
- Base 7c986dc97, lines 781-783: `if (typeof value === "string") return value; return JSON.stringify(value ?? emptyForKind(kind), null, 2);`, so prefilled objects and arrays opened indented by 2 spaces.
- Introduced by 07faf477e, which is the only commit that touches this file in the window.
- The only other writes to the form state are `setValues` at lines 86-100 (path and on_validation_failure prefill) and `onChange` at lines 112-122. Neither re-formats JSON text.
- No recorded ruling on the initial format: docs/reviews/2026-09-22-chat-card-repairs.md:32 mentions only raw-text retention, and a grep of recent-code-hints.md for JsonDraft or pretty returned no hits.

findings.title: fieldHasError comment is stale and its json-object/json-array string arms are unreachable
findings.summary: The comment above fieldHasError still says the check covers 'a JSON object/array whose text failed to parse' and that 'onChange handlers keep that raw text'. The window also left a dangling '//' line there. JSON fields now hold a JsonDraft (all three kinds, including wrong-container parses) or undefined, never a raw string, so the case json-object/json-array typeof-string arm at lines 477-479 is dead code.
findings.failure_scenario: No runtime failure. A maintainer who trusts the comment would conclude that json-value is still exempt and that raw strings still reach this function, and could edit the dead branch while the real check in the JsonDraft block goes unchanged.
findings.evidence: Lines 456-461: the comment, with an empty '//' line left by the deleted json-value paragraph. Lines 477-479: return typeof value === "string" && value.trim() !== "". Every JSON write goes through JsonDraft (lines 388 and 761), and the only other state for a JSON field is deletion to undefined (line 117).
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the comment to describe JsonDraft's behaviour and delete the unreachable json-object/json-array arms.

verdicts.reason: I traced it at 74c0ce0db and could not refute it. Every way a JSON-kind field gets a value produces either a JsonDraft or undefined, so the `typeof value === "string"` arm for json-object and json-array can never be reached. Commit 07faf477e deleted the json-value exclusion paragraph and left a bare `//` behind. The comment above it now describes the check incompletely: it covers only object/array parse failure, while the JsonDraft block also blocks json-value parse failures and wrong-container parses. One part of the comment is still roughly true: JsonDraft keeps the raw text in `.text`. No runtime effect, so severity stays low.
verdicts.evidence:
SchemaFormTurn.tsx:
- **Initial values:** lines 387-388 wrap every JSON-kind field in `new JsonDraft(JSON.stringify(...))`. For an undefined prefill this still yields a JsonDraft (with a failed parse), never a string.
- **Only JSON editor onChange:** line 761 is `onChange(new JsonDraft(event.target.value))`. The window replaced the old try/catch at that spot, which used to pass the raw string on a parse failure.
- **Hiding a field:** lines 115-118 only `delete` the key, so the value becomes undefined, not a string.
- **Only other state write:** the prefill effect at lines 86-100 writes only `path` and `on_validation_failure`.
- **Callers:** fieldHasError is called only from lines 135, 308 and 743, all with values from that same state. When a JsonDraft is passed, lines 463-472 return before the switch.
- **Dead arm:** lines 477-479 therefore never see a string for JSON kinds.
- **Stale comment:** lines 456-461 still say 'a JSON object/array whose text failed to parse' and end in a lone `//`. `git diff 7c986dc97 74c0ce0db` shows commit 07faf477e deleting the three-line 'json-value is excluded by design' paragraph beneath that `//` and adding the JsonDraft block, without updating the comment.

findings.title: LLM model label shown on llm transform cards but not on llm source cards
findings.summary: daad04b0b adds the model/profile to the node card and accessible description only when node_type === 'transform' && plugin === 'llm'. The source loop (1185-1197) and the source branch of the a11y describe loop pass no model label, but there is an LLM source plugin named 'llm' whose config has a model field.
findings.failure_scenario: A pipeline starts with an llm source (model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4) that feeds an llm transform (model gpt-4o). The transform card reads 'llm · model gpt-4o'. The source card reads just 'llm', and its a11y list entry has no model. So the canvas does not show which model generates the rows, although the collapsed Wiring table does, because pluginBindingLabel dispatches on plugin === 'llm' whatever the node kind.
findings.evidence: GraphView.tsx:1213-1215 and 2051-2053 gate on node_type === 'transform'. src/elspeth/plugins/sources/llm/source.py:122 has name = 'llm'. sources/llm/config.py:61 has model: str | None. lib/pluginBindingLabel.ts:8 calls llmBindingLabel for any plugin === 'llm'. The GraphView.test.tsx it.each added in daad04b0b covers only the transform case.
findings.suggested_fix: In the source loop, pass source.plugin === 'llm' ? llmBindingLabel(source.options) : undefined as modelLabel to makeRfNode, append the same label in the source describe branch, and add a source case to the test.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this. At 74c0ce0db the model label reaches the card only for transform nodes. The source loop never passes the new `modelLabel` argument, and the accessible-description loop for sources doesn't add it either. The LLM source plugin is a real plugin that the web path uses and assigns an operator profile, and its options include a `model` field. The frontend `SourceSpec` carries the options, and the Wiring table already labels sources through `pluginBindingLabel`. So an llm source card shows only 'llm', with no model or profile, while an llm transform card shows 'llm · model X'. The commit title is 'show LLM model in graph nodes', with no transform-only qualifier, and I found no recorded ruling that leaves sources out. This is cosmetic and informational, so the severity stays low.
verdicts.evidence:
- **Card gate:** GraphView.tsx:1213-1215 shows the label only when `node.node_type === "transform" && node.plugin === "llm"`, then calls `llmBindingLabel(node.options)`.
- **Source cards:** the source loop at GraphView.tsx:1184-1198 calls `makeRfNode` with 8 arguments. It never passes the new 9th argument `modelLabel` (added at :1073).
- **Accessible descriptions:** at GraphView.tsx:2046-2047 the source branch is `describe(sourceComponentId(sourceName), "source", source.plugin)` with no label added. Only the node loop at :2051-2053 appends one.
- **The LLM source exists:** plugins/sources/llm/source.py:120-128 defines `LLMSource`, with name="llm" and web_config_authority=OPERATOR_PROFILED. plugins/sources/llm/config.py:61 has `model: str | None`.
- **The web uses it:** web/plugin_policy/profiles.py:1479 registers a `PluginId("source", "llm")` resolver, and web/plugin_policy/compiler.py:21 lists `PluginId("source","llm")`.
- **The frontend has the options:** types/index.ts:141-148 `SourceSpec` has `options: Record<string, unknown>`.
- **The Wiring table labels sources:** GraphOutputs.tsx:76 calls `pluginBindingLabel(source.plugin, source.options)`, and lib/pluginBindingLabel.ts:8 dispatches to `llmBindingLabel` for plugin==="llm" whatever the node kind.
- **Test coverage:** the `it.each` that daad04b0b adds to GraphView.test.tsx covers only a transform node.
- **Rulings:** docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md has no ruling about graph-node model labels.

No runtime defect: the comment gets the call graph wrong. The same staleness appears in workspace.css:333, also added in the window, and in ChatPanel.tsx:3503, an untouched line.
findings.evidence: approvalRows.ts:65-67 at 74c0ce0db. grep over src/ finds approvalRows called only from components/workspace/ApprovalsView.tsx:20 and GraphApprovals.test.tsx. The 040b89986 diff removes the GraphApprovals ErrorBoundary block from GraphView.tsx.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to say the helper serves the Approvals tab (ApprovalsView), whose caller wraps it in an ErrorBoundary. Update the comments at workspace.css:333 and ChatPanel.tsx:3503 to name the Approvals tab.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at 74c0ce0db. 6a50bab15 (commit #111 in the window) added the docstring at approvalRows.ts:65-67, which says the helper is shared by the Workflow tab's Approvals table and the Approvals tab and that both callers sit inside an ErrorBoundary. verdicts.evidence:
- approvalRows.ts:65-67 (pinned) reads: "One row per approved interpretation, shared by the Workflow tab's Approvals table and the Approvals tab. ... both callers sit inside an ErrorBoundary."
- A grep over src/elspeth/web/frontend/src finds exactly one non-test call: ApprovalsView.tsx:20 `<ApprovalsTable rows={approvalRows(events, state)} />`. That call is wrapped by `<ErrorBoundary label="Approvals">` at ApprovalsView.tsx:48-50. The other hits are the tests in GraphApprovals.test.tsx.

findings.title: Multi-query prompt rows keyed by non-unique query name
findings.summary: LlmPromptRoles uses key={name} for each query's row. Names from queryEntries can repeat: duplicate list-form names, or the positional '#<index>' fallback matching a real name.
findings.failure_scenario: The planner authors queries: [{name:'score',template:'A'},{name:'score',template:'B'}]. The plugin rejects duplicate names, but only through validation. The state still holds both entries and the inspector renders two siblings with key 'score'. React warns, and when the options change during repair it can reuse or drop the wrong row, so the inspector shows a stale per-query user prompt.
findings.evidence: OptionRows.tsx:196-209 `queries.map(([name, entry]) => (<div key={name}>`; the positional label `#${index}` is at :164; multi_query.py:324-332 rejects duplicate names only at validation.
findings.suggested_fix: Key on position as well, e.g. queries.map(([name, entry], index) => <div key={`${index}:${name}`}>).

verdicts.reason: The defect is real, but the finding names the wrong way to reach it. The stated scenario, where the planner authors duplicate list-form names and the state keeps both, cannot happen. Every planner write path validates the options before storing them, and duplicate names fail that check. The other trigger in the finding, a nameless entry whose '#<index>' label matches a real name, is refused the same way. Validation happens inside LLMConfig's model validator, which calls resolve_queries. The tool paths that run it and return a failure without storing the state are upsert_node, patch_node_options, splice_transform and set_pipeline. So neither duplicate case can come from the planner. There is still a way in: the YAML import route. It copies node options verbatim, never parses LLMConfig, and saves with preflight_exception_policy="persist_invalid", so an imported state with duplicate list-form query names is stored with is_valid=False. The inspector then renders two sibling rows with the same key. The effect is smaller than claimed. The rows hold no local state and get their content from props, so a plain update of [score, score] to [score', score'] matches by position and shows the right text. A stale leftover row needs an unusual change in the list shape, such as re-importing over the same node. What is certain is a duplicate-key warning from React on a state that is already invalid. The suggested index-plus-name key is cheap and correct. Severity stays low.
verdicts.evidence:
- OptionRows.tsx:158-168: queryEntries labels list entries entry.name, or `#${index}` when the name is missing. OptionRows.tsx:196-197 renders `queries.map(([name, entry]) => (<div key={name}>`. Confirmed at 74c0ce0db. The component came in with 6211043bd.
- Duplicate names are rejected at config-parse time: plugins/transforms/llm/base.py:461-484 (`_validate_cross_query_rules` calls `resolve_queries`); multi_query.py:315-332 (a list entry without a name is refused, and so is a duplicate name).
- The planner paths run that parse before storing and fail on error with plugin_options_invalid: composer/tools/transforms.py:740-747 (upsert_node), :1762-1770 (patch_node_options), :1958 (splice); composer/tools/sessions.py:1483-1495 (set_pipeline). Each goes through _common.py:3293 `_prevalidate_transform_for_context`, then :3357, then `_prevalidate_plugin_options`, whose `config_cls.from_dict` at :2354 returns "Invalid options...". So the finding's planner scenario is unreachable.
- The route that does reach it: sessions/routes/composer/state.py:840-990 (`import_state_yaml` and `seed_state_from_runtime_yaml`). It builds the state with `composition_state_from_runtime_yaml`; yaml_importer.py:~656 copies options as `_json_mapping(entry.get("options"))` without parsing LLMConfig. Nothing on this route rejects the plugin config (the checks cover plugin policy, blobs, paths, secrets and interpretation rows). It then calls `_state_data_from_composer_state(..., preflight_exception_policy="persist_invalid")` (state.py:949; _helpers.py:2718-2730), which saves the state with is_valid=False instead of rejecting it.
- A YAML document with `queries: [{name: score, ...}, {name: score, ...}]` is legal, because YAML's duplicate-key rejection (yaml_importer.py:198-230) only applies to mapping keys, not list items.

findings.title: Unsaved-draft recovery branch is unreachable against the current backend
findings.summary: draftWasSaved is always true while the panel is mounted, so the new 'not saved on the server' alert, the Discard-focus arm and the conditional Apply button never run. The backend only sends partial_state after save_composition_state succeeds, with the persisted UUID id. When the save fails it sends partial_state_save_failed with no partial_state, and isComposerRecoveryError then returns false, so the panel never opens.
findings.failure_scenario: A composer turn fails and the partial-state save raises SQLAlchemyError. The 422 body carries partial_state_save_failed=true, partial_state_save_error and failed_turn, but no partial_state (_helpers.py:3214/3222, 3380/3381, 3616/3617). isComposerRecoveryError (types/recovery.ts:22-26) returns false, so the recovery panel never shows its new explanation and the user gets the generic chat error. The repair doc's item 8 (docs/reviews/2026-09-22-chat-card-repairs.md) and RecoveryPanel.test.tsx:105-110 exercise a response shape the server never sends. The panel also calls partial_state.id.trim() without the typeof check the store guard uses, so the defensive case it exists for would throw during render.
findings.evidence: _helpers.py:3199/3357/3606 set partial_state only after a successful save via _recovery_partial_state_response (the persisted record, UUID id). The recovery-error type guard requires partial_state != null. sessionStore.applyRecoveredState :3105-3114 has the same guard but predates the window (git log -L: 23e3a2be9, 2026-06-22).
findings.suggested_fix: Either delete the unreachable branch and its test, or make it reachable: route partial_state_save_failed bodies that have no partial_state to an explanation in the chat error or panel, and use a typeof check before .trim() as the store does.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute the finding. The unsaved-draft branch that commit 07faf477e added to RecoveryPanel is unreachable with any response body the server can send. There are only three places that write `partial_state` into a response body. Each writes it inside the `try`, after `save_composition_state` succeeds, so the id is always the saved record's id. The `except SQLAlchemyError` arm sets only `partial_state_save_failed` and `partial_state_save_error`. So no body carries both `partial_state` and `partial_state_save_failed=true`. `CompositionStateResponse.id` is a non-empty string built from the saved record. A body without `partial_state` fails `isComposerRecoveryError`, so neither the store nor `useRecoveryPanel` opens the panel. That means `draftWasSaved` is always true while the panel is mounted. As a result, the alert at :138-143, the Discard-focus arm at :55 and the conditional Apply button never fire in practice. RecoveryPanel.test.tsx:97-110 injects shapes the server never produces (`partial_state` together with `saveFailed=true`, and a blank id). The `.trim()` sub-claim is also correct. The panel omits the `typeof recoveredState.id !== "string"` check that `sessionStore.applyRecoveredState` has at :3107, so a malformed id would throw during render instead of reaching the defensive branch. That only matters for bodies the server does not send. Severity stays low because nothing is corrupted or blocked; the new code is only dead. The practical effect is that when the save fails, the user sees the generic chat error rather than the new in-dialog explanation that the repair doc's item 8 promises.
verdicts.evidence: Pinned HEAD is 74c0ce0db336. src/elspeth/web/sessions/routes/_helpers.py:3193-3199: `partial_record = await service.save_composition_state(...)`, then `response_body["partial_state"] = _recovery_partial_state_response(partial_record)`, both inside the try. :3200-3222: the `except SQLAlchemyError` arm sets only `partial_state_save_failed=True` and `partial_state_save_error`. The same pattern appears at :3357 vs :3380-3381 and at :3606 vs :3616-3617. Grepping `'"partial_state"\|partial_state='` over src/elspeth/web/*.py finds only those three response writers. _helpers.py:1045-1048: `_recovery_partial_state_response` returns `_state_response(record).model_dump`, and schemas.py:362 declares `id: str`, which is the saved record's id. types/recovery.ts:22-26: `isComposerRecoveryError` requires `partial_state != null && failed_turn != null`. sessionStore.ts:3078-3087 (`openRecoveryFromError`) and :2329/:2874 gate on it; hooks/useRecoveryPanel.ts:49 does the same. RecoveryPanel.tsx:49-51 (added in 07faf477e): `draftWasSaved = recoveryError !== null && recoveryError.partial_state_save_failed !== true && recoveryError.partial_state.id.trim() !== ""`, with no typeof check. Compare sessionStore.ts:3105-3108, which does check `typeof recoveredState.id !== "string"`. RecoveryPanel.test.tsx:97-105 sets `partial_state.id` to '' or '   ' or sets `partial_state_save_failed=true` alongside `partial_state`; the server produces neither shape. docs/reviews/2026-09-22-chat-card-repairs.md:35-36 (item 8) states the intended behaviour.

findings.title: Approvals tab dropped the keyboard-focusable scroll region the removed disclosure had
findings.summary: 040b89986 removed GraphApprovals' `<div className="graph-detail-table-scroll" tabIndex={0} role="group" aria-label="Approvals table">`, which existed under the house WCAG 2.1.1 ruling. The new tab renders a bare text-only table inside a tabpanel scroller (.artifact-workspace-panel, overflow:auto) that has no tabIndex and no focusable descendants.
findings.failure_scenario: A session with several prompt-template approvals, each rendering the full system and user prompt with pre-wrap, overflows the pane. A keyboard-only user in a browser without automatic focusable scrollers (Safari) presses Tab from the Approvals tab button, focus leaves the panel, and the rows below the fold cannot be scrolled into view.
findings.evidence: ApprovalsView.tsx:19-21; GraphApprovals.tsx ApprovalsTable has no interactive content; ArtifactWorkspace.tsx:601-611 tabpanel has no tabIndex; workspace.css:314-321 overflow:auto; ruling precedent at chat.css:1116 and ChatPanel.tsx:3397. The Spec and YAML panels share the tabIndex-less tabpanel pattern, so the regression is specifically the dropped explicit scroll group.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the table in a labelled tabIndex={0} scroll group, as before, or set tabIndex={0} on the tabpanel when its content has no focusable descendant.

verdicts.reason: The finding's framing is slightly off, but the defect is real. The Approvals tab never had the tabIndex scroll group. `ApprovalsView.tsx` is new in this window (6a50bab15, then 543ed1d68, 040b89986 and 29f9af13b), and none of its versions carried a tabIndex. The `<div className="graph-detail-table-scroll" tabIndex={0} role="group" aria-label="Approvals table">` that 040b89986 removed lived in the Workflow tab's `<details>` disclosure (GraphApprovals, rendered by GraphView). So the Approvals tab did not "drop" anything. What did change is where a keyboard user can reach the approvals. Before 040b89986, the approval rows could be read through the Workflow disclosure's focusable 12rem scroller. After it, the only place they appear is the Approvals tab, and nothing there can take focus. Tracing the render: ApprovalsView.tsx:19-21 is a plain `div.graph-detail-table` holding the ApprovalsTable. The table (GraphApprovals.tsx:5-37) contains only th/td/code/span/time, with no links, buttons or tabIndex. The header (ApprovalsView.tsx:37-46) is text only. The scroller is the tabpanel (ArtifactWorkspace.tsx:603-611), which has no tabIndex. Its CSS at workspace.css:314-321 sets overflow:auto. The only tabIndex in ArtifactWorkspace is on the tab buttons (line 518). Neither .checks-view nor .audit-readiness adds a scroller of its own. .audit-readiness is overflow:hidden, so the panel is what scrolls. The rows show the full approved prompt text (approvalRows.ts:94 `value: event.accepted_value`, and inspector.css:405-407 sets `white-space: pre-wrap` on `.graph-approvals-value`), so overflow is plausible once there are several prompt approvals. The house WCAG 2.1.1 ruling at chat.css:1113-1120 requires exactly this idiom, and GraphOutputs.tsx:113 still follows it. No recorded ruling exempts this panel. The failure path holds only in browsers that do not make scrollers focusable automatically, mainly Safari. Chrome/Edge 130+ and Firefox let the keyboard reach the overflowing panel, which keeps the severity low.

…

findings.title: Delete failure with an empty statusText shows no error
findings.summary: `(err as ApiError).detail ?? "Failed to delete file."` keeps an empty-string detail. parseResponse sets detail from response.statusText, which is "" over HTTP/2 when the body is not JSON. BlobManager renders `{error && ...}`, so nothing appears.
findings.failure_scenario: The app is served over HTTP/2 and the DELETE /blobs/{id} returns a 502 or 504 HTML page from ingress. The store sets error "", no message renders, and the file stays listed with no feedback. Before the window the fixed 'Failed to delete file.' always showed.
findings.evidence: api/client.ts:262 `let detail = response.statusText;` is kept on JSON parse failure (:453-455). api/client.ts:148 notes statusText is "" over HTTP/2. BlobManager.tsx:158 `{error && (`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `||` instead of `??`, or normalise an empty statusText to undefined in parseResponse.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this. I traced the path at 74c0ce0db and it is reachable. Nothing between `fetch` and the store replaces an empty `statusText`. The `??` fallback in blobStore does not catch `""`. BlobManager hides the error box when the error string is empty. This is a regression from the window's commit 7d981d6cf, which replaced a message that always showed. Severity stays low. It needs a non-JSON or detail-less error body, and a transport that sends an empty status phrase, which is always the case over HTTP/2. The delete fails safely: the file stays in the list, and only the feedback is missing.
verdicts.evidence:
- **blobStore.ts:200:** the window diff (7d981d6cf) replaced the fixed "Failed to delete file." / 409 message with `(err as ApiError).detail ?? "Failed to delete file."`. `??` does not fall back when the value is `""`.
- **api/client.ts:1712-1722:** `deleteBlob` passes any `!response.ok` response to `parseResponse`.
- **api/authSession.ts:14-23:** `authFetch` returns the raw `fetch` Response for every status. It does not throw on 5xx and does not normalise anything.
- **api/client.ts:262:** `parseResponse` starts with `let detail = response.statusText;`.
  - It overwrites that at :417 (`explicitDetail ?? firstErrorMessage ?? detail`) only inside the `try { await response.json() }` block.
  - An HTML body from a 502/504 ingress makes `json()` throw. The catch at :453-455 ("use statusText as detail fallback") keeps the value.
  - `detail` is then put into the thrown ApiError unchanged (:458-460).
  - The comment at client.ts:148 records that `statusText` is "" over HTTP/2.
- **Same path, second trigger:** a JSON body with no string `detail`/`message` and no `errors` also leaves `detail` as `statusText`.
- **Result:** the store runs `set({ error: "" })`. `BlobManager.tsx` wraps the error box in `{error && (...)}`, so `""` renders nothing.
- **What does not trigger it:** a network TypeError has no `.detail`, so the fallback works there.

The suggested fix is correct: use `||`, or normalise an empty `statusText` to undefined in `parseResponse`.

findings.title: Newest-started refresh fence discards successful older snapshots
findings.summary: refreshAll/refreshPending drop a response whenever a later refresh for the same session has started, even if that later refresh then fails. No snapshot is applied, and pending review cards (the fix affordance for a blocked Execute) stay missing until another refresh.
findings.failure_scenario: The compose completion fires refreshAll#1 (void). A successful auto-validate fires refreshAll#2 (executionStore.ts:485). #1 resolves after #2 starts and is dropped. #2 rejects on a network error or 5xx. The newly minted pending card never renders, and on first activation ChatPanel's reviewEventsLoaded stays false. Guided (retiring) respondGuided awaits refreshAll and can re-enable submit before the cards land.
findings.evidence: `if (state.refreshRequestBySession[sessionId] !== request) return state;` at :291 and :344. The request is set at the start (:276-282, :306-312) and never reconciled on failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a per-session monotonic sequence and drop a response only when a newer one has already applied (appliedSeqBySession). Keep the terminal-id filtering for resurrection.

verdicts.reason:
I traced the code at 74c0ce0db and the defect is real. The fence came in with 7d981d6cf, inside the review window. refreshAll and refreshPending write their request Symbol before the GET (interpretationEventsStore.ts:275-282, 309-315). The apply step drops the response if that Symbol has been replaced (:291, :344). Nothing clears or reconciles the Symbol when a later request rejects, and nothing retries. So if an older request succeeds after a newer one has started, and the newer one then fails, no snapshot is applied.

The only way a pending card gets into the store is a snapshot. addPendingEvent (:543) has no production callers, and a grep over non-test src finds none. So a card minted by that turn stays invisible until the next refresh. Before the window the last write won, so the older successful snapshot would have been applied; this is a regression.

The overlap the finding describes happens in production. Compose completion fires refreshAll without awaiting it (sessionStore.ts:2476, 2850, 910/1010/1067 via refreshInterpretationEventsForSession). The version bump also starts the auto-validate loop (subscriptions.ts:583), and a successful validate fires a second refreshAll without awaiting it (executionStore.ts:484, which predates the window). Session activation gives the same pairing: selectSession fires refreshAll at sessionStore.ts:2064, then auto-validate. In that case pendingBySession[sid] stays undefined, so reviewEventsLoaded stays false (ChatPanel.tsx:778-780).

The fence is a recorded design choice: docs/reviews/2026-09-22-composer-feedback-repairs.md:8 says "Per-session request ownership orders both interpretation snapshot endpoints". That note only covers responses arriving out of order. It says nothing about the newer request failing, so no ruling covers this gap.

Severity stays low because two things must coincide. The older GET has to outlast a full validate POST round-trip, since the second refresh starts only after validate resolves. Then the newer GET has to fail. The next compose, validate or resolve refreshes the store and recovers it.

One small correction to the finding: refreshPending has no production callers (grep shows only tests), so in practice only refreshAll can hit this. The guided respondGuided await path (sessionStore.ts:3965, 3735) is in the retiring guided lane.
verdicts.evidence:
src/elspeth/web/frontend/src/stores/interpretationEventsStore.ts
- :309-315 sets refreshRequestBySession[sid] to a new Symbol before `await api.listInterpretationEvents(sid, "all")` (:316).
- :344 `if (state.refreshRequestBySession[sessionId] !== request) return state;` has no try/catch or failure reconciliation around it. refreshPending has the same pattern at :275-282 and :291.
- :543 addPendingEvent has no production callers (grep over src excluding tests), so pending cards arrive only through a snapshot.

Callers that overlap:
- sessionStore.ts:2476 and :2850: `void refreshInterpretationEventsForSession(...)` on compose completion.
- sessionStore.ts:2064: `void ...refreshAll(id)` on session select.
- subscriptions.ts:583: the auto-validate loop calls validate on a version bump.
- executionStore.ts:484: `void useInterpretationEventsStore.getState().refreshAll(sessionId)` after a successful validate. This line also exists at base 7c986dc97.

Consequences and history:
- ChatPanel.tsx:778-780: reviewEventsLoaded reads `pendingBySession[activeSessionId] !== undefined`.
- Window diff `git diff 7c986dc97 74c0ce0db` on the store: the fence was added by 7d981d6cf. Before it, the code was an unconditional `set(pendingBySession: ...map)`, so the last write won.
- docs/reviews/2026-09-22-composer-feedback-repairs.md:8 records the intent, ordering of reverse-arriving responses, and does not mention the case where the newer request fails.

findings.title: New ordering logic protects addPendingEvent/refreshPending, which have no production callers; docs are wrong
findings.summary: The window added the pendingAtStart merge and guards in addPendingEvent to keep inline compose receipts through older reads. Neither method has ever had a production caller, so the branch cannot run. The addPendingEvent doc ('used when an event arrives via the compose-loop response') and the refreshPending doc ('overwrites') are false.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer trusts the docs and the repair note ('Inline events survive older reads'), assumes compose responses push cards inline, and removes or relies on the refreshAll call in refreshInterpretationEventsForSession. Removing it brings back the freeform review-card deadlock.
findings.evidence: grep for addPendingEvent/refreshPending outside the store hits only *.test.ts(x) files. `git log -S 'addPendingEvent(' -- src/elspeth/web/frontend/src ':!*.test.ts' ':!*.test.tsx'` returns only 1c23037c9 (the commit that created the store). Merge branch at :290-293 and :377-382, docs at :140-145 and :190-198.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire addPendingEvent to the compose response, or delete addPendingEvent/refreshPending and the pendingAtStart merge, and fix the docstrings.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this finding. addPendingEvent and refreshPending have no production callers. The pendingAtStart merge in refreshAll is also dead in production. That loop only runs when pendingBySession holds an event object that differs from the snapshot taken when this refresh started. The only production code that writes pendingBySession is refreshAll itself, resolveEvent (which only removes entries), optOut (which clears), and the auth reset. Two refreshAll calls cannot interleave to trigger it: the per-session ownership token discards the older response. So nothing adds a new event object while the owning refresh is in flight. The docstrings are out of date. addPendingEvent says it is 'used when an event arrives via the compose-loop response', but nothing calls it. refreshPending says it 'overwrites' the pending map, but after this change it merges local events, drops terminal IDs and respects opt-out. The repair note's claim 'Inline events survive older reads' is true only under test. The failure scenario (a maintainer trusts the docs and removes a refreshAll call) is speculative. What the evidence supports is dead code plus stale docs, so the severity stays low.
verdicts.evidence: Pinned HEAD: 74c0ce0db. A grep of the frontend src for addPendingEvent|refreshPending, excluding *.test.*, finds only the store's own lines: interpretationEventsStore.ts:145 and :198 (declarations) and :274 and :543 (implementations). `git log -S 'addPendingEvent(' -- frontend/src ':!*.test.ts' ':!*.test.tsx'` returns only 1c23037c9, the commit that created the store. Production writers of the store, all non-test getState()/setState() calls: refreshAll at executionStore.ts:485 and sessionStore.ts:736, :2064 and :3056, and the reset at authStore.ts:116 via setState(getInitialState(), true). The rest only read pendingBySession: ChatPanel.tsx:825, subscriptions.ts:419, executionStore.ts:239. Nothing in production calls refreshPending or addPendingEvent. Merge loops: refreshAll at interpretationEventsStore.ts:377-382 and refreshPending at :290-293. Both sit behind the ownership check at :290 and :344 (`refreshRequestBySession[sessionId] !== request` returns state unchanged). resolveEvent removes entries and keeps the same object references, and optOut clears the map, so `pendingAtStart[id] !== event` can never be true in production. The stale docs are at :138-145 (refreshPending 'overwrites') and :190-198 (addPendingEvent 'Used when ... compose-loop response'). The window added all of this in 7d981d6cf. That commit's repair note, docs/reviews/2026-09-22-composer-feedback-repairs.md:8, claims 'Inline events survive older reads. Tests cover ... inline additions', which is exercised only by tests.

findings.title: Rejected logout cleanup barrier is never cleared
findings.summary: pendingLogoutCleanup is reset only after a successful `await cleanup` (no try/finally). login, loginWithToken and loadFromStorage await it outside their try blocks, and the 401 interceptor awaits logout().
findings.failure_scenario: Any exception inside the cleanup .then (a store reset or a synchronous subscriber it triggers) rejects the barrier permanently. Every later login() rejects without setting loginError (silent submit failure), logout() rejects, and owned 401s throw the reset error instead of an ApiError, until a full reload. Before the window only that one logout() rejected. No throwing reset exists today, so this is hardening.
findings.evidence: authStore.ts:96-124 (`await cleanup; if (pendingLogoutCleanup === cleanup) pendingLogoutCleanup = null;`), awaits at :31, :71, :129 before any try, api/client.ts:251-255.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap `await cleanup` in try/finally to clear the barrier, and have waiters use `await pendingLogoutCleanup?.catch(() => undefined)`.

verdicts.reason: The finding reads the code correctly: the barrier is only cleared after `await cleanup` succeeds, and there is no try/finally. But I could not trace a way to make the cleanup reject at the pinned commit, and the reviewer's own evidence says "No throwing reset exists today, so this is hardening." Two ways it could reject are closed today. (1) The six dynamic imports cannot fail on a network or chunk-load error. Every one of those stores is also imported statically by eagerly loaded modules, and the frontend has no React.lazy, so each import() resolves to a module that is already loaded. (2) None of the called resets throws. The synchronous subscribers that the resets trigger also guard against null state. With no reachable path to a rejected barrier, the described failures (a silent login submit failure and 401s rethrowing the reset error) cannot happen. What is left is a robustness suggestion, not a defect.
verdicts.evidence: authStore.ts:96-124: the cleanup is Promise.all over six import() calls, then synchronous resets. The barrier is cleared only after `await cleanup` at line 124. The awaits are at :31, :71 and :129. The shape is confirmed, but reaching the failure needs a rejection. Static imports of the same stores: App.tsx:51 (executionStore); executionStore.ts:39-40 (interpretationEventsStore, sessionStore); CompletionBar.tsx:49 (shareableReviewStore); ChatInput.tsx:13 (blobStore); SecretsPanel.tsx (secretsStore). `grep -rn "lazy("` finds no lazily loaded components, so import() cannot fail with a chunk-load error. The resets cannot throw: blobStore.ts:243-249, secretsStore.ts:59-61, shareableReviewStore.ts:246-248 and preferencesStore.ts:456 each only set state. sessionStore.ts:4716-4731 clears timers and calls set. The subscribers that reset() fires are subscriptions.ts:283-339 (isContentOnlyVersionBump at :63-71 returns false when the snapshot or state is null), :347-357 (returns early when the session id is null), :359+ (returns early when there is no validationResult), and :493+ (returns early when the session id is null). None of them throws on the reset state. The reviewer's evidence field itself says: "No throwing reset exists today, so this is hardening."

findings.title: Failed accept hydration leaves compositionStateLoaded false permanently
findings.summary: After a committed accept, acceptProposal sets compositionState=null and compositionStateLoaded=false (2443-2447). If either hydration GET fails it returns (2455-2460), and no later publication path sets compositionStateLoaded back to true: sendMessage, recompose, applyResolvedInterpretation and the guided paths all skip it. Before this window, selectSession's failure arm (2090-2099) deliberately set it true so consumers would not wait forever. The early return also skips refreshInterpretationEventsForSession, and the doc comment at 1365-1374 is now false.
findings.failure_scenario: The user accepts a proposal and the POST commits. fetchCompositionState then fails transiently (a 503 or a replica restart). The user keeps chatting. sendMessage publishes version N+1, but compositionStateLoaded stays false. GraphMiniView shows 'Loading pipeline…' over a populated pipeline, #/{id}/yaml and #/{id}/spec deep links never pass the useHashRouter gate, and interpretation reviews created by the accept (which can gate execution) do not appear until the session is re-selected.
findings.evidence: sessionStore.ts:2443-2447 sets null/false. 2455-2460 is the catch that returns without settling the flag. The only setters of compositionStateLoaded=true are 1798, 2000, 2098, 2467 and 3021 (grep). The sendMessage return object (~2257-2270) omits the flag. GraphMiniView.tsx:47-60 and useHashRouter.ts:125-165 gate on it. selectSession 2090-2099 has the comment 'Marking loaded lets deferred consumers ... resolve ... instead of waiting forever'.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep null/false on failure, because loaded=true with a null state would let ImportYamlModal.tsx:965 skip its replace confirmation. Have every path that publishes an authoritative non-null compositionState also set compositionStateLoaded: true. Move the interpretation refresh before the hydration try, or into a finally gated on isCurrent(). Update the doc comment.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this. I traced the path at 74c0ce0db and it is reachable as described. Commit 7d981d6cf or 07faf477e changed acceptProposal in this window. After a committed POST it now sets compositionState=null and compositionStateLoaded=false (sessionStore.ts:2443-2447). If either hydration GET fails, the inner catch (2455-2460) sets an error banner and returns. That leaves the flag false, and it also skips refreshInterpretationEventsForSession (2475).

Every later publisher of compositionState writes the state without setting the flag. That includes sendMessage (2253-2265), which publishes newState without compositionStateLoaded, and the setters at lines 339, 579, 899, 996, 1061, 2833, 3122, 3162, 3277, 3636, 3759, 3989, 4027, 4118, 4420, 4446, 4620 and 4653. Only createSession (1798), selectSession (2000, 2098), the accept success path (2467) and forkFromMessage (3021) set it true. So the flag stays false until the session is re-selected, created or forked.

The consumers gate on the flag. GraphMiniView.tsx:47-56 renders 'Loading pipeline…' whenever !compositionStateLoaded, even over a non-null published state. The subscriber in useHashRouter.ts:129/148 returns early while the flag is false, so the #/{id}/yaml and #/{id}/spec intents never dispatch. The flag's doc comment at sessionStore.ts:1365-1374 says it is true once the selectSession fetch settled, or once the session was created or forked. The accept path now breaks that. This is a regression: before the window, acceptProposal never touched the flag, and a hydration failure left the earlier (true) value in place.

I lowered the severity to low. It needs a transient GET failure after a committed accept. The error banner at 2458 tells the user to 'Reload the session to refresh it', and re-selecting the session through selectSession fixes everything. No data or audit is lost; the problem is a stuck UI and dead deep links until that manual reload.
verdicts.evidence:
- sessionStore.ts:2443-2447: set compositionState null, compositionStateLoaded false.
- sessionStore.ts:2455-2460: catch sets the error and returns. The flag is not reset and the interpretation refresh at 2475 is skipped.
- `grep -n compositionStateLoaded sessionStore.ts`: the only true-setters are 1798 (createSession), 2000 and 2098 (selectSession), 2467 (accept success) and 3021 (forkFromMessage).
- sessionStore.ts:2253-2265: the sendMessage return object has compositionState: newState and no flag.
- GraphMiniView.tsx:47-56: isLoading = !storeCompositionStateLoaded, which renders 'Loading pipeline…'.
- useHashRouter.ts:126-131 and 148: dispatchIfAvailable and the subscriber both bail while the flag is false.
- `git diff 7c986dc97 74c0ce0db`: the pre-window acceptProposal did not set compositionStateLoaded at all. The new null/false reset and the early-return catch came in during the window (commits 7d981d6cf and 07faf477e).
- Mitigation: the error text at 2458 tells the user to reload the session, and selectSession restores the flag.

findings.title: 409 detail dropped when conflict refresh snapshot is superseded
findings.summary: reconcileProposalConflict publishes the 409's error detail only while its own list snapshot is still current (604, 613, 614-619). acceptProposal and rejectProposal clear error at dispatch. So if any newer proposal-list read starts before the conflict refresh returns, the user gets no message.
findings.failure_scenario: Pending proposals A and B are both visible. Accept on A returns 409 'Session operation is already active'. While its refresh GET is in flight, the user confirms Reject on B, which succeeds and starts a newer snapshot. A's refresh resolves, snapshot.isCurrent() is false, and the function returns. error stays null and A's Accept re-enables silently, so the accept did nothing and the user is not told.
findings.evidence: sessionStore.ts:604 `if (!isCurrent() || !snapshot.isCurrent()) return;`. The error is set only at 613, or at 614-619 under the same guard, and is cleared at 2424-2429. The window's test 'does not let an older conflict refresh retire a proposal found by a newer read' runs exactly this sequence (409 'Busy', then a newer loadCompositionProposals) and never asserts error. Lease 409: session_operation_handlers.py:28-30. DecisionPanel.tsx:274-275 and 329-330 disable buttons per proposal only.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the error from error.detail whenever isCurrent() is true, whether or not the snapshot is still current. Keep the snapshot guard only on the compositionProposals and staleProposalIds writes. Assert error in the existing test.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this. The code at 74c0ce0db behaves as the finding says. reconcileProposalConflict, which is new in this window (commits 7d981d6cf and 07faf477e), sets error.detail only when the refresh's own snapshot is still current. The success branch returns early at sessionStore.ts:604, and the catch branch at 614-619 has the same guard. The 409 detail describes the action that failed, not the refresh read, yet it is dropped whenever any newer proposal snapshot has started. No recorded ruling covers this, and the commit message gives no rationale.

The path is reachable, but only through a narrow timing race. At the pinned tree, beginProposalSnapshot is called from four places: loadCompositionProposals (2403), accept success (2450), reject success (2548) and the conflict function itself (601). Outside tests, loadCompositionProposals is called only from the 422 branch of accept (2492). advanceGuidedPublicationGeneration also bumps the sequence, but it breaks isCurrent() as well, so it is not the snapshot-only case.

So the error is lost only when three things happen in order. First, another proposal's accept or reject POST succeeds. Second, it starts its refresh snapshot. Third, A's conflict refresh GET is still in flight at that point.

The most natural trigger is proposal B's Accept holding the session lease. The user clicks Accept on A, which returns 409 "Session operation is already active". B's POST then completes and begins its snapshot before A's GET resolves. DecisionPanel.tsx:274-275 and 329-330 disable buttons per proposal only, so A can be clicked while B is busy.

When this happens, both dispatches have already cleared error (2424-2429 for accept, 2522-2527 for reject). B's success path sets no error, and A's refresh returns at 604. A stays pending and not stale, so its Accept button re-enables with no message. That is the reported outcome.

The window is roughly one GET round-trip, and the user can simply click again, so low severity stands. The test at sessionStore.test.ts:2774 exercises this exact sequence and does not assert error, which matches the finding.
verdicts.evidence:
sessionStore.ts:604 `if (!isCurrent() || !snapshot.isCurrent()) return;` means the error at 613 is set only when the snapshot is still current. The catch branch at 614-615 has the same guard.

sessionStore.ts:1093-1096 builds the snapshot's isCurrent as `sequence === proposalSnapshotSequence`, which any later beginProposalSnapshot call makes false.

Newer snapshots start at 2450 (accept success) and 2548 (reject success). Neither path sets error on success. Their only error writes are at 2459 and 2553, and those run only when the refresh fetch fails.

Both actions clear error at dispatch: 2424-2429 (accept) and 2522-2527 (reject).

loadCompositionProposals is called outside tests only at 2492 (grep of stores/*.ts and components, excluding tests).

The DecisionPanel.tsx:274-275 isBusy check is per proposal, and the Accept button at 329 is disabled only for `isBusy || isStale`.

The backend 409 detail "Session operation is already active" comes from session_operation_handlers.py:28-30.

The test at sessionStore.test.ts:2774-2791 runs a 409 'Busy' followed by a newer loadCompositionProposals and asserts only compositionProposals and staleProposalIds, never error.

Both commits in the window that touched this file (7d981d6cf, 07faf477e) introduced reconcileProposalConflict, so the finding is diff-anchored.

findings.area: proposal actions (guided respond is the trigger; guided retiring)
findings.title: Guided respond during proposal action strands busy flag
findings.summary: The accept and reject isCurrent() checks now also fence on guidedPublicationGeneration (2416-2419, 2522-2526). Their finally blocks (2510-2518, 2575-2583) clear proposalActionPendingIds only when isCurrent() is true. respondGuided (3368), startGuided, seedGuided and chatGuided advance the generation within the same session without clearing proposalActionPendingIds, so the busy id is never removed. Before the window, the finally checked only the session id.
findings.failure_scenario: In a guided session that shows a pending proposal in DecisionPanel, the user confirms Reject and answers a guided turn before the reject POST settles. respondGuided advances the generation, so the reject's error or receipt handling and its pending cleanup are all skipped. If the proposal is still pending (for example, the reject returned a lease 409), its Accept and Reject stay disabled={isBusy} until the session is re-selected, and no error is shown.
findings.evidence: sessionStore.ts:3368 advances the generation unconditionally on each respond. The resets of proposalActionPendingIds are only at 1802, 1872, 1938, 2080, 2115, 2142 and 3025 (activation paths). DecisionPanel.tsx:329-330.
findings.suggested_fix: In the finally, clear the pending id whenever get().activeSessionId === activeSessionId, and keep the generation fence only on the publication writes. This is a local fix in the freeform store and needs no investment in the guided lane.

verdicts.reason:
I traced the claimed path at 74c0ce0db and could not refute it. Both proposal actions capture guidedPublicationGeneration. Their finally blocks now remove the busy id only when isCurrent() is true, and isCurrent() requires the generation to be unchanged. Before the window, the finally checked only the session id (commit 7d981d6cf changed `get().activeSessionId === activeSessionId` to `isCurrent()`). advanceGuidedPublicationGeneration() runs in respondGuided (3368), startGuided (3142), seedGuided (3185), chatGuided's cold-start branch (4161) and reset (4721). None of those paths clears proposalActionPendingIds. The only resets are on session activation or selection (1802, 1872, 1938, 2080, 2115, 2142, 3025). So an in-flight accept or reject that settles after a same-session guided action leaves its id in proposalActionPendingIds for good. It also skips the proposal merge and the error it would have shown, so the proposal can keep rendering as pending with both buttons disabled until the user re-selects the session.

The path is reachable. Guided sessions do carry pending composition proposals: the Step-3 and guided-full proposals, whose anchors guided_proposal_rebase.py moves. The guided branches of ChatPanel render the same DecisionPanel ({decisionPanel} at ChatPanel.tsx:2706 and 3267). The GuidedTurn widget's onSubmit calls respondGuided (ChatPanel.tsx:2999) with no gate on proposalActionPendingIds.

The severity stays low for three reasons. The race needs the user to start a guided action inside the latency window of a proposal POST. It only affects the guided lane, which is being retired. Re-selecting the session recovers it. No automatic effect advances the generation after an accept or reject: the startGuided call at ChatPanel.tsx:996 sits inside a user retry handler.
verdicts.evidence: sessionStore.ts:560-564 advanceGuidedPublicationGeneration bumps the generation (and proposalSnapshotSequence). acceptProposal: sessionStore.ts:2417-2420 is the isCurrent that includes the generation, and 2510-2518 is the finally with `if (isCurrent()) { ...filter proposalId }`. rejectProposal: the same pattern at 2523-2526 and 2575-2583. `git diff 7c986dc97 74c0ce0db` shows `-      if (get().activeSessionId === activeSessionId) {` changed to `+      if (isCurrent()) {` in that finally. `grep proposalActionPendingIds` finds the clears only at 1802/1872/1938/2080/2115/2142/3025, all activation paths. The generation advances without a clear at 3142 (startGuided), 3185 (seedGuided), 3368 (respondGuided), 4161 (chatGuided cold start) and 4721 (reset). ChatPanel.tsx:2324-2338 passes proposalActionPendingIds to DecisionPanel, and {decisionPanel} renders inside the guided branches at 2706 and 3267. ChatPanel.tsx:2999 is `onSubmit={(body) => void respondGuided(body)}` with no proposal-busy gate. DecisionPanel.tsx:275 has isBusy=proposalActionPendingIds.includes(id), and :329-330 disables Accept and Reject on isBusy. guided_proposal_rebase.py module docstring: guided settlements carry still-pending composition proposals, so they exist in guided sessions.

findings.title: Readiness type guard does not check the new required blocker `note` field
findings.summary: 6a34007fb added `note: string | null` to ValidationReadinessBlocker (TS and pydantic). isValidationReadiness in api/validationReadiness.ts:8-23 is the only admission check for /validate and audit readiness, and it was not updated. It still asserts `value is ValidationReadiness` without checking `note`.
findings.failure_scenario: A blocker arrives without a `note` key (a pre-6a34007fb backend during a mixed rollout, or any producer that drops it). The guard admits it, blocker.note is undefined, and decisionPanelRows.ts:164 copies it. DecisionPanel.tsx:230 tests `row.note !== null`, which is true, so every blocking row shows an empty 'Reviewer's note (the advisor's own words — not verified by ELSPETH):' block and claims advisor provenance for blockers the advisor never wrote. If `note` is an object, React throws 'Objects are not valid as a React child' in the chat panel.
findings.evidence: api/validationReadiness.ts:14-21 checks code/component_id/component_type/detail/suggestion only; types/index.ts:611 `note: string | null`; components/chat/decisionPanelRows.ts:164 `note: blocker.note`; components/chat/DecisionPanel.tsx:230 `{row.note !== null && (...label... {row.note})}`; backend src/elspeth/web/execution/schemas.py:262 requires note (strict model), so this is low severity.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `(typeof blocker.note === "string" || blocker.note === null)` to the per-blocker predicate in api/validationReadiness.ts. auditReadiness.ts reuses that guard, so this one change covers both paths.

verdicts.reason: The finding is correct. 6a34007fb, which is in the window, added the required `note: string | null` to the wire type and the pydantic model. It did not add a `note` check to `isValidationReadiness`, the one Tier-3 admission guard for readiness. The guard checks every other blocker field. It is the only gate on POST /validate (client.ts:1391) and on audit-readiness validation results (auditReadiness.ts:133). So its `value is ValidationReadiness` predicate asserts a field it never checks. That matches the brief's "half-wired" category exactly: a field added on one side and not validated on the other. The downstream path is real. decisionPanelRows.ts:164 copies `blocker.note` straight through. DecisionPanel.tsx:230 tests only `!== null`, so an `undefined` note renders the "Reviewer's note (the advisor's own words — not verified by ELSPETH)" label with an empty body. An object-valued note would throw during render. Severity stays low because the backend at the pinned commit cannot trigger this. ValidationReadinessBlocker at schemas.py:247-262 is a strict model and `note` has no default. Every producer (service.py, no_tool_policy.py, completion_gates.py, _validation_model.py and others) constructs that model. No readiness response path serialises with exclude_none. So the wire always carries `note`, and the trigger needs a non-conforming producer. The only one I can name is a brief mixed-replica rollover window. This is a hole in the admission guard, not a failure users can currently see.

{row.note}
