findings.title: Review-only save (advisor decision changed, graph unchanged) moves the head and orphans proposals staged in the same turn
findings.summary: Since 41aeaeac0 the send route (messages.py:845) and recompose route (compose.py:591) take the save branch when completion_gate_decision_changes() is true, even when state.version did not change. save_composition_state gives the new row version max+1 (sessions/service.py:6562), so the head row id changes. Freeform proposals are staged with base_state_id set to the pre-turn row (tool_batch.py:1647). Only guided proposals are ever re-based. accept_composition_proposal then returns a 409 proposal_base_state_changed (proposals.py:371-379), and the SPA marks the proposal stale.
findings.failure_scenario: The session is in trust_mode explicit_approve and head row S0 has a non-empty graph and a clean envelope. The user asks for a change, so the model stages proposal P with base S0 and ends the turn without a tool call. The END advisor reviews the unchanged S0 graph and blocks it. The decision differs from the prior fact, so the route saves S1 with the same graph and a new id. The user clicks Accept on P and gets a 409 saying the session state changed after the proposal was created, although they changed nothing. The same save also sets lastComposeChangedPipeline (sessionStore.ts:2216/2259), so the badge says 'Pipeline updated' and validation is cleared. For block causes other than graph_rejected (unavailable, malformed, message_rejected), the gate reviews again on the unchanged graph. Advisor detail and note text varies between runs, so a re-block with different wording saves another row and the next proposal gets the 409 too.
findings.evidence: At 74c0ce0db: messages.py:845 and compose.py:591 read `elif result.state.version != state.version or completion_gate_decision_changes(...)`. sessions/service.py:6562 computes next_version as max+1. tool_batch.py:1647 stages proposals with base_state_id=UUID(current_state_id). The only proposal.rebased writer is guided (sessions/service.py:2991, guided_proposal_rebase.py). proposals.py:371-379 is the base check. _evaluate_terminal_no_tool_advisor_gate (composer/service.py:6672+) has no exemption for turns that staged proposals. AdvisorBlockCause members are listed at advisor_decision.py:7-11. The recent-code-hints ruling allows the review-only save but does not address how pending proposals are bound to a base state.
findings.suggested_fix: On a save that only changes the review outcome, either carry pending freeform proposals' base forward (append a rebase hop), or compare the graph fingerprint rather than the row id in the accept base check. Alternatively, persist the review outcome without minting a new head row. Also have the SPA derive 'pipeline changed' from a graph change rather than from the version number.

verdicts.reason: I traced the whole path at 74c0ce0db and could not refute it. When a turn changes only the review outcome, the route saves a new head row. Freeform proposals are bound to the old head row id. Nothing in the freeform lane re-bases them, so accepting one returns a 409 even though the graph did not change. Two things in the finding go too far. First, the recent-code-hints ruling asks for a new row on a review-only save, but it says nothing about proposals that are still pending. Second, when the cause is graph_rejected there is a workaround. On the next turn, advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph skips the gate for the unchanged graph, so no new row is saved and a re-staged proposal can be accepted. That is why I lowered the severity from high to medium. For the causes that can be retried (unavailable, malformed, message_rejected), the gate reviews the graph again, so the proposal can be orphaned again.
verdicts.evidence:
Route branch: messages.py:845-847 and compose.py:591-593 take the save branch when `result.state.version != state.version or completion_gate_decision_changes(...)` is true. Both routes were added by 41aeaeac0; before that commit the check was `result.state.version != state.version` only. The prior fact is parsed from the compose base row (messages.py:216, compose.py:135).

completion_gate_decision_changes (completion_gates.py:238-248) returns True when a block fact replaces the clean or absent prior fact.

Staging a proposal leaves the state and version unchanged (tool_batch.py:1659-1661, `updated_state=state`). The proposal is still bound to the old row: tool_batch.py:1648 sets `base_state_id=UUID(current_state_id)`.

The END gate still runs on turns that staged a proposal. The terminal handler (composer/service.py:6123-6275) has no pending-proposal exemption before the gate call. Inside the gate (6672+), the only early exits are:
- the state is structurally empty;
- the pass budget is spent;
- a graph_rejected fact already covers the unchanged graph (6760);
- genuine orphans exist.

A block produces AdvisorGateBlocked with cause unavailable, malformed, message_rejected or graph_rejected (8627-8643). The result attaches that decision at 6395 via _with_advisor_gate_decision (2349).

The save mints a new row id and a new version as max+1 (sessions/service.py:6562-6571). The same insert only supersedes interpretation events and approvals. It does not touch composition proposals.

The accept check at proposals.py:370-379 compares `current_record.id != proposal.base_state_id` and raises 409 proposal_base_state_changed.

The only writer of proposal.rebased is guided (guided_proposal_rebase.py and sessions/service.py). The freeform routes have no rebase path, per grep under web/sessions/routes.

In the SPA, sessionStore.ts:593-597 adds the proposal to staleProposalIds when it receives that error.

The plan (docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md:180-186) requires 'a new persisted state id/version' on advisor-only saves. Neither the plan nor the ruling mentions pending proposals, so this is an interaction the ruling did not cover, not a ruling that the finding contradicts.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute the finding; the failure path holds at 74c0ce0db. Before the window (7c986dc97, messages.py:830) the route saved only on `result.state.version != state.version`. Commit 41aeaeac0 added `or completion_gate_decision_changes(...)` at messages.py:845 and compose.py:591. A turn that only changes the review outcome now inserts a new head row with a fresh UUID (sessions/service.py:6562-6567). Both accept paths compare the base by row id. Generic proposals return 409 `proposal_base_state_changed` (routes/composer/proposals.py:369-379). `set_pipeline` proposals fail with BASE_CONFLICT on `current_state_id != base.state_id` (pipeline_commit.py:402-404), even when the content hash matches. The END gate has no exemption for turns that staged proposals. `last_mutation_was_pending_proposal` is only an unused alias in service.py:444 and is not consulted in `_evaluate_terminal_no_tool_advisor_gate` (service.py:6672-6720). The skip applies only to a prior `graph_rejected` fact on the same graph. The advisor sees the user's message but not the pending proposals (service.py:8391-8411). So when a user asks for a change that is staged but not applied, a block on the unchanged graph is a realistic outcome, not a corner case. The recorded ruling in recent-code-hints.md (changed by 41aeaeac0) intends the new snapshot on an unchanged graph. It does not mention pending proposals, so it does not cover this effect. The test file added with the change (test_advisor_recovery_routes.py) never mentions proposals. I am lowering severity from high to medium because the impact is narrower than claimed. (1) Only explicit_approve sessions stage ordinary proposals, and the default is auto_commit (models.py:489,523). In auto_commit, `set_pipeline` settles through `route_settlement` before this branch. (2) Nothing is lost or corrupted. The SPA marks the proposal stale (sessionStore.ts:593-597), and the 409 text tells the user to ask ELSPETH to rebase, which re-stages it on the new head. That follow-up turn is usually safe: a `graph_rejected` fact on the unchanged graph makes the gate skip (`advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph`), so there is no second save. It repeats only for unavailable, malformed or message_rejected blocks whose wording differs between runs. The finding also omits a side effect: the same review-only save runs `supersede_open_approvals` (sessions/service.py:6583-6588). That retires open workflow approvals on a head change that did not change the graph.
verdicts.evidence:
- Pre-window, `git show 7c986dc97:src/elspeth/web/sessions/routes/messages.py` line 830 reads `elif result.state.version != state.version:`. At 74c0ce0db, messages.py:845-847 and compose.py:591-593 add `or completion_gate_decision_changes(prior_completion_gates_facts, result.advisor_gate_decision, result.state)`.
- completion_gates.py:238-247 returns True when an explicit decision changes the facts. Examples: clean to Blocked, Blocked to Passed, or a re-block whose detail or note differs.
- sessions/service.py:6562-6567 computes `next_version = max+1` and `allocated_state_id = state_id or str(uuid.uuid4())` (a new row id). Lines 6583-6588 also call `supersede_open_approvals`.
- tool_batch.py:1593-1599 builds `set_pipeline` proposals with `PresentBase(state_id=UUID(current_state_id), ...)`. tool_batch.py:1647 stages other proposals with `base_state_id=UUID(current_state_id)`.
- Accept path, routes/composer/proposals.py:369-379: `current_record.id != proposal.base_state_id` raises 409 `proposal_base_state_changed`.
- pipeline_commit.py:402-404: `current_state_id != authority.proposal.base.state_id` raises BASE_CONFLICT before the content-hash check.
- service.py:6716-6724 skips only when `advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph` holds. There is no check for pending proposals, and `_last_mutation_was_pending_proposal` (service.py:444) is never called in service.py.
- recent-code-hints.md (41aeaeac0 diff) says "Both routes save changed review outcomes in a new fenced snapshot even when the graph is unchanged". It says nothing about proposal bases.
- models.py:489,523 set the default trust_mode to auto_commit, so the impact is limited to explicit_approve.
- sessionStore.ts:593-597 marks the proposal stale on the 409.
- sessionStore.ts (around 2214-2259) sets `lastComposeChangedPipeline: versionChanged`, so the SPA shows the unchanged pipeline as updated.

findings.title: completion_gates format change (schema_version 2 + cause) landed without a session epoch bump
findings.summary: 539121b17 set SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH to 65 for the note key. At that commit the writer saved `completion_gates: {}` on every clean compose save. 41aeaeac0 then made parse_completion_gates require schema_version == 2 and a cause key, which makes `{}` and blocks saved without a cause invalid. The epoch stayed at 65 (models.py:358), and schema.py:37-40 still describes epoch 65 as the note change only. Epoch 62 set the convention that a JSON format change is rejected at startup through an epoch bump.
findings.failure_scenario: Take any session store stamped 65 by a release/0.8.1 build between 539121b17 and 41aeaeac0. It passes the startup epoch check (65 == 65, and the 74c0ce0db CHANGELOG says startup accepts such a store). Every session that composed once holds `completion_gates: {}`. parse_completion_gates raises a Tier-1 ValueError from messages.py:216, compose.py:135, execution/routes.py:1003, execution/service.py:1272/1800/2794, audit_readiness/service.py:564 and shareable_reviews/service.py:434. Every send, validate, execute and audit-readiness read then returns 500 for those sessions. I could not check whether such a store exists in any deployment.
findings.evidence: The 41aeaeac0 diff removes completion_gates_meta_value, which returned {} on a clean turn, and adds the version check at completion_gates.py:275 plus the cause requirement. `git log -S'SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65'` shows only 539121b17. The models.py epoch comments have no entry for 65. The recent-code-hints ruling says 'no old-format compatibility'. That covers the parser; the epoch bump is the mechanism that forces the store to be recreated.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH and _COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH to 66 together, with a comment naming the schema_version 2 + cause change. Move the literal epoch sites (tests, docs, website/get-started.html). Do not add compatibility code.

verdicts.reason: I traced the finding at the pinned commit and it holds. A session store stamped epoch 65 by release/0.8.1 at 5bcd983c9 has the same epoch and schema that 74c0ce0db accepts at startup. Its rows still hold the old completion_gates envelope: `{}` on every clean turn, and blocked facts with no schema_version or cause. The 74c0ce0db parser raises a Tier-1 ValueError on both. The raise sits outside every try on the send, compose, execute, validate, audit-readiness and shareable-review read paths. I found no guard, normaliser or recorded ruling that exempts this change from the project's epoch-bump convention. The only mitigation is that few stores are exposed. Such a store could only come from a build of release/0.8.1 in the roughly two hours between 5bcd983c9 and 23185f55a. Even so, 5bcd983c9 is on origin/release/0.8.1, and turning exactly this case into a clean startup refusal is what the epoch mechanism is for.
verdicts.evidence:
1) Epoch 65 was on the release branch without the format change. 5bcd983c9 is the 2026-09-22 22:55 merge on release/0.8.1's first-parent line, and it is on origin/release/0.8.1 (`git branch -r --contains`). It contains 539121b17, which sets models.py:358 SESSION_SCHEMA_EPOCH = 65, but not 41aeaeac0. 41aeaeac0 arrives only with 23185f55a (2026-09-23 00:55).
2) The old writer produced envelopes the new parser rejects. At 5bcd983c9, completion_gates.py:186-202 `completion_gates_meta_value` returns `{}` when there is no advisor blocker. _helpers.py:2772-2781 stores that value as `completion_gates` on every compose-preflight save. The blocked form has no schema_version and no cause.
3) The new parser rejects them. At 74c0ce0db, completion_gates.py:274-276 sets `version = raw["schema_version"] if ... else None` and raises unless it equals 2, so `{}` raises "schema_version must be 2". Lines 318-321 then require `cause`.
4) Startup does not stop such a store. `git diff --stat 5bcd983c9 74c0ce0db -- src/` touches no sessions models.py or schema.py. Epoch is still 65 at models.py:358 and schema.py:40 `_COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH = 65`. The schema.py:37-39 comment still says epoch 65 is only the note-key change. The 74c0ce0db CHANGELOG says startup accepts a database at the exact current epoch, session 65.
5) The raise escapes to the request. messages.py:212-216 parses deliberately "outside every try" so a corrupt envelope propagates. The same unguarded call appears at compose.py:135, _helpers.py:998/2760, execution/service.py:1272/1800/2794, execution/routes.py:1003, audit_readiness/service.py:564 and shareable_reviews/service.py:434.
6) No ruling covers it. The 41aeaeac0 plan says "Unversioned envelopes are rejected, including empty mappings ... Do not add migrations, compatibility branches or reset existing data". The recent-code-hints entry says "no old-format compatibility". Neither mentions the epoch. 539121b17's own message sets the precedent: a stricter Tier-1 envelope parser means "an epoch-64 store cannot be read forward", so the epoch was bumped. 41aeaeac0 tightens the same envelope further and did not bump.
Severity stays medium. The exposure is limited to stores created by release-branch builds in that roughly two-hour window, but an affected store fails on every session read with a 500 instead of being refused at startup.

findings.title: COST_UNAVAILABLE progress copy and reason updated on send_message but not on recompose
findings.summary: messages.py:656-670 branches the evidence and likely_next copy on COST_UNAVAILABLE and uses freeform_planner_progress_reason, which yields service_setup_failed. The recompose handler at compose.py:429-437 still hard-codes 'model did not return a usable pipeline plan' with reason=provider_unavailable, although its own comment says the two routes must translate identically.
findings.failure_scenario: Model pricing is not configured and the user clicks Retry, which calls recompose. The HTTP 503 body, which both routes build in _handle_planner_failure, says 'Ask an administrator to configure model pricing'. The progress snapshot the SPA renders instead blames the composer provider and invites a retry.
findings.evidence: compose.py:436 has reason="provider_unavailable" with fixed evidence text. messages.py:660 has the COST_UNAVAILABLE conditional. _helpers.py:2954 maps COST_UNAVAILABLE to service_setup_failed.
findings.suggested_fix: Have recompose use freeform_planner_progress_reason(exc.code) and the same COST_UNAVAILABLE-conditional copy, or move both into one shared helper.

verdicts.reason: The finding holds. Recompose reaches the same freeform planner as send_message and can raise PipelinePlannerError(code="COST_UNAVAILABLE"). The HTTP body for that error comes from the shared _handle_planner_failure and is the pricing-specific 503. The recompose progress event, though, still has fixed "model did not return a usable pipeline plan" wording and reason="provider_unavailable". The window commit 101824e7d added the COST_UNAVAILABLE wording to messages.py only; it did not change compose.py. The reason-attribution drift is older: messages.py started using freeform_planner_progress_reason in e300c95e35 on Aug 17, outside the window. Even so, the recompose comment says the two routes must translate "identically", and the window extended a divergence that the comment rules out. Nothing earlier in the call chain normalises or intercepts the error. Severity stays low: only the progress snapshot's wording and reason tag are wrong. The HTTP 503 body, the failure_code and the audit disposition row are all correct.

- `git show --stat 101824e7d` lists messages.py and _helpers.py but not compose.py.

findings.title: Shared readiness decoder does not check the new note field; an absent key renders an empty labelled reviewer note
findings.summary: 6a34007fb made ValidationReadinessBlocker.note required (string | null) in both pydantic and TypeScript. The shared admission check in validationReadiness.ts:15-21, used by validatePipeline and the audit-readiness decoder, never checks note. DecisionPanel.tsx:230 renders the block when row.note !== null, and undefined passes that test.
findings.failure_scenario: A readiness payload without note (or with a non-string note) passes isValidationReadiness. The decision panel then shows the "Reviewer's note (the advisor's own words — not verified by ELSPETH):" label with an empty body, or unvalidated content, instead of rejecting the shape. The backend always sends note today, so this is latent.
findings.evidence: validationReadiness.ts:15-21 checks code, component_id, component_type, detail and suggestion only. types/index.ts:611 has `note: string | null`. decisionPanelRows.ts:164 sets note: blocker.note.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `(typeof blocker.note === "string" || blocker.note === null)` to isValidationReadiness.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at 74c0ce0db, and I could not refute it. The shared decoder isValidationReadiness never checks blocker.note. Both routes that feed executionStore.validationResult go through this decoder. The first is validatePipeline in client.ts:1391. The second is the audit-readiness snapshot, which goes through isValidationResult in auditReadiness.ts:133 and then setValidationResult in useAuditReadinessSync.ts:42. No other check guards note before it is rendered. DecisionPanel.tsx:230 tests `row.note !== null`, and undefined passes that test, so the labelled reviewer-note block renders with an empty body. A non-string note, such as an object, would also get through the decoder. React would then throw when it tries to render that object as a child. This is a real case of the decoder accepting less than the producer and the wire type promise. It stays latent, and low severity is right: the backend's ValidationReadinessBlocker (schemas.py:262) is a strict pydantic model with a required `note: str | None` and no exclude_none, so the server always serialises note. docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md records no ruling that makes this decoder deliberately loose.
verdicts.evidence:
validationReadiness.ts:15-21 checks code, component_id, component_type, detail and suggestion only, not note. types/index.ts:611 declares `note: string | null`. decisionPanelRows.ts:164 passes `note: blocker.note` through unchanged. DecisionPanel.tsx:230-241: `{row.note !== null && (... "Reviewer's note (the advisor's own words — not verified by ELSPETH):" ...

{row.note}

)}`. Where validationResult is set: executionStore.ts:470-478 via api.validatePipeline, which is gated by isValidationReadiness at client.ts:1391. The other setter, executionStore.ts:508, is called from useAuditReadinessSync.ts:42 with snapshots decoded by auditReadiness.ts:133. Backend side: execution/schemas.py:262 has `note: str | None` with no default on a _StrictResponse (extra=forbid, strict), and no exclude_none serialisation touches it. Commit 6a34007fb added note to pydantic and TypeScript but did not touch validationReadiness.ts, and no commit in the window touches that file.

findings.title: cost_unavailable is sent to the freeform client but the failed row still offers Retry
findings.summary: The new freeform failure_code cost_unavailable (a 503 telling the user an administrator must fix pricing first) is threaded onto the failed message row (sessionStore.ts:2326). MessageBubble.tsx:284 hides Retry only for policy_blocked and admission_refused, so it still offers Retry for a failure that retrying cannot fix until the config changes.
findings.failure_scenario: Pricing for the composer model is missing. The user sends a message, gets the 'Ask an administrator' error, and is shown a Retry button. Each retry spends another provider call and fails the same way.
findings.evidence: _helpers.py:2894 has the cost_unavailable entry. MessageBubble.tsx:284 has the retry suppression list. MessageBubble.tsx was not touched in the window.
findings.suggested_fix: Either treat cost_unavailable as non-retryable in MessageBubble, or deliberately keep Retry and change the copy to match.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute it. I traced the path end to end at 74c0ce0db and it is reachable as described. The planner raises COST_UNAVAILABLE after the provider call. The window's change maps it to a new freeform failure_code, cost_unavailable, which returns a 503 whose text says an administrator must fix pricing. The client puts that code on the failed message row. MessageBubble still shows Retry for every code except policy_blocked and admission_refused. The commit's own runbook says repeating the request cannot repair a missing catalog entry. So the change is half-wired: the new code and its "ask an administrator" text landed, but the retry affordance was not updated. This is not a regression in retry availability. Before the window, COST_UNAVAILABLE mapped to invalid_provider_response, whose text said "Retry the request", so Retry was offered then too and matched the copy. The new text now contradicts the button. Severity stays low: it is a UX inconsistency and each retry wastes one provider call, but it does not block the user or corrupt anything.
verdicts.evidence:
- **Freeform mapping:** src/elspeth/web/sessions/routes/_helpers.py:2983-2984 maps exc.code "COST_UNAVAILABLE" to "cost_unavailable". Lines 2894-2897 return 503 with "Ask an administrator to configure or correct model pricing before trying again." Before the window, COST_UNAVAILABLE was in _FREEFORM_PLANNER_INVALID_PROVIDER_CODES (the diff removes it at about line 2861), which gave invalid_provider_response and "Retry the request."
- **Code reaches the client:** _helpers.py:3024 and 3051 put "failure_code" in the response body. frontend/src/api/client.ts:314 and 465 parse it into ApiError.failure_code.
- **Stored on the failed row:** frontend/src/stores/sessionStore.ts:2323-2326 and 2359 set local_failure_code on the failed row from any string failure_code.
- **Retry still shown:** frontend/src/components/chat/MessageBubble.tsx:284 renders the Retry button unless the code is "policy_blocked" or "admission_refused". The window did not touch this file.
- **Retry costs a call:** src/elspeth/web/composer/pipeline_planner.py:4062-4066 says cost enforcement is "intentionally post-call and pre-parse". It records the LLM call and then raises COST_UNAVAILABLE, so each retry spends a real provider call.
- **Retry cannot help:** docs/runbooks/azure-llm-composer-troubleshooting.md:61-62, added by the same fix commit 101824e7d, says "Repeating the request cannot repair a missing catalog entry."
- **Progress text agrees:** src/elspeth/web/sessions/routes/messages.py:664-667 sets likely_next to "Ask an administrator..." for COST_UNAVAILABLE, which also contradicts the Retry button.

findings.title: tutorial_live_run_failed 409 tells users to open run details the tutorial error screen does not offer; run_id is dropped

TutorialTurn4Run renders only the detail text with Retry and Back buttons.
findings.failure_scenario: A tutorial run finishes as empty or completed_with_failures with zero rows succeeded. The learner is told to open run details, but no link or affordance exists on that screen. Retry re-runs the same pipeline and hits the same outcome.
findings.evidence: tutorial_service.py:445-458. client.ts parseResponse builds ApiError without run_id. TutorialTurn4Run.tsx:365-380.
findings.suggested_fix: Either decode run_id and offer a link to the run, or change the copy so it does not point to an affordance that is not there.

verdicts.reason: I confirmed this at the pinned commit 74c0ce0db. The only change to tutorial_service.py in the window is 101824e7d. It added the 409 branch. When a run ends as `completed_with_failures` or `empty` with rows_succeeded == 0, that branch returns error_type `tutorial_live_run_failed` together with run_id, the rows_* counts and the copy "Open the run details to review row errors and source results." Nothing earlier blocks this path. It is not a cancelled run (handled at line 420), the status is an allowed completion status (line 430), and a landscape_run_id is present (line 439). A run in which every row fails, for example because every LLM call errors, reaches it. On the frontend, TutorialTurn4Run's catch handler only special-cases `tutorial_run_cancelled`. Everything else goes through formatError, which returns the bare `detail` string, and the component renders that string with just Retry and Back buttons. The frontend does not read run_id or rows_* anywhere on this path; the only runId it reads is from a successful response (line 181). So the screen tells the learner to open run details it gives them no way to reach. One point softens this but does not refute it: the learner could still leave the tutorial and look at the session's runs elsewhere, because tutorial sessions are not hidden. Retry clears the cache and runs the same pipeline again. Severity stays low: the copy is misleading and run_id is dropped, but the learner is not blocked.

{error}

` plus Retry (onRetryClick clears the cache and bumps a nonce) and Back, with no link to the run. src/elspeth/web/frontend/src/api/client.ts:243-285: parseResponse extracts a fixed set of fields, and run_id is not one of them. findings.title: Decision-only state save is invisible to the frontend readiness refresh (content-equal carry-forward)
findings.summary: 41aeaeac0 persists a new composition state row (version+1, byte-identical sources/nodes/edges/outputs/metadata) whenever completion_gate_decision_changes is true on an unchanged graph (messages.py:842-872, compose.py:588-618). The frontend assumes a content-equal version bump has identical readiness. subscriptions.ts:515-531 skips /validate, subscriptions.ts:293-316 carries the audit-readiness snapshot forward (auditReadinessStore.ts:341-372 re-keys it), and useAuditReadinessSync then projects the stale validation_result back. sessionStore.ts:2221/2802 has already called clearValidation on versionChanged, so the result is either the stale verdict or null.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) Turn 1 mutates the graph and the advisor is unavailable, so an UNAVAILABLE block is persisted on v5 and the frontend shows the blocker. Turn 2: the user says 'retry', the END gate re-reviews and gets CLEAN, and the route saves v6 with identical content and no gate. The frontend carries the v5 blocked verdict forward, so the DecisionPanel still shows 'advisory review could not be obtained' and Save for review stays withheld. If no snapshot existed, validationResult is null and Run shows 'This pipeline hasn't been validated yet'. Either way this lasts until a manual Ctrl+Shift+V or a reload. (b) v5 is clean; a question-only turn is FLAGGED on its final pass (GRAPH_REJECTED), so v6 is saved with the blocked fact. The frontend keeps the clean v5 verdict, and the advisor blocker and the new reviewer's note never render.
findings.evidence: messages.py:842-846 `elif result.state.version != state.version or completion_gate_decision_changes(...)`; sessions/service.py save_composition_state 'Version is max(existing versions for session) + 1'; lib/compositionContent.ts compares only sources/nodes/edges/outputs/metadata; subscriptions.ts:515 `const carriedVerdict = ... isContentOnlyVersionBump(...)` then `lastValidatedVersionBySession.set(sessionId, version); return;`; auditReadinessStore.ts:367 `[sessionId]: { ...cached, composition_version: toVersion }`; useAuditReadinessSync.ts:79-85 loadSnapshot early-return then projectMatchingSnapshotToExecution; audit_readiness/service.py:564 merges completion_gates into that snapshot; ExecuteButton.tsx:598 validationNotRun disables Run.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the compose/recompose response signal a review-status change, or carry a completion-gate identity in the state response. sendMessage/recompose should then force requestValidate and skip carrySnapshotForward for that bump. Do not widen compositionContentEqual's content projection, because that breaks its stated parity with composition_content_hash. Add a frontend test where a content-equal version bump changes the advisor blocker.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this finding. I traced the failure path myself at the pinned commit 74c0ce0db. The window's own plan requires what the frontend now defeats. docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md step 7 says "Return a state response for advisor-only changes so the client sees the new readiness immediately", and the Done criterion requires "GET state/readiness and revalidation agree with the just-returned result". No recorded ruling covers the frontend. The content-equal carry-forward (elspeth-986801d218, lib/compositionContent.ts:7-15) rests on a premise: a content-equal version bump "wrote nothing" that changes readiness. That premise held for guided settlement rows. 41aeaeac0 broke it by adding decision-only saves. The DecisionPanel.tsx:36-42 header still says "A compose turn that mutates nothing saves no composition-state row, so the durable completion gate cannot be rewritten by it". That comment is now stale and shows the frontend was never updated for the new save.

I lowered the severity from high to medium. The server stays authoritative: lib/compositionContent.ts:28-30 notes that execute re-runs the full preflight. So no audit, integrity or authz consequence follows. Nothing is lost, and the wrong display lasts only until a reload, a manual revalidate or the next real edit. The practical effect is still real. The user-visible purpose of 41aeaeac0 is that retrying an unchanged turn clears a transient advisor block. On the client that purpose is defeated: the stale blocker keeps Save for review withheld. In scenario (b) a new GRAPH_REJECTED block and the reviewer's note do not render.

One minor correction to the finding: the "validationResult is null" branch does not happen. When no v5 snapshot exists, carrySnapshotForward is a no-op, so useAuditReadinessSync fetches a fresh v6 snapshot and projects the correct result. The ambient hook (ArtifactWorkspaceSurface) normally caches a v5 snapshot, and in that case the stale verdict is what gets projected.
verdicts.evidence:
Backend, confirmed:
- messages.py:844-846 and compose.py:591-593 now save when `completion_gate_decision_changes(...)` is true, even though result.state.version == state.version. That save goes through _state_data_from_composer_state with the unchanged result.state, so the new row has the same content.
- completion_gates.py:238-248: a decision that differs from the prior fact returns True.
- completion_gates.py:381-398: UNAVAILABLE and message-scoped blocks are not skipped, so a retry is re-reviewed. A CLEAN result there is an AdvisorGatePassed, which clears the fact and triggers a decision-only save.

1. sessionStore.ts:2215-2222 calls clearValidation when the version changes.
2. subscriptions.ts:287-321: isContentOnlyVersionBump is true because compositionContent.ts:78-92 compares only sources, nodes, edges, outputs and metadata. carrySnapshotForward then runs.

7. ChatPanel.tsx:2024-2028 builds the DecisionPanel rows from executionStore.validationResult.
8. The only forced reloads are manual: AuditReadinessPanel.tsx:391/496 and subscriptions.ts:617.

Intent: the window's plan docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md:186 says "so the client sees the new readiness immediately", and line 190 requires readiness to agree with the returned result. The frontend's own safe-direction note, compositionContent.ts:24-27, calls a false "equal" the harmful case: "leaves a stale verdict on screen".

verdicts.reason: I traced the whole path at 74c0ce0db and could not refute it. 41aeaeac0 now saves a new composition_states row when only the advisor decision changes and the graph does not. The frontend decides whether to re-validate by comparing authored content only (sources, nodes, edges, outputs, metadata). So it treats that bump as bookkeeping: it skips /validate and carries the previous version's audit-readiness snapshot forward. That snapshot holds the old completion-gate verdict. Scenario (a) is the exact recovery path the commit adds. advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph now skips the END gate only when the cause is GRAPH_REJECTED, so an UNAVAILABLE or MALFORMED block gets a fresh review on the unchanged graph. A CLEAN result returns AdvisorGatePassed, completion_gate_decision_changes returns true, and the route saves v6 with the same content. The UI then shows the stale v5 blocker. I lowered the severity to medium for three reasons. It is a stale-UI defect, not a hole in enforcement: the execution service re-merges the durable gates at Run (execution/service.py:1547). A reload or Ctrl+Shift+V recovers. Nothing already in the window fixes it (41aeaeac0..74c0ce0db after it is docs only).
verdicts.evidence:
Backend (the save is reachable):
- messages.py:844-846 and compose.py:591-593: `elif result.state.version != state.version or completion_gate_decision_changes(...)`.
- completion_gates.py:238-248: the function returns effective != previous whenever a decision is present.
- completion_gates.py:396: `advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph` returns False for any cause other than GRAPH_REJECTED, so UNAVAILABLE, MALFORMED and MESSAGE_REJECTED get a fresh review on an unchanged graph.

Frontend (the stale verdict is carried forward):

- subscriptions.ts:292-321: when `isContentOnlyVersionBump` is true, it calls `carrySnapshotForward(v5->v6)`.

findings.title: ABSENT-preflight flagged block promises re-review 'on your next message', but it is now persisted as GRAPH_REJECTED and the next message is skipped
findings.summary: The comment at no_tool_policy.py:157-167 and _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_PUBLISHED_NOTICE rest on 'a fact persists only with a new state row, which only a mutating turn writes ... Such a block persists nothing'. 41aeaeac0 made that false: decision-only saves now persist the fact on unchanged turns. A final-pass FLAG with runtime_preflight None maps to AdvisorBlockCause.GRAPH_REJECTED (service.py:8625) and is persisted. advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph then skips the END gate on the next unchanged message. The detail (service.py:10956 notice) and the chat footer say 'run again on your next message', while the same blocker's suggestion (service.py:11388) says 'after your next pipeline change'. 41aeaeac0 deleted the matching premise from recent-code-hints but left the code comment, the copy and the test pin (_NOTICES_FOR_AN_UNCHANGED_TURN_BLOCK).
findings.failure_scenario: An unchanged, Stage-1-valid, blob-free graph means _reuse_or_recompute_runtime_preflight returns None. The user asks a question with no tools, and the advisor FLAGs on its final pass. The route saves v+1 with a GRAPH_REJECTED fact. The chat and DecisionPanel detail tell the user the review runs again on their next message. The user sends another message; the END gate is skipped (unchanged_graph_already_blocked), the block persists and the same false copy repeats. Only a pipeline edit clears it.
findings.evidence: no_tool_policy.py:163 '# GREEN/RED notices say so. A fact persists only with a new state row, which' and :168-172 UNVERIFIED_PUBLISHED_NOTICE '...validation and the advisory review run again on your next message.'; service.py:8625 flagged_final_pass -> GRAPH_REJECTED; completion_gates.py:381-398 skip for GRAPH_REJECTED; 41aeaeac0 diff of docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md removed 'the ABSENT-preflight ... family ... persists nothing, and keeps "on your next message"'; recent-code-hints ruling: 'graph rejection requires a pipeline change'.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the ABSENT family by cause, as the GREEN/RED families already are: the flagged or graph-rejected unverified notice should say 'after your next pipeline change', and the outage and message-rejected variants keep 'next message'. Correct the comment and re-pin the segment test.

verdicts.reason: I traced the full path at 74c0ce0db and could not refute it; the defect is real. On an unchanged turn, `_reuse_or_recompute_runtime_preflight` (service.py:3706-3745) returns None when there is no preview, no blob reference, and the wired graph passes Stage-1 validation. When the model answers without tools, the advisor flags on pass 1, repair-continue runs, and the advisor flags again on pass 2. That is `flagged_final_pass`. `_advisor_blocked_result` then builds `AdvisorGateBlocked` with cause GRAPH_REJECTED no matter what the preflight shape is (service.py:8621-8639). The ABSENT branch (service.py:8682-8692) publishes `_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_*` in the chat and in this turn's validation detail (service.py:10956). That copy says "validation and the advisory review run again on your next message". The result carries `advisor_gate_decision=decision` (service.py:8763). In the message route (messages.py:844-846), `completion_gate_decision_changes` returns True because the prior fact was None and the new one is Blocked. So the route saves a new state row even though the version did not change, and `resolve_completion_gate_facts` stores the fact because the fingerprint matches the same state. On the next unchanged message, `advisor_block_covers_unchanged_graph` (completion_gates.py:381-398) sees GRAPH_REJECTED with a matching fingerprint. The END gate then falls through with reason `unchanged_graph_already_blocked` (service.py:6741-6748), and no fresh review runs. The comment premise at no_tool_policy.py:163-167 ("A fact persists only with a new state row, which only a mutating turn writes ... Such a block persists nothing") is therefore false after 41aeaeac0. That commit removed the matching premise from recent-code-hints.md and replaced it with "graph rejection requires a pipeline change". It left this comment, the notice, and the test pin unchanged: `_NOTICES_FOR_AN_UNCHANGED_TURN_BLOCK` in test_no_tool_policy_segments.py:869-877 still lists `_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_PUBLISHED_NOTICE` and asserts "on your next message". The same turn contradicts itself: its suggestion (service.py:11388) says "after your next pipeline change". One overstatement in the finding: "the same false copy repeats" on the skipped turn is not quite right. The skip emits no new block notice, and the persisted fact's detail uses the default PENDING notice (service.py:11315, which says "after your next pipeline change"). So the false promise appears on the blocking turn itself, and after that the user's next message quietly gets no re-review. The core defect still stands: user-facing copy on the blocking turn promises a re-review that the gate is now built to skip. Medium severity is reasonable. The user is misdirected, but no data or authorization is at risk.
verdicts.evidence: no_tool_policy.py:160-172 (the premise 'A fact persists only with a new state row, which only a mutating turn writes'; UNVERIFIED notice '...run again on your next message.'); service.py:3744 (returns None on an unchanged, Stage-1-valid, blob-free state); service.py:6741-6748 (END gate skip); service.py:6914-6921 (the reason becomes flagged_final_pass on the last pass); service.py:8621-8639 (flagged_final_pass -> GRAPH_REJECTED, decision built before the shape split); service.py:8682-8692 (ABSENT arm publishes the unverified notice); service.py:8763 (advisor_gate_decision=decision); service.py:10956 (notice=_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_NOTICE on this turn's validation detail); service.py:11374-11388 (the suggestion says 'after your next pipeline change'); messages.py:378 (completion_gates=prior_completion_gates_facts passed into compose); messages.py:844-846, 870 (a save happens when the decision changes, even with the version unchanged); completion_gates.py:213-248 (the decision replaces the prior fact, and the changes check is True when there was no prior fact); completion_gates.py:381-398 (skips on GRAPH_REJECTED when the fingerprint matches, and the fingerprint excludes version); 41aeaeac0 diff of docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md removed 'the ABSENT-preflight ... family ... persists nothing, and keeps "on your next message"'; tests/unit/web/composer/test_no_tool_policy_segments.py:869-892 still pins the UNVERIFIED notice as 'on your next message'.

findings.title: Blocker detail and persisted gate fact claim ELSPETH withheld the composer's summary, but the END gate now publishes it
findings.summary: _advisor_signoff_blocked_wording defaults notice=_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_NOTICE, and the unverified builder passes _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_NOTICE (service.py:10956). Both are the withheld forms (…_PUBLISHED_NOTICE + ADVISOR_PROSE_WITHHELD_PUBLIC_DISCLOSURE, no_tool_policy.py:144/173). _advisor_blocked_result now fixes prose_withheld=False (service.py:8611) and publishes the model's reply, yet the flagged detail (service.py:11387) still ends 'ELSPETH withheld the composer's own summary of this exchange'. That detail is persisted in completion_gates.advisor_signoff.detail, rendered in the DecisionPanel, and drafted into the Ask button question.
findings.failure_scenario: On any rendered FLAG on a green or absent preflight, chat shows the composer's full reply with the published notice. Beside it, the DecisionPanel blocker row says ELSPETH withheld that reply, and the Ask draft repeats the false claim.
findings.evidence: service.py:11315 `notice: str = _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_NOTICE`; service.py:11387 `f"{_advisor_flagged_header(category, step_ids)} {notice}"`; service.py:8611 `prose_withheld = False`; no_tool_policy.py:128-130 ADVISOR_PROSE_WITHHELD_PUBLIC_DISCLOSURE text.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the _PUBLISHED_ notice twins into _advisor_signoff_blocked_wording for END-gate blocks, or make the notice track prose_withheld.

verdicts.reason: I traced the code at the pinned commit (74c0ce0db) and the finding holds. At service.py:8611 `_advisor_blocked_result` now sets `prose_withheld = False`, and every chat composer it calls gets that False, so the chat shows the model's reply with the published notice. The durable `detail` is built separately, at service.py:8628, by `_advisor_signoff_blocked_wording` with no `notice` argument. That falls back to the default `_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_NOTICE` (service.py:11315), which is the withheld twin: the published twin plus ADVISOR_PROSE_WITHHELD_PUBLIC_DISCLOSURE (no_tool_policy.py:144). The detail goes into `AdvisorSignoffGateFact(detail=...)`, which is persisted, and into the check/blocker. The same wording reaches the green shape through `_advisor_signoff_pending_validation`, which also uses the default notice. The absent-preflight shape, `_advisor_signoff_unverified_validation`, passes `notice=_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_NOTICE` (service.py:10956), which is also withheld + disclosure (no_tool_policy.py:173). For `flagged_final_pass` and `flagged_no_repair` without backend-authored findings, the detail is `f"{header} {notice}"`, so it ends with "ELSPETH withheld the composer's own summary of this exchange". Nothing upstream stops this: every rendered FLAG reaches that branch. On the frontend, DecisionPanel.tsx:229 renders `row.detail` word for word, and DecisionPanel.tsx:247-248 passes the same `row.detail` into the Ask draft. This is not a deliberate ruling. The branch review in the window (docs/reviews/2026-09-22-advisor-reviewer-note-final-review.md, ledger L16 and M-6) records it as a known false sentence that was escalated to the operator and left unfixed. So it is an open defect, not an approved behaviour. Severity stays low: the copy is false and contradicts the reply shown beside it, but no data or authority is affected.
verdicts.evidence: service.py:8611 `prose_withheld = False`. service.py:8628-8634 calls `_advisor_signoff_blocked_wording(...)` without `notice=`. service.py:11315 `notice: str = _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_PENDING_NOTICE`. service.py:11387-11388 returns `f"{_advisor_flagged_header(category, step_ids)} {notice}"` for flagged_final_pass / flagged_no_repair. service.py:10952-10956 passes `notice=_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_UNVERIFIED_NOTICE` on the absent-preflight path. no_tool_policy.py:128-130 is the disclosure text "ELSPETH withheld the composer's own summary of this exchange; ...". no_tool_policy.py:133-139 says the withheld form "would be false" when prose is published. no_tool_policy.py:144 and :173 define the withheld notices as `_PUBLISHED_NOTICE + " " + DISCLOSURE`. service.py:8636-8641 has `AdvisorSignoffGateFact(detail=detail, ...)`, the persisted fact. DecisionPanel.tsx:229 renders `{row.detail}`, and DecisionPanel.tsx:247-248 drafts the Ask question from `row.detail`. docs/reviews/2026-09-22-advisor-reviewer-note-final-review.md:508-521 (M-6) and :536 (L16, "FINDING escalated, not fixed") record it as a known, unresolved false sentence, not a ruling.

findings.area: control messages replayed into model context
findings.title: Unconditional model-facing disclosure says the review 'did not clear' on outage blocks where no review was obtained
findings.summary: 4e0d5d0d9 made the _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_WITHHELD_DISCLOSURE row unconditional on every terminal block, including UNAVAILABLE/MALFORMED blocks where nothing was injected. Its text (service.py:11172) opens 'The completion advisory review did not clear'. The codebase's own vocabulary (no_tool_policy.py:175-178) says that phrase is true only when the advisor rendered a verdict.
findings.failure_scenario: Both advisor passes are unavailable on turn N, so the terminal block writes the disclosure. On turn N+1 the model reads that the review 'did not clear' and may tell the user the reviewer rejected the pipeline, when it was never reviewed.
findings.evidence: service.py:6897-6907 add_message(... advisor_signoff_withheld_control_envelope(_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_WITHHELD_DISCLOSURE)) with no reason condition; service.py:11172-11178 disclosure text; no_tool_policy.py:175-178 comment on 'did not clear'.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose the disclosure wording by failure class (not cleared versus could not be obtained), keeping it fixed backend copy.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds up: an outage-only block does reach the unconditional disclosure write. The loop in the END gate (service.py:6788-6811) re-asks until `verdict.ok` or the budget runs out. After that, `terminal_block` (service.py:6819-6821) is True for `not verdict.ok`. The disclosure is then written at service.py:6895-6907 under nothing but `if session_id is not None`. That happens before `reason` is chosen as 'unavailable'/'malformed' (service.py:6914-6922). The fixed text (service.py:11172-11178) says 'The completion advisory review did not clear'. By the codebase's own definition (no_tool_policy.py:177-185), that is true only when the advisor gave a verdict. That definition is why no_tool_policy.py:186-192 has separate user-facing 'could not be obtained' notices for outages. The model-facing row never got the same split. The recorded ruling (recent-code-hints.md:80-87) requires the row to be written on every block. It says nothing about the wording, so it does not cover this.

One correction to the attribution: 4e0d5d0d9 did not introduce this relative to the window base. At 7c986dc97 the same text was already written unconditionally on every terminal block. A later commit in the window made it depend on `advisor_repair_context_introduced`, f776a8a8d deleted it, and 4e0d5d0d9 put back the base behaviour. So this is an old wording defect on lines the window touched, not a new regression.

Severity stays low. The row's working instruction is correct in both failure classes: don't assume the change was applied, check the authoritative state. The harm is limited to the model possibly describing an outage as a rejection.
verdicts.evidence: service.py:6819-6821: `terminal_block = (verdict.blocking or not verdict.ok) and (is_last_pass or ...)`, reached with an unavailable/malformed verdict once the budget is spent (comment at 6813-6816). service.py:6895-6907: `if session_id is not None:` ... `add_message(..., _ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_WITHHELD_DISCLOSURE, tool_calls=[advisor_signoff_withheld_control_envelope(...)])`, with no reason or failure_class condition. service.py:6922: the reason is picked afterwards as 'unavailable' if failure_class == 'unavailable' else 'malformed'. service.py:11172-11173: "[composer-system] The completion advisory review did not clear, so ELSPETH withheld...". no_tool_policy.py:177-185: "say the review 'did not clear', which is true only when the advisor RENDERED a verdict", followed by the unrendered counterparts at 186-192 ("could not be obtained"). tests/unit/web/composer/test_advisor_checkpoint.py:5125-5127 shows the row replaying as a user-role history message. Window history: at 7c986dc97 (`git show 7c986dc97:.../service.py`, around line 6715) the same text was written unconditionally. f776a8a8d removed the then-conditional (`if advisor_repair_context_introduced and session_id is not None`) write, and 4e0d5d0d9 restored it unconditionally. recent-code-hints.md:80-87 records 'written on EVERY block' as a ruling but does not rule on the wording for outages.

findings.title: An Azure pipeline node with no pricing model is priced from the bare deployment name, so LiteLLM uses the OpenAI rate card
findings.summary: `pricing_model = self._pricing_model or model` is the fallback added in 896b450b9 (the error path at :527 does the same). For provider=azure, `model` is the operator-chosen deployment name (derive_azure_model copies deployment_name into model). AzureLLMProvider passes pricing_model=None when the node or profile does not set it. LiteLLM resolves a bare gpt-* name to the OpenAI catalog entry, not azure/<name>. The provider is known to be Azure, but that knowledge is dropped, so routing and billing identity are conflated again on this path.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator profile has provider=azure, deployment_name=gpt-4o-mini and no pricing_model. Every row call records pricing_model='gpt-4o-mini', provider_cost_source='litellm.cost_per_token' and a cost at OpenAI rates, 10% below Azure (1M+1M tokens: 0.75 against 0.825). The record looks like an authoritative catalog calculation. With a deployment named gpt-35-turbo (Azure's canonical name), the call records not_available although azure/gpt-35-turbo is priced at 2.0.
findings.evidence: Measured calculate_missing_provider_cost with 1M prompt + 1M completion tokens: 'gpt-4o-mini' gave (0.75, 'litellm.cost_per_token'); 'azure/gpt-4o-mini' gave (0.825, ...); 'gpt-35-turbo' gave (None, 'not_available'); 'azure/gpt-35-turbo' gave (2.0, ...). Catalog: gpt-4o-mini OpenAI 1.5e-07/6e-07 vs Azure 1.65e-07/6.6e-07. azure.py passes pricing_model=self._pricing_model (None by default); config_validation.py:163-165 copies the deployment name into model.
findings.suggested_fix: In AzureLLMProvider, default the fallback pricing identity to f'azure/{deployment}' when pricing_model is unset, or leave the cost unavailable. Do not apply the generic `or model` fallback to Azure.

verdicts.reason:
The code path is real. For an Azure node with no pricing_model, llm.py:582 (and :527) prices the call from the deployment name, and at a bare name like gpt-4o-mini LiteLLM returns a cost at OpenAI rates. But the finding's central claim does not hold. Nothing shows this is the wrong rate card, and the fallback is documented, deliberate behaviour of the same commit.
(1) The OpenAI rate is not wrong for every Azure deployment. The bundled LiteLLM catalogue has `azure/global-standard/gpt-4o-mini` at 1.5e-07/6e-07, exactly the bare `gpt-4o-mini` price. The `azure/gpt-4o-mini` entry at 1.65e-07/6.6e-07 is the regional price. So the "10% below Azure" gap exists only for some deployment types. ELSPETH cannot tell which type a deployment is from its name. The suggested fix of defaulting to `azure/{deployment}` would therefore misprice every Global Standard deployment by the same 10% the other way.
(2) The design says to fall back to the routing identity and makes the operator responsible for choosing a catalogue entry. environment-variables.md (added in 896b450b9) says "Each role uses its routing identity when its pricing override is unset" and "The operator must select the catalogue entry matching the actual deployment's model and billing terms". The runbook at docs/runbooks/azure-llm-composer-troubleshooting.md:115-142 tells Azure profile operators to set `pricing_model` next to `deployment_name`. The node field description at base.py:208-215 says the same.
(3) The record is not hidden or passed off as authoritative. The identity that priced the call is written to the audit as `pricing_model` next to `provider_cost_source='litellm.cost_per_token'`. An auditor can see that it was priced as `gpt-4o-mini`.
(4) The `gpt-35-turbo` case gives `not_available`, not a wrong number. That matches the documented rule that "A missing catalogue price remains unavailable, never zero".
(5) This is not a regression. Before 896b450b9, AuditedLLMClient worked out no cost at all on this path (the diff adds `provider_cost_from_captured_usage` and the pricing fields fresh). What remains is at most a low-severity documentation or UX point: a warning when an Azure node has no pricing_model might help. It is not a correctness defect.
verdicts.evidence:
src/elspeth/plugins/infrastructure/clients/llm.py:527 and :582 use `self._pricing_model or model`. The code is reachable, because the OpenAI SDK response carries no usage.cost and no _hidden_params, so it goes on to calculate_missing_provider_cost (src/elspeth/core/llm_pricing.py:69-99, 414-517).
Catalogue lookup with the main venv's litellm (read-only):
- gpt-4o-mini: (1.5e-07, 6e-07)
- azure/gpt-4o-mini: (1.65e-07, 6.6e-07)
- azure/global-standard/gpt-4o-mini: (1.5e-07, 6e-07), identical to the bare entry
- gpt-35-turbo: None
- azure/gpt-35-turbo: (5e-07, 1.5e-06)
Documented fallback, added in 896b450b9 to docs/reference/environment-variables.md: "Each role uses its routing identity when its pricing override is unset ... The operator must select the catalogue entry matching the actual deployment's model and billing terms."
docs/runbooks/azure-llm-composer-troubleshooting.md:115-142 shows an Azure profile with `pricing_model: azure/gpt-5.6-sol` and says that missing pricing stays `not_available`.
src/elspeth/plugins/transforms/llm/base.py:208-215 describes `pricing_model` as "LiteLLM catalog identity for audit costing".
The 896b450b9 diff of llm.py shows that no provider_cost was computed on this path before, so this is a new capability, not a regression.

findings.title: Malformed or missing provider usage is reported as COST_UNAVAILABLE, which 101824e7d now shows as a pricing-configuration fault
findings.summary: The planner checks `call.provider_cost is None` (raising COST_UNAVAILABLE) before its `completion_tokens is None` MALFORMED_RESPONSE branch. core/llm_pricing.py returns the same (None, 'not_available') for an unknown catalog entry and for missing or malformed usage and cost metadata. 101824e7d took COST_UNAVAILABLE out of the invalid-provider codes and mapped it to cost_unavailable: a 503 'Ask an administrator to configure or correct model pricing', reason service_setup_failed. So an invalid provider response is now presented as the pricing case, the opposite of that commit's aim, and the MALFORMED_RESPONSE branch cannot be reached for calculated-cost providers such as Azure.
findings.failure_scenario: An Azure composer deployment has a priceable composer_pricing_model. One planner response arrives with usage absent or completion_tokens missing. The call is recorded with status SUCCESS, COST_UNAVAILABLE is raised, and the user sees 'The composer could not determine the model cost. Ask an administrator to configure or correct model pricing before trying again.' A retry would have succeeded, and before 101824e7d this case read as invalid_provider_response / 'Retry the request'.
findings.evidence: Measured provider_cost_from_response(..., pricing_model='openai/gpt-4o-2024-08-06'): full usage gave (0.00045, 'litellm.cost_per_token'); usage missing, completion_tokens missing, negative usage.cost and an unknown model all gave (None, 'not_available'). Mapping sites: sessions/routes/_helpers.py:2894 and :2983, routes/composer/guided_plan.py:307, routes/guided_operations.py:93, routes/messages.py:661-667.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the cost check, test whether usage is admissible (prompt/completion tokens present, optional counters valid) and raise MALFORMED_RESPONSE when it is not. Alternatively, have llm_pricing report a distinct 'usage invalid' reason while keeping the audit source not_available.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute the finding. At 74c0ce0db, pipeline_planner.py:4063 checks `call.provider_cost is None` and raises COST_UNAVAILABLE before the `completion_tokens is None` MALFORMED_RESPONSE branch at :4067. Both values come from the same usage object in build_llm_call_record (llm_response_parsing.py:647-684). When the response has neither usage.cost nor _hidden_params.response_cost, calculate_missing_provider_cost (core/llm_pricing.py:424-434) returns (None, not_available) for invalid optional counters, a missing pricing_model, missing prompt or completion tokens, and impossible cached or reasoning subtotals. It also returns that for an unknown catalog entry (:449-450). So malformed usage takes the COST_UNAVAILABLE path. Commit 101824e7d then removed COST_UNAVAILABLE from _FREEFORM_PLANNER_INVALID_PROVIDER_CODES and mapped it to 'cost_unavailable': a 503 with 'Ask an administrator to configure or correct model pricing', reason service_setup_failed (_helpers.py, guided_plan.py, messages.py). The call is also audited with status SUCCESS, not MALFORMED_RESPONSE. The intended semantics are pinned by test_missing_completion_token_metadata_is_audited_then_rejected (tests/unit/web/composer/test_pipeline_planner.py:5599-5618), which expects MALFORMED_RESPONSE. That test only passes when a provider cost field is present, so it does not cover the calculated-cost path, where the ordering flips the outcome. docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md has no ruling on this. The new runbook only says COST_UNAVAILABLE can involve incomplete usage; it does not say that should read as a pricing fault. I am lowering severity to low for three reasons. The path needs a Tier-3 anomaly: a successful Azure completion with usage or completion_tokens missing, together with a deployment alias LiteLLM cannot price. If LiteLLM can price the returned alias, _hidden_params.response_cost is set and the MALFORMED branch is reached. Finally, nothing is lost: the call is recorded, no content is parsed or dispatched, and the failure is a misleading user message plus a SUCCESS status on the audit row.
verdicts.evidence: pipeline_planner.py:4061-4081 (cost check at 4063 comes before the completion_tokens check at 4067; the COST_UNAVAILABLE path records `call` unchanged with status SUCCESS). core/llm_pricing.py:77-103: the calculated path is reached only when usage.cost and hidden response_cost are both absent or null. llm_pricing.py:424-434: malformed optional counters, missing prompt or completion tokens, and impossible subtotals all return (None, PROVIDER_COST_SOURCE_NOT_AVAILABLE). :449-450: an unknown catalog entry returns the same tuple. llm_response_parsing.py:647-684: build_llm_call_record takes provider_cost and completion_tokens from the same response usage. The 101824e7d diff removes "COST_UNAVAILABLE" from the invalid-provider set and adds 'cost_unavailable': (503, '...Ask an administrator to configure or correct model pricing...') plus 'COST_UNAVAILABLE': 'service_setup_failed' in sessions/routes/_helpers.py, the same mapping in routes/composer/guided_plan.py, and the pricing-admin text in routes/messages.py. tests/unit/web/composer/test_pipeline_planner.py:5599-5618 expects MALFORMED_RESPONSE for missing completion_tokens, which holds only when a provider cost field is present.

findings.title: Boolean max_tokens rejection misses the operator profile and LLM source boundaries; profile lowering converts true to 1 first
findings.summary: b97358ab6 added reject_boolean_max_tokens only to LLMConfig (transforms/llm/base.py:374) and QueryDefinition (multi_query.py:184). LLMProfileSettings.max_tokens (line 130, lax int; the adjacent temperature field gained strict=True in this window) and LLMSourceConfig.max_tokens (plugins/sources/llm/config.py:81) still turn True into 1. Web authors cannot set max_tokens because it is a private profile field, so on the web the budget always comes from the unguarded profile, and lowering hands the node an int 1.
findings.failure_scenario: ELSPETH_WEB__LLM_PROFILES='{"fast": {"provider": "openrouter", ..., "max_tokens": true}}' loads without error. Every web LLM transform and source bound to 'fast' sends a 1-token output budget. On an Azure reasoning deployment max_completion_tokens=1 is spent before any visible output, so every call reads as an empty completion.
findings.evidence: Measured on the worktree: LLMProfileSettings(..., max_tokens=True).max_tokens gives 1; lower_llm_profile_options gives executable max_tokens=1 (int); OpenRouterLLMSourceConfig(..., max_tokens=True).max_tokens gives 1. Control: OpenRouterConfig(..., max_tokens=True) raises 'max_tokens must be an integer, not a boolean'.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same mode='before' boolean rejection, or strict=True, to LLMProfileSettings.max_tokens and LLMSourceConfig.max_tokens, including the Gateway source override at sources/llm/config.py:322.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this. I checked the claimed path at 74c0ce0db, and it is reachable with nothing blocking it. b97358ab6 added the mode="before" boolean rejection only to LLMConfig (base.py:366-372) and QueryDefinition. Its commit message scopes the fix to "node and query authoring boundaries". LLMProfileSettings.max_tokens (llm_profiles.py:130) is still a lax `int | None`, while `temperature` next to it (line 131) is strict=True. On the web, settings_from_env (web/config.py) decodes ELSPETH_WEB__LLM_PROFILES with json.loads, so a JSON `true` arrives as Python True. It then goes through WebSettings(**kwargs) in lax Python mode, which turns True into 1. RuntimeLLMProfile.from_settings (llm_profiles.py:226) copies ("max_tokens", 1) into provider_options. lower_llm_profile_options (llm_profiles.py:~281) merges those options into the executable config with executable.update(profile.provider_options). By then the value is the int 1, so the LLMConfig before-validator has no bool left to reject. max_tokens is listed in LLM_PROFILE_PRIVATE_FIELDS (line 62), so an author can never supply their own value on a profiled node. The batch path, core/config.py:2718 LLMProfileSettings(**profile_dict), coerces the same way. LLMSourceConfig.max_tokens (sources/llm/config.py:81) and the Gateway override (line 322) are also lax int, and source.py:224/343 passes the value straight to the provider call. I lowered the severity from medium to low. On the profile path the input is operator-owned config, and the operator would have to type a literal `true` where a number belongs, which is a narrow typo. The finding is still real: the same class of input is rejected on the node boundary and accepted on the profile and source boundaries. The adjacent temperature field in the same model got strict=True, which shows the inconsistency. The result also fails silently: every call gets a 1-token budget instead of failing at startup.
verdicts.evidence: Measured with PYTHONPATH set to the worktree src, confirmed by elspeth.__file__ resolving to the worktree: LLMProfileSettings(provider='openrouter', model='m', credential_scope='server', credential_ref='OPENROUTER_KEY', max_tokens=True).max_tokens -> 1 <class 'int'>; RuntimeLLMProfile.from_settings('fast', p).provider_options -> {'timeout_seconds': 60.0, 'max_tokens': 1}. As a control, the same model with temperature=True raises ValidationError because temperature is strict=True at llm_profiles.py:131. Code points: llm_profiles.py:130 (lax max_tokens), :226 (copied into provider_options), :62 (max_tokens is a private field, so authors cannot override it), lower_llm_profile_options executable.update(profile.provider_options); web/config.py settings_from_env json.loads -> WebSettings(**kwargs) with no bool guard for JSON object fields; core/config.py:2718 batch path; sources/llm/config.py:81 and :322 lax max_tokens, consumed at sources/llm/source.py:224 and :343; b97358ab6 touched only transforms/llm/base.py and multi_query.py plus one test file.

findings.title: The docs say pricing_model records the effective billing identity, but it is recorded even when it did not price the call
findings.summary: ComposerLLMCall.pricing_model (always set by build_llm_call_record, llm_response_parsing.py:669) and LLMCallResponse.pricing_model (clients/llm.py:582, gateway.py:746, openrouter.py:529) record the configured or fallback identity whatever provider_cost_source is. When the cost came from response_usage.cost or _hidden_params.response_cost, the provider or LiteLLM priced it under an identity ELSPETH never saw.
findings.failure_scenario: An auditor sees pricing_model='azure/gpt-5.6-sol' next to a cost with source '_hidden_params.response_cost' and, following the doc, concludes the cost reflects that catalog entry. It was priced from LiteLLM's own routing or returned-model identity.
findings.evidence: The doc line was added in 896b450b9. llm_pricing.provider_cost_from_captured_usage returns response_usage.cost or hidden response_cost without consulting pricing_model (lines 78-79, 96-101). contracts/composer_llm_audit.py:174 correctly says 'configured for fallback pricing'.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the doc: pricing_model is the identity used only when provider_cost_source == 'litellm.cost_per_token'. Or record pricing_model only for that source.

verdicts.reason: The code facts in the finding are right, but they do not make the doc false. At commit 74c0ce0db, `pricing_model` is always recorded (llm_response_parsing.py:669). It is ignored when `response_usage.cost` or the hidden `response_cost` is present (llm_pricing.py:78-79, 96-101). The finding reads 'effective billing identity' as 'the identity that priced this call'. The project does not use the term that way. Commit 896b450b9, which added the doc line, is titled 'separate routing and billing model identities'. There, 'billing identity' means the pricing identity the operator configured, as opposed to the routing identity. The runbook uses the term the same way. 'Effective' refers to how that identity is resolved: the override if it is set, otherwise the routing identity. The next doc sentence says exactly that, and it matches what the code records (`pricing_model if not None else model_requested`). The same paragraph also says, just before the cited clause, that these settings 'affect fallback cost calculation only'. So the doc limits the identity to fallback pricing. It does not claim the identity priced provider-reported costs. The finding's auditor also sees `provider_cost_source` recorded next to `pricing_model`, and that field says which source priced the call. An auditor would have to ignore both the doc's own limiting clause and the recorded source to reach the wrong conclusion. That makes this a possible wording improvement at most, not a stale doc that misstates behaviour.
verdicts.evidence: docs/reference/environment-variables.md:207-210: 'These optional settings affect fallback cost calculation only; routing names and requested/returned model audit fields are preserved, and `pricing_model` records the effective billing identity. Each role uses its routing identity when its pricing override is unset.' src/elspeth/web/composer/llm_response_parsing.py:669: `pricing_model=pricing_model if pricing_model is not None else model_requested`. Code check confirmed: src/elspeth/core/llm_pricing.py:78-79 and 96-101 return provider or hidden cost without using pricing_model; the result carries a distinct provider_cost_source. What the term means in this project: commit 896b450b9 'feat(llm): separate routing and billing model identities'; docs/runbooks/azure-llm-composer-troubleshooting.md:115 '## Execution model and billing identity' and :135 'cannot override its private billing identity' (both mean the configured pricing identity); docs/reference/configuration.md:1055 'LiteLLM catalogue identity used for cost calculation'. src/elspeth/contracts/composer_llm_audit.py:174 'Catalog identity configured for fallback pricing' agrees with this reading and does not contradict the doc.

findings.area: composer Stage-1 probe / source data-contract demand
findings.title: azure_ai_search cannot be built from authored options, so Stage-1 treats it as guaranteeing nothing and the source data-contract demand is empty
findings.summary: The window made azure_ai_search operator-profiled (line 92) and it is a known pass-through (line 88). prepare_validation_probe_options (web/composer/_validation_probe.py:66) supplies inert private bindings only for plugin=='llm'. Probing the authored azure node therefore fails with 'endpoint: Field required; profile: Extra inputs are not permitted'. _effective_producer_vote_uncached (state.py:4984-5049) then fails closed to (True, frozenset()). Everything that uses authored-state Stage-1 math sees zero guarantees behind the azure node. That includes the source_data_contract demand backtrace (interpretation_state.py:1428-1459; tools/sessions.py:2516; sessions/pending_interpretation.py:605).
findings.failure_scenario: Web RAG pipeline: uploaded CSV (observed schema) -> azure_ai_search(profile, index, query_field=question, output_prefix=policy) -> llm/passthrough requiring [question, policy__rag_context] -> sink. Profile-aware validation of the executable state reports 'question' missing on the rag->consumer edge. current_source_data_contract_demand on the AUTHORED state returns (), where the lowered state gives ('question',). The pending-site enumerator never offers the source_data_contract card, and request_interpretation_review(user_term='source_data_contract') is refused with 'missing pending source_data_contract review site'. The planner cannot clear the error through the flow the skill teaches. The cheap Stage-1 gate at composer/service.py:3733 also sees the state as invalid on every prose turn and pays a full runtime preflight each time.
findings.evidence:
Executed read-only with PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src (elspeth.__file__ pointed into the worktree), PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, cwd in the scratch dir.
- Authored options: create_transform raised ValueError 'Invalid configuration for transform azure_ai_search: endpoint: Field required; profile: Extra inputs are not permitted'.
- Authored state.validate(): is_valid=False; schema_contract_violation 'Producer (azure_ai_search) guarantees: [(none)]. Missing fields: [policy__rag_context, question]'; plus a high contract_probe_failed warning.
- Lowered options (profile removed, endpoint and use_managed_identity injected): constructs, with guarantees {policy__rag_context, policy__rag_score, policy__rag_count, policy__rag_sources}; the edge is satisfied when the source guarantees question.
- current_source_data_contract_demand: authored=(), lowered=('question',).
- Known class: elspeth-bc527113e7 'Stage-1 constructor probes fail for every operator-profiled plugin' (docs/reviews/2026-09-22-p1-triage.md:703); recent-code-hints.md:1594-1607 says to prove binding-independence before adding a stub for another profiled plugin.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an azure_ai_search arm to prepare_validation_probe_options that drops 'profile' and injects an inert https *.search.windows.net endpoint with use_managed_identity=True. This is sound because the output contract does not depend on the binding: the endpoint is used only in _build_searcher at on_start. Alternatively, fix the class under elspeth-bc527113e7.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this. azure_ai_search was added entirely inside the window (commit 2b897a957, new file) and is marked both passes_through_input=True (line 88) and OPERATOR_PROFILED (line 92). On the web, the options an author writes go through the public schema at plugin_policy/profiles.py:1185-1260. That schema requires 'profile', hides the private binding fields, and sets additionalProperties=False, so the node stored in composer state carries 'profile' and no 'endpoint'. The profile is swapped for the real endpoint and credentials only later, when validation lowers it (plugin_policy/validation.py:516/779). prepare_validation_probe_options (_validation_probe.py:66) fills in stand-in bindings only when plugin=='llm', so an azure_ai_search node reaches the constructor unchanged and the constructor rejects it. The rejection starts with the transform config-error prefix, so _is_config_probe_exception (state.py:2004) accepts it as a config-probe failure. Because azure_ai_search is in _known_pass_through_plugins() (state.py:4736-4752), _effective_producer_vote_uncached returns (True, frozenset()) at state.py:5046-5047 and adds a high contract_probe_failed warning, so the authored state sees no fields guaranteed past the azure node. backtraced_source_demand (source_demand.py:199-270) stamps only sources. A field missing behind the azure node therefore stays missing when the source is stamped too, and the demand comes back as (). That empties the source_data_contract demand used by the site enumerator and by request_interpretation_review (tools/sessions.py:2498-2515; pending_interpretation.py:605-607). The recorded ruling (recent-code-hints.md:1591-1607) asks for proof that the output contract does not depend on the binding before a stub is added, and it points to elspeth-bc527113e7 as the tracker. It does not say a new profiled pass-through plugin may ship broken. The window added a new plugin to a class that is already known to be broken.
verdicts.evidence:
I ran this read-only with the worktree first on PYTHONPATH (elspeth.__file__ = worktree/src/elspeth/__init__.py) and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.
- Authored options: I passed {profile, index, query_field=question, output_prefix=policy, schema observed} through prepare_validation_probe_options(plugin='azure_ai_search'). They came back unchanged, still including 'profile'. create_transform then raised: ValueError "Invalid configuration for transform 'azure_ai_search': endpoint: Field required; profile: Extra inputs are not permitted".

- Known class and ruling: docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md:1591-1607 and docs/reviews/2026-09-22-p1-triage.md:703 (elspeth-bc527113e7).
