findings.title: actor='composer-llm' still written for server-route surfaces and sealed into arguments_hash when review is disabled
findings.summary: 889913b1a made LLM provenance follow the new surface_origin, which is NULL for state_revert, yaml_import and e2e_seed. The pending/auto-bake row insert still hardcodes actor='composer-llm' (repository.py:1256), and the review-disabled hash domain binds actor='composer-llm' (pending_interpretation.py:2089). The create_pending docstring (service.py:8599-8601) still says the sentinel means the composer LLM created the row. The contract and TS docstrings for the surface-specific opt-out shape (composer_interpretation.py:257-260, 280-285; types/interpretation.ts:147-155) still promise full LLM provenance.
findings.failure_scenario: The user opts out of reviews, then reverts to an older state (POST state/revert) or imports YAML whose llm node carries a pending prompt review. surface_pending_interpretation_reviews_for_state(surface_origin=STATE_REVERT, provenance None) → plan() takes the review_disabled branch → an auto_interpreted_opt_out row is born resolved with surface_origin='state_revert', model_identifier NULL, actor='composer-llm', and an arguments_hash computed over actor='composer-llm'. The row is immutable, so an audit record permanently attributes a server-route surface to the composer LLM. That is the same false-label class the commit removed from the provenance columns. Pending server-route rows also expose actor='composer-llm' on the wire until resolved.
findings.evidence: repository.py:1256 and :1267 (surface_origin added beside the untouched actor literal); pending_interpretation.py:2079-2094; service.py:8572 (surface_origin param added in window) vs docstring 8599-8601; routes/composer/state.py:143-154. recent-code-hints.md has no ruling on actor/composer-llm/surface_origin.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the pending-row actor from surface_origin (e.g. system:state_revert, or the requesting user) and bind that same value in the review-disabled hash domain. Update the three docstrings.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this. I traced the path end to end at 74c0ce0db, and nothing on it rejects or normalises a server-route surface on a session with reviews turned off.

1. The revert route (routes/composer/state.py:143-154) takes a COMPOSE lease, so the operation-kind fence in the pending-row writer (sessions/service.py:8614-8619) accepts it. It then calls surface_pending_interpretation_reviews_for_state with surface_origin=STATE_REVERT and all four provenance fields None. The YAML import (state.py:955) and E2E seed (state.py:1134) routes do the same.
2. That call reaches _auto_surface_prompt_template_reviews_for_state (composer/service.py:1939). It passes the NULL provenance straight to create_pending_interpretation_event and never checks whether reviews are off.
3. repository.py:1090 reads sessions.interpretation_review_disabled, and the planner (pending_interpretation.py:2071-2094) then takes the review-disabled branch. There it builds the v2 hash domain with a hardcoded actor="composer-llm".
4. The repository's check on an OPTED_OUT decision (repository.py:1195-1215) looks only at choice, hash shape and the appended state. It never checks surface_origin or actor. The insert at repository.py:1256 then writes actor="composer-llm" next to surface_origin=command.surface_origin.value (:1267) and NULL provenance.

A test in the window runs exactly this path. tests/unit/web/sessions/test_routes.py:8717 opts out as actor="user:alice", then POSTs state/yaml with an llm node and asserts that no pending rows remain. So the import did write auto-resolved opt-out rows, and each one says actor='composer-llm' although no LLM was consulted.

The contract defines actor as "user identity at resolution" (composer_interpretation.py:304). The create_pending docstring (service.py:8599-8601) says the sentinel means "created by the composer LLM". The contract's surface-specific opt-out text (composer_interpretation.py:280-285) and types/interpretation.ts:147-155 still describe a row the LLM wrote with "full LLM provenance". All three contradict what the server-route path writes. I found no ruling on actor or surface_origin in recent-code-hints.md, and no CHECK constraint on this table's actor column (the only actor CHECKs in models.py are on the guided_operation tables, lines 1029 and 1253).

Why severity is low rather than medium:
- The same row records surface_origin='state_revert' or 'yaml_import' truthfully and has NULL provenance, so a reader of the full row can still tell what raised it.
- The actor literal was not changed in this window; it predates 889913b1a (diff_anchored=false is correct).
- Nothing reads actor to make a decision, and the frontend has no decoder that checks it. The harm is a misleading sentinel sealed into an immutable hash, plus stale docstrings, with no wrong control-flow outcome.
verdicts.evidence:
- repository.py:1256 writes actor="composer-llm" and :1267 writes surface_origin=command.surface_origin.value on the same insert. The OPTED_OUT check at :1195-1215 never looks at surface_origin or actor.
- pending_interpretation.py:2071 returns early only when reviews are on. When they are off, :2079-2094 builds _interpretation_hash_domain_v2 with actor="composer-llm".
- composer/service.py:1939-1952 passes surface_origin and the None provenance to create_pending_interpretation_event and never checks whether reviews are off.
- routes/composer/state.py:143-154 is the STATE_REVERT caller. It runs under a COMPOSE lease, which the fence at sessions/service.py:8614-8619 accepts.
- tests/unit/web/sessions/test_routes.py:8717-8763: the opt-out is recorded with actor="user:alice", then the YAML import auto-resolves every surface (pending list is empty).
- Stale docs: sessions/service.py:8599-8601; contracts/composer_interpretation.py:280-285 (contradicted by :251-253 and the enum docstring at :85-102); frontend/src/types/interpretation.ts:147-155 ("full LLM provenance").
- composer_interpretation.py:304 defines the field as actor: str  # user identity at resolution.
- No actor, composer-llm or surface_origin ruling in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md.

findings.title: Inline-compose-receipt preservation and addPendingEvent guard defend a path with no production caller
findings.summary: The window added loops in refreshPending (291-294) and refreshAll (379-383) that preserve 'inline compose receipts received after the GET began', plus an opted-out/terminal guard in addPendingEvent (543-553), whose comment says it 'exists for inline-add from the compose-loop response path'. Neither addPendingEvent nor refreshPending has a non-test caller, at the window base or at the tip.
findings.failure_scenario: No runtime misbehaviour. In production, pendingBySession changes between a refreshAll start and its landing only through resolveEvent (removes), optOut (clears) or a newer refreshAll (whose token supersedes). The preservation branch therefore never fires, and the comments describe a delivery path that does not exist. A maintainer who relies on them could assume compose responses push review cards inline when they only arrive via refreshAll.
findings.evidence: git grep 'addPendingEvent|refreshPending' over src/elspeth/web/frontend/src at 7c986dc97 and 74c0ce0db: only the store and four test files match. All production refreshes are refreshAll: sessionStore.ts:736/2064/3056/3735, executionStore.ts:485.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire the compose response into addPendingEvent or delete the preservation branches and correct the comments.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this. I traced the code at the pinned commit and it matches the finding. addPendingEvent and refreshPending have no production caller, either at the window base or at the tip. Every production refresh goes through refreshAll. In production, pendingBySession[sid] changes between the start and the landing of a refreshAll in only four ways, and none of them can trigger the "preserve inline compose receipts" branch (`pendingAtStart[id] !== event`). So the new preservation loops (292-294, 381-383) and the new optedOut/terminal guard in addPendingEvent (547-552) only defend a path that tests exercise. One correction to the finding: the comment "exists for inline-add from the compose-loop response path" was already there at the base (7c986dc97:453-455). The window added the guard and the preservation loops underneath it, and wrote a new comment at 379-380 that describes the same delivery path, which does not exist. Nothing misbehaves at runtime, so the severity stays low.
verdicts.evidence:
Caller search: `git grep -nE 'addPendingEvent|refreshPending'` over src/elspeth/web/frontend/src at 7c986dc97 and at 74c0ce0db. Outside the store, it matches only test files: ChatPanel.test.tsx, useInterpretationResolver.test.tsx, interpretationEventsStore.test.ts, and, at the tip only, test/interpretationConflict.integration.test.tsx:55. Production refreshes all call refreshAll: sessionStore.ts:736, 2064, 3056 and 3735, and executionStore.ts:485.

Every production writer of pendingBySession, checked against the preservation branch:
(1) resolveEvent (interpretationEventsStore.ts:444-452) copies the surviving entries by reference and deletes the one it resolved. Surviving entries keep their identity, so `pendingAtStart[id] !== event` is false for all of them.
(2) optOut (line 532) sets the session to {}, so the loop has nothing to iterate.
(3) A newer refreshAll replaces the request token, so the older one hits `refreshRequestBySession[sid] !== request` and returns state unchanged (line 354).
(4) authStore.ts:116 resets the store with `setState(getInitialState(), true)`, which clears refreshRequestBySession, so the token check rejects the in-flight refresh.

The branch could only fire through addPendingEvent (lines 543-561), which only tests call. Window provenance: a single commit, 7d981d6cf "fix(composer): preserve decision state across delayed responses", added the preservation loops and the guard. The comment it sits under was already at base lines 453-455.

findings.title: completion_gates grammar v2 (schema_version + cause) shipped without a session epoch bump
findings.summary: 41aeaeac0 made parse_completion_gates require schema_version==2 and a cause, but _COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH stayed 65 (sessions/schema.py:40). The only bump in the window, 539121b17, was for the note key. Epoch-65 stores written by the previous grammar (unversioned `{}` on every clean compose turn, blocked facts without cause) pass startup and then fail as Tier-1 corruption.
findings.failure_scenario: A session DB is created at epoch 65 on a tree in 539121b17..41aeaeac0^ (release/0.8.1 first-parent 5bcd983c9..23185f55a^) and the service is then upgraded to 74c0ce0db. Startup accepts the exact epoch, as the CHANGELOG says. For any session whose current state row was compose-saved (envelope `{}`): POST /execute gets CompletionGateIntegrityError → 500 completion_gate_integrity_failure (service.py:1799-1805). /validate fails the same way (service.py:1272). A chat send fails with an unhandled 500 at messages.py:216. The user can neither run nor compose. Whether such a store exists is not measured.
findings.evidence: `git show 41aeaeac0^:src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py` has `return {}` at lines 199/202/234 and no schema_version. At HEAD, completion_gates.py:274-276 raises 'schema_version must be 2' and 309-316 require cause. `_COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH = 65` at both 41aeaeac0^ and HEAD; `git log -S` shows only 539121b17 bumped it. The recent-code-hints ruling says 'no old-format compatibility is provided'. CHANGELOG (74c0ce0db) says epoch 65 is accepted as is.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump the session schema epoch (and its coupled literal sites) with the grammar change, or document that epoch-65 stores created before 23185f55a must be recreated.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute the code path. 41aeaeac0 made the persisted completion_gates grammar strictly incompatible with the old one: schema_version must be 2 and cause is now required. It did not bump the session epoch, which stayed at 65. The first-parent release/0.8.1 commits 5bcd983c9, 7a0c3172d, df9c76ec7 and 44e13a82e all run at epoch 65 with the old writer, which persists an unversioned `{}` on every clean compose turn and blocked facts with no cause. A store created on any of those trees passes the exact-epoch startup check at 74c0ce0db, then fails the Tier-1 parse as soon as a session's current state row carries an old envelope. Nothing normalises the envelope before parse. The execute and validate paths wrap the ValueError into CompletionGateIntegrityError. The chat send, compose and recovery paths let it propagate.

The ruling in recent-code-hints ("no old-format compatibility is provided") rules out compatibility code, not the epoch bump. The project's own practice ties strict-grammar breaks to an epoch bump so that startup refuses the store: 539121b17 bumped 64 to 65 for exactly this reason (the note key), and test_epoch_61_is_rejected_before_reading_old_advisor_gate_grammar pins the pattern. The 74c0ce0db CHANGELOG edit only requires recreating stores below epoch 65, so it does not cover the gap stores. That makes this a real enforcement gap, not a recorded ruling.

I lowered the severity from high to medium. The exposure window is about 10 hours of local, unpushed commits (539121b17 at 09-22 14:38 through 23185f55a at 09-23 00:55) on pre-release software. Whether any such epoch-65 store exists is unmeasured, and each affected session fails loudly. Nothing corrupts silently.
verdicts.evidence:
- **Pinned HEAD grammar:** src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py:273-276 reads `raw["schema_version"] if "schema_version" in raw else None` and raises "Tier 1: completion_gates.schema_version must be 2". Lines 309-315 require a `cause` string that parses as AdvisorBlockCause.
- **Old grammar at 41aeaeac0^ and at 5bcd983c9:** `git show 5bcd983c9:src/elspeth/web/execution/completion_gates.py | grep -n 'return {}\|schema_version'` gives `return {}` at lines 199, 202 and 234, and no schema_version. `git diff 41aeaeac0^ 5bcd983c9 -- completion_gates.py` is empty.
- **Epoch per first-parent merge:** b99f0198d=64, a11a564fe=64, 5bcd983c9=65 (old grammar), 23185f55a=65 (new grammar; its second parent is 41aeaeac0). `git log 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db -- src/elspeth/web/sessions/schema.py` lists only 539121b17 as touching the epoch.
- **Stale comment:** schema.py:36-40 still says epoch 65 exists only for the note key.
- **Uncaught call sites of parse at HEAD:** execution/service.py:1272 and 1800 (wrapped into CompletionGateIntegrityError), sessions/routes/messages.py:216 (chat send, outside any try by design), sessions/routes/composer/compose.py:135, sessions/routes/_helpers.py:998 and 2760, audit_readiness/service.py:564, shareable_reviews/service.py:434, execution/service.py:2794.
- **Precedent:** the 539121b17 message says "the Tier-1 parser refuses an envelope written without it, so an epoch-64 store cannot be read forward. Pre-1.0 policy: the store is recreated". 41aeaeac0 edited tests/unit/web/sessions/test_schema.py:536-541 to expect "schema_version must be 2" in the "rejected before reading old grammar" test, but did not bump the epoch.
- **CHANGELOG at 74c0ce0db:** "Session databases below epoch 65 ... must be recreated. Startup accepts ... the exact current schema epoch (session 65 ...)". It does not cover epoch-65 stores written before 23185f55a.
- **Severity basis:** 539121b17 is dated 2026-09-22 14:38 and 23185f55a is dated 2026-09-23 00:55. Project memory says these merges were local and not pushed. Nobody has measured whether such a store exists.

verdicts.reason:
The mechanics are right. At HEAD, parse_completion_gates rejects an unversioned or cause-less envelope, and the pre-41aeaeac0 writer emitted `{}`. The failure is still not a real defect. It follows a recorded operator ruling, and no published build can reach it.

(1) Recorded ruling: the implementation plan for 41aeaeac0 records the operator's explicit decision to reject old-format envelopes, including empty mappings. It also rules out migrations, compatibility branches and resetting existing data. An epoch bump would force exactly that store reset. The recent-code-hints entry added in the same commit repeats "no old-format compatibility is provided".

(2) Unreachable for any published tree: the remote-tracking reflog shows origin/release/0.8.1 moved from fe01ad94b, where the epoch is 64, straight to 9fce3b2c6. That later push already contains 23185f55a, the merge that brought in the v2 grammar. So no pushed or released commit ever paired epoch 65 with the old writer. Every published predecessor has epoch 64 or lower (0.8.0 has 53), and startup refuses those.

The only store that could be hit is one built from an unpublished local commit during the roughly 2-hour window when the old grammar sat on local release/0.8.1 at epoch 65 (5bcd983c9 at 22:55 to 23185f55a at 00:55). If it hit, it would fail loudly, as ruled. The plan's rollback section already covers such a store with an explicitly approved development-store reset.

The new writer is self-consistent: both writer paths emit schema_version 2, so a fresh store at 74c0ce0db does not reject its own rows. At most a documentation nit remains. The runbook's epoch-65 paragraph mentions only the note key, not the v2 envelope with a cause.
verdicts.evidence:
- docs/plans/2026-09-22-advisor-transient-failure-recovery.md:17: "No database reset, signing, deployment or external publication is authorized. Subsequent explicit ruling: pre-release, no backwards compatibility; old-format gate envelopes must fail validation."
- Same plan, line 111: "Unversioned envelopes are rejected, including empty mappings... Do not add migrations, compatibility branches or reset existing data as part of implementation."
- Same plan, line 264: the rollback path is "an explicitly approved development-store reset".
- docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md, entry dated 2026-09-22, edited in 41aeaeac0: "Gate envelopes require schema version 2 and a cause; no old-format compatibility is provided."
- `git reflog show refs/remotes/origin/release/0.8.1`: "fe01ad94b ...@{2026-09-22 09:35} update by push" is followed directly by "9fce3b2c6 ...@{2026-09-23 05:46} update by push".
- `merge-base --is-ancestor 23185f55a 9fce3b2c6` prints yes.
- fe01ad94b:src/elspeth/web/sessions/schema.py:37 sets `_COORDINATION_HARD_CUT_EPOCH = 64`; dae99bb69 (release 0.8.0) sets it to 53.
- First-parent merge times: 5bcd983c9 at 2026-09-22 22:55, 23185f55a at 2026-09-23 00:55.
- New writer: completion_gates.py:199 returns {"schema_version": 2} and :201 writes schema_version 2 on a blocked fact. _helpers.py:997-998 and :2763 send every save through completion_gates_meta_from_facts, so fresh v2 stores are consistent.
- Parser at completion_gates.py:274-276 (version) and :309-316 (cause) confirms the mechanics the finding describes.

findings.title: Poll-path live-run attach seeds progress 'pending', and Run gates only check 'running'
findings.summary: attachLiveRunIfUnattached now runs from the 3s loadRuns poll (line 921) and seeds progress.status from liveRun.status, which can be 'pending'. ExecuteButton canExecute (ExecuteButton.tsx:587), primaryRunBlockReason and CommandPalette (line 124) block only on status === 'running'. For a run started elsewhere, Run stays enabled during the backend's pending phase.
findings.failure_scenario: Another tab, an agent or the API starts a run. The backend creates it as pending and flips it to running only at service.py:3485, after settings, YAML and graph/plugin build. This tab's Run-tab poll attaches with status 'pending' while execution_ready is true, so Run is enabled with no block reason. The click POSTs /execute and gets a 409 (run_already_active or a session-operation conflict).
findings.evidence: executionStore.ts:960-990 (new attach, `status: liveRun.status`); ExecuteButton.tsx:587 `progress?.status !== "running"`; ExecuteButton primaryRunBlockReason progressRunning is `=== "running"`; service.py:3480-3487 is the pending→running transition.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate Run on progress being live (not isTerminalRunStatus) instead of === 'running'.

verdicts.reason: The mechanics check out. At 74c0ce0db, attachLiveRunIfUnattached (executionStore.ts:960-989) seeds `progress.status: liveRun.status`, and that value can be "pending". The loadRuns poll (line 921) now calls it. The Run gates only test "running": ExecuteButton.tsx:587 and :595, and CommandPalette.tsx:124. So while the backend still has the run pending (service.py:3460-3487 builds the graph and preflights sinks before update_run_status("running")), Run is enabled with no block reason. I can't refute that. But the finding overstates it in two ways. (1) It is not a regression from this window. At base 7c986dc97, rehydrateActiveRun already seeded `status: liveRun.status` with pending included (base executionStore.ts:958-977), and ExecuteButton already gated on `!== "running"` (base :580, :588). Also, before 60baa12ad a run started from another tab, an agent or the API was never attached by the poll, so Run stayed enabled for that run's whole pending AND running life. The change shortens how long Run is wrongly enabled; it does not create the problem. diff_anchored=true is only loosely true: the gate mismatch predates the window. (2) The result is harmless. execute() handles a 409 with error_type run_already_active by showing "A run is already in progress for this pipeline." (executionStore.ts:617-624). The backend refuses the second run, so no duplicate run and no audit problem. Once the backend flips to running and the WebSocket or poll updates progress, the gate closes. What remains is a small UI inconsistency: ArtifactWorkspace.tsx:265 treats pending as live and the Run gates do not. It is real, but low severity, not medium.
verdicts.evidence: executionStore.ts:921 `get().attachLiveRunIfUnattached(sessionId, runs)` (new in 60baa12ad); executionStore.ts:961-963 finds a pending or running run; executionStore.ts:985 `status: liveRun.status`; ExecuteButton.tsx:587 `progress?.status !== "running"` and :595 `progressRunning: progress?.status === "running"`; CommandPalette.tsx:124 has the same check. Base 7c986dc97: executionStore.ts:958-977 rehydrate already seeded pending, and ExecuteButton.tsx:580/588 already had the running-only gate, so this is pre-existing. execute() at executionStore.ts:617-624 maps 409 run_already_active to a clear message. Own-tab execute() seeds `status: "running"` (executionStore.ts:562), so the pending gap only affects attached runs. ArtifactWorkspace.tsx:265 treats pending as live, which shows the inconsistency. service.py:3470-3487 is where the backend moves pending to running, after build_validated_runtime_graph and preflight_runtime_sink_effects.

findings.title: composerBusy gate added only to the REQUEST_RUN_EVENT owner, so other Run surfaces become silent dead controls
findings.summary: 5623ceb6d added !composerBusy to ExecuteButton's canExecute. CommandPalette 'Execute pipeline' (CommandPalette.tsx:120-125), Ctrl+E (App.tsx:551-563) and the InlineRunResults 'Run pipeline' button (InlineRunResults.tsx:389) still gate only on execution_ready. They dispatch REQUEST_RUN_EVENT, which handleRunClick drops on !canExecute. This breaks InlineRunResults' own rule against silent dead controls.
findings.failure_scenario: While the composer is thinking with execution_ready true, the Run tab shows an enabled 'Run pipeline' button (or the palette shows Execute enabled). Clicking does nothing and that surface gives no reason. The backend is consistent: exclusive COMPOSE/EXECUTE leases give a 409 'Session operation is already active'.
findings.evidence: ExecuteButton.tsx:582-588 and handleRunClick `if (!canExecute ...) return`; InlineRunResults.tsx:380-400 comment and executionReady-only gate; CommandPalette.tsx:120-125; App.tsx:551-563.
findings.suggested_fix: Share one admissibility predicate (including composerBusy and isRunBlocked) across every REQUEST_RUN_EVENT dispatcher.

verdicts.reason:
I confirmed this at the pinned commit 74c0ce0db. Commit 5623ceb6d added `!composerBusy` only to ExecuteButton's `canExecute`, at ExecuteButton.tsx:582-588. `handleRunClick` at :643-645 returns early when `!canExecute`, and it is also the handler for REQUEST_RUN_EVENT (:653-658), so a dispatched event is silently dropped while the composer is busy. Three other dispatchers still gate only on `execution_ready`, `isExecuting` and `progress`, and none checks `composerBusy`:
- the palette's "Execute pipeline" `enabled` predicate (CommandPalette.tsx:117-130);
- Ctrl+E (App.tsx:551-563);
- InlineRunResults' empty-state "Run pipeline" button (InlineRunResults.tsx:251-253 and 389-398).

The state the finding needs can really occur. When a compose turn starts, sessionStore.ts:2178-2186 sets `isComposing: true` without calling `clearValidation()`. Validation is cleared only after the response arrives with a changed version (:2219-2223). So during a follow-up turn on a pipeline that already passed validation, `execution_ready` stays true.

The InlineRunResults comment at :383-388 states the rule this breaks: the button is rendered only when the run is admissible, because otherwise it "would be a silent dead control". No commit after 5623ceb6d in the window changes these gates; 29f9af13b touches App.tsx only for a JSX type import. I found no recorded ruling in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md that makes this deliberate.

The impact is small, so severity stays low. The sticky action bar in the same pane shows "Wait for the composer to finish thinking." (RUN_BLOCK_REASON_TEXT.composing), and the backend's exclusive leases turn any attempt into a 409 rather than a harmful run. The same partial mirroring already existed for `isRunBlocked` (pending interpretations) before this window. The new gate widens that existing gap; it did not create the pattern.
verdicts.evidence:
- ExecuteButton.tsx:513-515: `composerBusy = isComposing || guidedChatPending || guidedResponsePending`.
- ExecuteButton.tsx:582-588: `canExecute` includes `!composerBusy`.
- ExecuteButton.tsx:643-645: `if (!canExecute || !activeSessionId) return;`
- ExecuteButton.tsx:653-658: the REQUEST_RUN_EVENT listener calls `handleRunClick`.
- CommandPalette.tsx:117-130: the execute command's `enabled` is `runAdmissionAvailable && execution_ready && !isExecuting && progress.status !== "running" && activeSessionId`, with no `composerBusy` check.
- App.tsx:551-563: Ctrl+E dispatches whenever `execution_ready`.
- InlineRunResults.tsx:248-253: `executionReady` is the only admission fact mirrored.
- InlineRunResults.tsx:383-398: the comment states that the owner drops inadmissible events, "so the button would otherwise be a silent dead control", yet the button is enabled on `executionReady` alone.
- sessionStore.ts:2178-2186: compose start sets `isComposing: true` and leaves `validationResult` in place.
- sessionStore.ts:2219-2223: `clearValidation()` runs only after the response, and only when the version changed.
- `git log 5623ceb6d..74c0ce0db` on these files shows only 29f9af13b, which has no gate changes.

findings.title: Readiness decoder does not admit the new required note field
findings.summary: The backend ValidationReadinessBlocker.note is required (schemas.py:259-262) and the TS type declares note: string | null. isValidationReadiness (api/validationReadiness.ts:14-21) validates suggestion but not note. DecisionPanel.tsx:230 renders the reviewer-note block when row.note !== null, which is also true for undefined.
findings.failure_scenario: A blocker without the note key (a test app, a future producer, or a surface that drops the key) passes admission. The panel renders the 'Reviewer's note (the advisor's own words — not verified by ELSPETH):' label over an empty paragraph. The live pydantic /validate wire always sends note, so there is no failure today.
findings.evidence: validationReadiness.ts:14-21; decisionPanelRows.ts:164; DecisionPanel.tsx:230-240; schemas.py:259-262.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `(typeof blocker.note === 'string' || blocker.note === null)` to isValidationReadiness.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed as a half-wired change. Commit 6a34007fb ("readiness blockers carry an explicit note field") added `note: str | None` to the backend model. The backend field is required with no default. The commit also added the field to the TS wire type. It did not touch the shared admission guard isValidationReadiness, which still checks every other blocker field but not `note`. The guard is the only frontend admission for readiness. Both the /validate client path and the audit-readiness decoder go through it. A blocker with no `note` key is therefore admitted, typed as `string | null`, and carried into DecisionRow unchanged. DecisionPanel's `row.note !== null` check is true for `undefined`, so the panel renders the reviewer-note label over an empty paragraph. I could not find a live path that triggers this today. Every Python producer builds a ValidationReadinessBlocker pydantic model with `note` required, and the web routes do not use `exclude_none`. The rubric counts a field added on one side but not validated on the other as a finding, so the defect stands at low severity.
verdicts.evidence:
- The worktree HEAD is 74c0ce0db. - src/elspeth/web/frontend/src/api/validationReadiness.ts:15-21: the blockers `.every` checks code, component_id, component_type, detail and suggestion. It does not check `note`. The file has no diff in 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db. - src/elspeth/web/frontend/src/types/index.ts:611: `note: string | null`. This line was added by 6a34007fb, whose --stat touches types/index.ts but not validationReadiness.ts. - src/elspeth/web/execution/schemas.py:259-262: `note: str | None`, with the comment "REQUIRED (no default) so a builder cannot forget the decision". - Admission call sites: api/client.ts:1391 `!isValidationReadiness(result.readiness)` and api/auditReadiness.ts:133 `isValidationReadiness(result.readiness)`. - components/chat/decisionPanelRows.ts builds rows with `note: blocker.note`, which passes through unchanged. - components/chat/DecisionPanel.tsx:230 checks `row.note !== null &&`, then renders the label at line 237 and `

{row.note}

` at line 239. Both render when `note` is undefined. - All backend ValidationReadiness constructions use the pydantic model: composer/service.py:1043, 1130, 10985 and 11454; no_tool_policy.py:1638; and execution/_validation_model.py:45. A grep for exclude_none in the web routes finds only guided_operations.py, where it is False. So there is no live omission today, which keeps the severity low.

findings.title: Edited 'canonical 23 checks' docstring does not match a measured registry count
findings.summary: The window changed the literal from 24 to 23. The measured registry at HEAD has 26 blocking check names and 29 total. 23 matches only if validate_pipeline's own emission excludes state_exists, advisor_signoff, proof_diagnostics and the 3 advisory checks, which I did not measure.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer who uses the docstring to audit check coverage counts against 23 and finds 26 or 29 registered names, then misjudges whether a check was dropped.
findings.evidence: PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src python: len(VALIDATION_BLOCKING_CHECK_NAMES)=26, len(VALIDATION_CHECK_NAMES)=29; elspeth.__file__ resolved inside the worktree.
findings.suggested_fix: Name what is counted (for example 'the 23 validate_pipeline ledger checks') or derive it from the registry.

verdicts.reason: "Canonical 23 checks" is a defined term in this codebase, and 23 is its measured count, fixed by an import-time guard. It is CORE_VALIDATION_CHECK_NAMES: the checks in VALIDATION_BLOCKING_CHECK_NAMES from the start up to and including schema_compatibility, which is the 23rd entry. The reviewer's 26 also counts state_exists, advisor_signoff and proof_diagnostics, which come after that cut-off. Its 29 adds the 3 advisory checks as well. Neither number is what the docstring counts. Commit 364801194 deleted managed_identity_policy, changed _CORE_CHECK_COUNT from 24 to 23 and updated the docstring in the same change, so the docstring is accurate and not stale. A maintainer cannot count 23 against a different set without the module failing at import: if the canonical prefix were not 23 long, the module would raise AssertionError on load.
verdicts.evidence: Pinned HEAD 74c0ce0db336e8ed67c6f532d070e7553fcd5059. src/elspeth/web/execution/_validation_ledger.py:23 `_CORE_CHECK_COUNT: Final = 23`; :25 `CORE_VALIDATION_CHECK_NAMES = VALIDATION_BLOCKING_CHECK_NAMES[: _SCHEMA_CHECK_INDEX + 1]`; :29-30 `if len(CORE_VALIDATION_CHECK_NAMES) != _CORE_CHECK_COUNT: raise AssertionError("core validation checks must be the 23-name canonical prefix through schema_compatibility")`; :60 and :122 runtime messages also say "all 23 core checks". src/elspeth/web/execution/schemas.py:102-129: RUNTIME_CHECK_SCHEMA_COMPATIBILITY is entry 23 (line 125); CHECK_STATE_EXISTS, CHECK_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF and CHECK_PROOF_DIAGNOSTICS follow it (26 total). :130-135 adds 3 advisories (29). Commit 364801194 message: "the managed_identity_policy validation check: the canonical core check count moves 24 -> 23 (import-time guard, ledger messages and test pins re-pinned...)". The same commit changes service.py:1457 docstring 24->23 together with the ledger constant.

findings.title: nginx X-Forwarded-For is dropped under Compose, so every client gets the bridge IP
findings.summary: nginx sets X-Forwarded-For and proxies to the Docker-published 127.0.0.1:8451. uvicorn (launched by cli.py:4791 without forwarded_allow_ips) trusts the header only from 127.0.0.1, but inside the container the peer is the Docker bridge gateway. The header is ignored and request.client.host is the same IP for every user.
findings.failure_scenario: Compose plus the shipped nginx.conf: one user mistypes a password 20 times in a minute, or a few tabs hold expired tokens (get_current_user's failure path calls check_auth_rate_limit). The shared per-IP auth bucket (auth_rate_limit_per_minute=20) fills and /api/auth/login returns 429 for all users. An attacker can sustain this lockout with 20 req/min. Auth-failure audit rows and the ip_address fields in messages.py:1239 and inspect.py:60 all record the bridge IP.
findings.evidence: nginx.conf:26,30. cli.py:4791 uvicorn.run passes no proxy settings. uvicorn/config.py:342 defaults forwarded_allow_ips to FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS or '127.0.0.1'. No FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS anywhere in deploy/ or the docs. rate_limit.py:202 keys on request.client.host. auth/middleware.py:61. auth/audit.py:594-598. The SSO spec (2026-09-02-pluggable-sso-design.md:956-958) records the same limitation as deferred work only for ECS.
findings.suggested_fix: Set FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS to the bridge gateway/subnet in web-postgres.yaml (or expose a forwarded-allow-ips setting via `elspeth web`), or document that Compose client IPs collapse.

verdicts.reason:
I traced the path at 74c0ce0db and it holds. Nothing earlier in the path guards against it or normalises the address. The window added deploy/compose/nginx.conf (a new file, commit 6e377bdc4/fa26f34b8). It sets X-Forwarded-For and proxies to the Docker-published port. Nothing in the launch path makes uvicorn trust that header from a Docker peer.

- `elspeth web` (cli.py:4792-4799) calls uvicorn.run with no proxy_headers or forwarded_allow_ips arguments.
- In the pinned uvicorn 0.46.0 (uv.lock:4534-4535), config.py:341-342 defaults the trusted list to FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS or "127.0.0.1".
- ProxyHeadersMiddleware only rewrites scope["client"] when the connecting peer is in the trusted list.
- FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS is not set anywhere: not in the Dockerfile ENV lines (176-179), not in web-postgres.yaml, not in deploy/ or docs.
- Host nginx connects to 127.0.0.1:8451, the published port (web-postgres.yaml:66-67). Docker then delivers the connection to the container from the network gateway address. That is true for docker-proxy and for DNAT with hairpin MASQUERADE. So the peer uvicorn sees is never 127.0.0.1, the header is ignored, and request.client.host is the gateway IP for every user.

The consequence is also confirmed:
- check_auth_rate_limit (rate_limit.py:191-203) keys on request.client.host. It runs on the auth routes (auth/routes.py:306 and 359) and in the get_current_user failure path (auth/middleware.py:61).
- The limit defaults to 20 per minute (config.py:452).
- So every client behind the shipped nginx shares one auth bucket. One user or attacker making about 20 failed auth requests a minute gets 429s for everyone.
- Auth audit client_host (auth/audit.py:593-597) and the ip_address fields at messages.py:1239 and inspect.py:60 all record the gateway IP.

Neither ruling nor docs cover this:
- recent-code-hints.md has no ruling on proxy headers or client IP.
- docker.md:331-363 documents the nginx template but says nothing about client IPs collapsing.
- The SSO spec (lines 956-958) records the limitation as deferred work for ECS only.

The rate_limit.py:197-199 docstring assumes "--proxy-headers enabled". That is exactly the setting the Compose launch leaves effectively off for non-loopback peers.

Nginx sets X-Forwarded-For to $remote_addr, overwriting the header rather than appending to it. So the fix would not open a spoofing hole. Medium severity fits: an unauthenticated attacker can deny logins to all users at a low request rate, and the audit trail loses client attribution.
verdicts.evidence: deploy/compose/nginx.conf:26 `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8451;`, nginx.conf:30 `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;`. deploy/compose/web-postgres.yaml:64 runs `web --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8451` and :66-67 publishes "8451:8451". The environment block (lines 3-30) has no FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS. src/elspeth/cli.py:4792-4799 is `uvicorn.run("elspeth.web.app:create_app", host=host, port=port, reload=reload, factory=True, access_log=False)` with no proxy args. In uvicorn 0.46.0, config.py:207 has `proxy_headers: bool = True` and config.py:341-342 has `os.environ.get("FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS", "127.0.0.1")`. In middleware/proxy_headers.py, `if client_host in self.trusted_hosts:` gates the XFF rewrite. Dockerfile:176-179 sets ENV for PATH, HOME, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE and PYTHONUNBUFFERED only. A grep for FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS/forwarded_allow_ips across src, deploy, docs and the Dockerfile finds only docs/specs/2026-09-02-pluggable-sso-design.md:957, which covers ECS only. src/elspeth/web/middleware/rate_limit.py:202 is `client_ip = request.client.host if request.client else "unknown"`. web/config.py:452 is `auth_rate_limit_per_minute: int = Field(default=20, ge=1)`. web/auth/middleware.py:61 and auth/routes.py:306 and 359 apply check_auth_rate_limit. auth/audit.py:593-597 derives client_host from request.client.host. docs/guides/docker.md:331-363 documents nginx without mentioning client-IP collapse.

findings.title: systemd env example says the shipped nginx uses 240s; it uses 360s
findings.summary: fa26f34b8 raised the only shipped nginx example to 360s but did not update the systemd example's comment, which still states 240s.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator puts the shipped nginx.conf (360s) in front of a systemd host, reads that the template uses 240s, and gets a false fact about the ingress. The direction is safe (declared 240 < real 360), but the two artefacts disagree and test_linux_systemd_bundle.py:116-117 pins 180/240, so nothing catches the drift.
findings.evidence: elspeth-web.env.example:21-22 vs nginx.conf:33-34. git show fa26f34b8 touches nginx.conf, web-postgres.yaml and docker.md but not the systemd file.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the comment to name the actual ingress (or 360s for the shipped template) and state whether the systemd profile deliberately keeps 180/240.

verdicts.reason: I confirmed the finding at 74c0ce0db. Commit 6e377bdc4, inside the window, added the comment at deploy/linux-systemd/elspeth-web.env.example:21: "Match the actual minimum ingress timeout; the shipped nginx example uses 240s." Commit fa26f34b8, later in the same window, raised the only nginx config in the tree (deploy/compose/nginx.conf:33-34) to 360s and did not touch the systemd file. The comment is therefore now false. No guard or other file makes it true: there is no second nginx example, and docker.md:334 points at deploy/compose/nginx.conf. As the finding says, the direction is safe: the declared ceiling of 240 is below the real 360, so a lower ceiling only makes the app give up sooner, never later than the proxy. The defect is documentation drift, so low severity is right. A related drift the finding did not name: line 17 says "Production composer limits shared by the supported deployment profiles", but the compose/docker profile now uses 300/360 while systemd keeps 180/240, so that comment is stale too.
verdicts.evidence: deploy/linux-systemd/elspeth-web.env.example:21-22 (blame: 6e377bdc4, 2026-09-22 02:02, inside the window) says the "shipped nginx example uses 240s" and sets the ceiling to 240. deploy/compose/nginx.conf:33-34 sets proxy_read_timeout and proxy_send_timeout to 360s, changed from 240s by fa26f34b8 (2026-09-22 04:10). `git show --stat fa26f34b8` lists only nginx.conf, web-postgres.yaml, docker.md and test_compose_bundle.py. `find deploy -name 'nginx*'` returns only deploy/compose/nginx.conf. tests/unit/deployment/test_linux_systemd_bundle.py:117 pins the systemd ceiling at "240" and does not check it against nginx.conf. deploy/compose/web-postgres.yaml:17 now says "any additional ingress hop must allow at least 360s", and docker.md says the same, so they contradict the systemd comment.

findings.title: Reference says the Docker timeout is 180.0; it is now 300.0, which also needs a ceiling not listed
findings.summary: The reference table still says the standalone Docker example uses 180.0, while docker.md:79-80 uses 300.0 plus COMPOSER_TRANSPORT_IDLE_CEILING_SECONDS=360.0. The table has no row for the ceiling or headroom. The new EXECUTION_RATE_LIMIT (24dccdd9e) is documented nowhere.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator configuring from the reference sets COMPOSER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=300 to match docker.md without the ceiling. The default ceiling 300 minus headroom 30 is 270, so _validate_composer_timeout_transport_headroom fails and the service crash-loops. An operator hitting the 60-rows/minute web-run limit has no documented knob.
findings.evidence: environment-variables.md:161. docker.md:79-80. config.py:73-74 defaults and 1178-1198 validator. No ELSPETH_WEB__EXECUTION_RATE_LIMIT or execution_rate_limit in docs/ or deploy/.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the example value, add rows for the transport ceiling, headroom and EXECUTION_RATE_LIMIT (JSON RateLimitSettings object), and pin them in test_deployment_platform_docs.py.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute this finding, and I confirmed it at 74c0ce0db. Commit fa26f34b8 ("allow five minutes for Composer requests", inside the window) changed the Docker example in docs/guides/docker.md to 300.0 and added the 360.0 ceiling. It did not touch docs/reference/environment-variables.md, which still says the example uses 180.0. The reference table also has no row for the transport ceiling or the headroom. The failure path is real: an operator who sets a 300 s timeout and leaves the ceiling at its default gets a startup ValueError. That error message names the fix, so the operator is not stuck, and the severity stays low. The claim about execution_rate_limit also holds: a grep of docs/, deploy/, CHANGELOG.md and README.md returned no matches (exit 1). The same grep over config.py did match, so the search itself works. One caveat: the reference table leaves out many optional settings (for example write_rate_limit_per_minute and composer_planner_*). The missing EXECUTION_RATE_LIMIT row is therefore a documentation gap, not a strict half-wiring defect. The 180.0 value, however, is a clear stale-doc defect.
verdicts.evidence:
- docs/reference/environment-variables.md:161 still says "The standalone Docker example uses `180.0`".
- docs/guides/docker.md sets `ELSPETH_WEB__COMPOSER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=300.0` and `ELSPETH_WEB__COMPOSER_TRANSPORT_IDLE_CEILING_SECONDS=360.0`, and its prose says the timeout is five minutes with a six-minute ceiling.
- `git show fa26f34b8 --stat` lists only deploy/compose/nginx.conf, deploy/compose/web-postgres.yaml, docs/guides/docker.md and tests/unit/deployment/test_compose_bundle.py. The environment-variables reference was not updated.
- src/elspeth/web/config.py:73-74 sets the defaults: ceiling 300.0, headroom 30.0.
- In config.py:1189-1198, `_validate_composer_timeout_transport_headroom` raises ValueError when the timeout exceeds the ceiling minus the headroom. So a 300 s timeout against the default 270 s maximum fails at startup with an explicit message.
- config.py:511 declares `execution_rate_limit: RateLimitSettings`, and config.py:1446 lists it among the JSON-decoded env keys.
- `grep -rln 'execution_rate_limit|EXECUTION_RATE_LIMIT'` over docs/, deploy/, CHANGELOG.md and README.md returned nothing (rc=1).
- Among the docs, TRANSPORT_IDLE_CEILING appears only in docker.md, the ACA runbooks and the plans, never in the environment-variables reference.

findings.title: Probe rejects a valid server-built terminal event that has no event_sequence
findings.summary: _event_sequence requires an int event_sequence on every frame. The server's _build_terminal_run_event sends a terminal RunEvent without event_sequence (excluded when None) whenever the run is terminal but no terminal run_events row exists, e.g. after an orphan cancel, which writes no run_events.
findings.failure_scenario: A canary run is orphan-cancelled (web restarted during the ingress rollout). The probe's replay leg, or its first leg, receives the synthesized cancelled frame and raises invalid_event_sequence. The output {"status":"failed","error_class":"ValueError"} looks exactly like an ingress or replay defect even though nginx works.
findings.evidence: probe:34-35. routes.py:717-797 (_build_terminal_run_event, no with_event_sequence), 1733-1736, 2136-2140. schemas.py:655 exclude_if None. run_recovery_authority.py has no run_events writes. app.py:389/395 call the orphan cancellers.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept a terminal frame without event_sequence as the final event (or report it as a distinct 'synthesized_terminal' outcome), and document that the canary must have a persisted terminal event.

verdicts.reason: The failure path the finding describes (an orphan cancel after a web restart that writes no run_events row) cannot happen in the production server. The orphan-cancel branches it cites at app.py:389/395 run only when `recovery_coordinator is None`. The only caller of `_periodic_orphan_cleanup` (app.py:782-790) always passes a real `RunRecoveryCoordinator`, and that coordinator is also run once at startup (app.py:769-777). Every terminal projection the coordinator makes goes through `project_terminal`, which ends with `append_terminal_run_event_once` (recovery.py:121). That writes a sequenced terminal run_events row, so the websocket replay loop (routes.py:1716-1728) sends a frame with `event_sequence`, sets `replayed_terminal` and closes 1000 before it ever reaches the unsequenced `_build_terminal_run_event` fallback. A restart also does not orphan-cancel a running canary: a RUNNING Landscape run with no live leader goes to `recover_run` (a resume), not to a cancel. The other terminal writers also persist a sequenced terminal event: the executor's `_persist_and_broadcast_run_event` (service.py:4574-4596), a user cancel before the start permit (run_cancellation_authority.py:78-100) and an admission refusal (repository.py:1665). The one leftover gap I found is a setup/submission failure (`_handle_pipeline_submission_failure`, service.py:2627-2650), which marks the run failed without an event. The finding does not cite it, and there the canary never ran, so a failed probe is the right result; only the ValueError label is unhelpful. The scenario as stated is refuted.
verdicts.evidence: app.py:782-790 is the only caller of _periodic_orphan_cleanup and passes recovery_coordinator=recovery_coordinator, built at app.py:769-777; app.py:386-387 takes the coordinator branch, so the cancel_all_orphaned_runs / cancel_all_orphaned_run_records calls at 389/395 never run in production (grep shows no other caller). recovery.py:68-125 project_terminal always ends with transaction.runs.append_terminal_run_event_once (recovery.py:121), which is backed by repository.py:1846-1875 and gives the event a sequence (append_run_event, repository.py:1877+). routes.py:1716-1728 replays persisted events with with_event_sequence (routes.py:801-808) and returns before the unsequenced fallback at routes.py:1732-1736. recovery.py:285 sends a still-running run to recover_run (a resume), not a cancel. Residual unrelated gap: execution/service.py:2627-2650 (a setup failure marks the run failed with no terminal event), which the finding did not cite.

findings.title: Firewall advice for port 8451 is usually ineffective for a Docker-published port
findings.summary: The guide and nginx.conf:3 tell operators to restrict direct access to port 8451 with the host firewall, but Docker's own DNAT rules for published ports usually bypass ufw/firewalld INPUT rules. The shipped compose file still publishes '8451:8451' on 0.0.0.0 rather than 127.0.0.1.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator follows the first option (ufw deny 8451). The plaintext HTTP backend stays reachable from the network, bypassing TLS and nginx log redaction, so login passwords and bearer tokens can cross the network in cleartext.
findings.evidence: docker.md:337-339 (new in window). nginx.conf:3. web-postgres.yaml:4 (HOST 0.0.0.0), :67 ('8451:8451'). The Docker/ufw bypass is documented Docker networking behaviour and was not measured in this read-only session.
findings.suggested_fix: Ship the compose file with '127.0.0.1:8451:8451' now that the bundle includes a proxy pointing at loopback, or drop the host-firewall option from the guide.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute the core claim. The guide text added in this window (docs/guides/docker.md:337-339, from commits fa26f34b8 and 6e377bdc4) gives operators two ways to protect the plaintext backend: "Restrict direct access to port 8451 with the host firewall or change the Compose port binding to `127.0.0.1:8451:8451`." The shipped overlay still publishes the port on every interface: deploy/compose/web-postgres.yaml:67 has `- "8451:8451"`, and that line did not change in the window. Docker's own packet-filtering documentation says published-port traffic is DNAT'd in nat PREROUTING and passes through the FORWARD/DOCKER chains, so it never reaches the INPUT chain where a plain `ufw deny 8451` rule sits. firewalld zone rules are bypassed the same way. The only filter point that works is the DOCKER-USER chain, and the guide never mentions it. I searched docs/ and deploy/ for ufw, firewalld, DOCKER-USER and iptables and found none of them, so no caveat exists anywhere. No ruling in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md covers this.

The finding does overstate its case in three places:
(1) nginx.conf:3 says only "restrict direct access to backend port 8451". It does not recommend a firewall.
(2) The guide's second option, binding to 127.0.0.1, is correct and sits in the same sentence, so the defect is incomplete prose, not a missing safeguard.
(3) `ELSPETH_WEB__HOST: 0.0.0.0` (web-postgres.yaml:4) and `--host 0.0.0.0` (:64) set the bind address inside the container. They are needed for any published port to work (docker.md:87-88 says so), so they are not part of the defect.

The failure path is real only for an operator who picks the firewall option and uses ufw INPUT rules. It is a documentation-only defect, and low severity is right.
verdicts.evidence: docs/guides/docker.md:337-339 (new in window, git diff 7c986dc97..74c0ce0db): "Restrict direct access to port 8451 with the host firewall or change the Compose port binding to `127.0.0.1:8451:8451`". deploy/compose/web-postgres.yaml:67 `- "8451:8451"`: the host IP is unspecified, so the port is published on 0.0.0.0, and this line is unchanged in the window. deploy/compose/nginx.conf:3 (new file) says only "restrict direct access to backend port 8451", and nginx.conf proxies to http://127.0.0.1:8451, so a loopback-only binding would work with the shipped proxy. grep -rni 'ufw|firewalld|DOCKER-USER|iptables' over docs/ and deploy/ finds nothing relevant, so the guide carries no Docker-firewall caveat. docker.md:87-88 explains that the in-container 0.0.0.0 bind is needed, which weakens the finding's use of web-postgres.yaml:4 as evidence. The claim that Docker bypasses ufw rests on Docker's documented packet-filtering behaviour (published ports are DNAT'd before ufw's INPUT rules see them). I did not measure it: this session is read-only.
